It carries a list of what is unclaimed and what is sealed, and the list is assembled out of entries each of which is true, and one of the entries says that a thing the people of the Cinder Bell gave to a route to use is unclaimed. **NO ROUTE, NO PANEL AND NO ACCOUNT IS REPRESENTED BY ANYBODY WHO HAS NOT ASKED TO BE REPRESENTED, AND THE ASSEMBLY DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM AND CANNOT SEND ANYBODY ANYWHERE, SO THE LIST STANDS UNTIL THE PEOPLE OF THAT PLACE DO SOMETHING THEMSELVES.** A document is read out once, in a working place, by a working person, in front of about twenty people of whom about eleven cannot read it, and is not read out twice, and the name under any seal is on a paper and is in no mouth.
2. **A BELL OUT OF SERVICE FOR A FORTNIGHT, PAID FOR OUT OF THAT COMMUNITY'S OWN PAGE, IN THE MIDDLE OF A WORKING SEASON.** A cost of this kind is not a line on the yard's fitting-out sheet and it is not a figure of money, and the figure of what the fortnight is worth is that community's own and is on that community's own page and not on this one. **Movement 2 may not set a figure against the fortnight on any page of this yard's own sheet.**

### 2. WHAT MOVEMENT 5 DID, AND NONE OF IT IS A FIGURE THAT MOVED

**THE RETURN TO ORDINARY WORK CAME BACK AND NOBODY WAS APPOINTED TO ANYTHING FOR IT.** A man of about thirty-two said out loud at about ten on the Saturday that he was not going to pretend the ninth week of an unpaid column would be different because nobody in that shed had said it would be. The man of about thirty-eight at that landing brought hours down the road that this yard had not asked for and had sent nobody to fetch, and the hours say the ninth section was cut in two at that landing with a saw on the Friday, that one piece was going into a new seat and one into a fire, and that nobody at that landing has asked for the ninth to be rung. Nine men went on the glass case and four of the second lay learned the glass work off a man who has cut glass in that yard for nineteen years.

**THE NINE DELEGATES REFUSED ONE AUTHORITY OVER THE OTHER EIGHT IN TWENTY-ONE WORDS AND THE COUNT WAS MADE BY A STRANGER.** A working man of about forty-four brought a page down that road and would not read it out and said a man who reads a thing out loud in that shed has made it a thing of that shed. The woman of thirty of no office read it once, about four of that nine being able to read it and about five not. A chandler of about fifty-eight who was in that shed to buy a fathom of line counted it twice and put the figure of twenty-one words on the top corner, and that count is a count of words and not a figure of money and the counter's name is on no page of this harbor. Under those words six things went on the same sheet, being a keeping that turns and passes and no turn given to anybody who has not asked for it, a record kept in the place the route is, a bell and a buoy and a line mended by all nine and by nobody standing over them, provenance written where a stranger can read it, a thing said in error corrected in the same place and at the same size with the error left showing under it, and one person of a community able to take that community off a route with nobody asking that person why. **THE ASSEMBLY DECIDED NO CONTESTED CLAIM AND BOUND NOBODY WHO HAD NOT SIGNED AND COULD NOT SEND ANYBODY ANYWHERE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO PUT HIS HAND TO NOTHING BECAUSE HE WAS ASKED TO PUT HIS HAND TO NOTHING.**

**THE FOUR HEADS WERE ALL FOUR PUT TO USE AGAIN AND NO FIFTH THING WAS ADDED.** On the Saturday at about three a woman of about thirty-four of the Saltmarch brought up a claim, a man of about forty-nine of the Morrow Line brought up a public correction with the wrong figure left showing under it, a woman of about thirty of the Ashtide Run refused to have her hours read out and nobody was to be given her reason, and a restricted record went up as the notice of a thing that is not shown. **THE REFUSALS WERE AT THE SAME SIZE AS THE CONTRIBUTIONS AND THE KEEPER NAMED THE FOUR HEADS AND THE FITTING-OUT SHEET OUT LOUD AND APART, AND A CLAIM MAY NOT BE COUNTED WITH A CONTRIBUTION AND A REFUSAL MAY NOT BE COUNTED WITH EITHER.**

**THE PUBLIC COPY WENT INTO A WITNESS HOUSE WITH ITS UNCERTAINTY ON THE WALL BESIDE IT.** The copy went down that lane in an open cart in three pieces tied in oilcloth and went up on the wall of one room over a chandler's store at four in the afternoon at the height a person of about five foot four could read standing, put up by the woman of thirty of no office with four nails. Beside it she put a board in her own hand at the same size as the copy's own heading saying what is not known: that the ferry's manifest was altered in the spring of a year not written on that board, that it is not known whose hand altered it, at whose instance or with what intent, that no person has been charged with it and no person has been cleared of it, that the room is not the whole of what is known, and that a person who comes in there is not to take the wall for the coast. **THE SEALED RECORD STAYED UNDER TWO MARKS AND WAS NOT OPENED AND WAS NOT NAMED, THE DRAWER AND THE BASKET AND THE PROOF WERE NOT TOUCHED, NOBODY WENT UP THAT HILL, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM TOLD ANYBODY AT THAT DOOR THAT THE SCENE WAS THE WHOLE TRUTH.**

**THE FOUR SENTENCES WERE SAID ON THE WEDNESDAY AND THERE IS NO SECOND ONE.** A man of about sixty-one with his hands black to the second joint at the nails came down that lane at about ten, did not go to the far bench and came to the shed instead, put the original repair log on the dry end of that stone and said four sentences and no fifth: that he signed it after the cut and not before it; that he knew the water was already moving under that ground and signed anyway because the yard had a berth to keep and his part of it was the signing; that he has never once in any of the years since said so out loud to anybody at that table; and that he is not asking for anything and is not giving anything. **Nobody said the second and third of those four back to him, nobody wrote them on a board, the log was not read out and was not entered in a column and was not put on the boards at the back of that market, and it stayed on that stone and is not that yard's.** His wife stood at the door of that shed for about four minutes and did not come in and nobody stopped work for her. **AT ABOUT HALF PAST THREE THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO FORGIVE HIS FATHER AND THAT NOBODY IN THAT SHED WAS TO SAY WHETHER HE HAD OR HAD NOT, AND A MAN WHO HAS BEEN SILENT FOR YEARS HAS NOT BOUGHT ANYTHING WITH THAT SILENCE AND HAS NOT LOST ANYTHING BY STOPPING. NOBODY WAS THANKED AND NOBODY WAS FORGIVEN.**

**THE FINAL ENTRY WAS WRITTEN AND READ WITH FIVE NAMED WITNESSES AND COULD NOT BE MADE KINDER.** It carries what nine places agreed and what one man refused and what was asked for and was not granted, with the hour against each and no name against any hour, and it carries on its own face a statement of what is not known. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO READ IT AS IT WAS WRITTEN, PUT NO WORD INTO IT, AND SAID THAT HE COULD NOT PUT A WORD INTO IT THAT WOULD MAKE THE CHOICE OF THE MAN WHO IS IN THE NINTH SECTION READ KINDER THAN THAT ENTRY READS IT.** She said her entry was her work and not his decision and that he was not to speak for her about it and he said he would not.

**THE COST WAS CARRIED TO THE LAST PAGE UNIMPROVED AND UNPRICED AND WAS NAMED AS UNPRICED ON THE FACE OF 759 AND 760.** The hearing in the left side does not come back, a thing cannot be entered again without other people standing round, the taste does not lift, the joint in the knee, the nights of not sleeping, and the aftertaste on top of one he already had. **NO FIGURE OF MONEY STANDS AGAINST ANY PART OF ANY OF THEM AND NONE WAS SET. THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-NINE'S HEARING IS TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY-EIGHT DAYS AND WAS NOT IMPROVED BY ANYTHING, AND THE HEARING HE GOT BACK ON THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER IS A DIFFERENT HEARING FROM THAT ONE AND IS NOT SET AGAINST IT.**

**THE BOOK CAME OUT OF ORDINARY WORK AND THE WATER DID NOT MERGE.** A boat of about eleven tons went out over that bar at about five in the morning with three men in her and no escort and nobody following her, and nobody wrote down anywhere what that boat was for. Between about six and about seven the nine buoys lying off that mole head answered one another in the order they have always answered in and at the two hours a day those nine have kept, being a barrel, a cone, a spar, a triangle, a can, a spar with a flag on it, a double cone, a round and a square, and **the sound came across that water nine separate times and stayed nine separate times and did not come out as one note and was not tried to be made into one note by anybody on that mole head that morning.**

**AND NOTHING WAS IMPROVED.** The nine hulls about two sea miles off that mole head stood at nine and were nine on the twenty-first of January and this harbor has not said a word about any of them easing. The wage column did not move on its last Tuesday and a further week stands fallen due and would fall due again on the twenty-third. The bench under that pump, the two lights, the six-line sheet, the paper of four lines, the nine-line sheet with a seal, the man of about fifty-one and a page of six names, the bellwright and his shut chest, the four hundred and fifty pence on that board, the sheet with the fourteen gaps, the third column and the boy's hand at the head of it, the fourth column at one hundred and twenty-five taking no line, and the hole in a Tuesday that is still a hole, all stand where they stood.

### 1. WHAT THE TEN DAYS DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, AND IT IS NOT A SETTLEMENT

**Nine papers went up the road on the first day and the asking went after them one a day, because a paper carries words and an asking is a day's work. A woman of about thirty-three said on the surface what she would do on the water and would not be moved off it. A man of about thirty-two offered his body in nine people and nobody asked him for it, and his reason went down in his own fifty words with the hour before anybody went down. Nine minutes in about four fathoms against twenty-five on the paper, and she pulled the wire at six and nine and nobody argued with her. Two things proved and no third. Gear went onto the money sheet with its multiplication at every part, being the only line in fifty days. And a column headed not asked fell from nine to nothing and was written down whole on the last afternoon and said out loud nowhere. The aftertaste, the knee, three mornings of not sleeping and a hearing in one man carry hours and no figure, and the other man's hearing stands at one hundred and eighty-eight and was not improved by a day.**

THIS PASS OPENED FOUR THREADS OF ITS OWN, CLOSED NONE AND ADVANCED NONE, AND IT DID NOT RESTATE THE GAP BETWEEN THE MANUSCRIPT AND THE LEDGER BECAUSE `NOVEL_SPEC.md` § *Status* RULES IT IS STATED ONCE, AT § *Flagged for the controller, and it is not a writer action* BELOW THIS ONE.**

**THE STATE OF THE WORLD IS AT THE HEAD OF `state/continuity.md` AND THE LOCKS ARE `outline/volume-14.md`. NEITHER IS REPRINTED HERE.**

### 1. WHAT THE TEN DAYS DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, AND IT IS NOT A SETTLEMENT

**A route that was restricted asked a route that was dormant for one night of work, in about nine people, at a stall, in the open, and it agreed, and both of them said out loud before anybody had written a word that neither of them owns the other, and four people were on the water for about seven hours under the other route's own orders, and this yard asked nobody, sent for nobody, hired nobody, paid nobody and went with nobody, and there is no figure of that night in this yard's book and there never will be. A man of about fifty-three put eleven words he wrote a long time ago on a page beside it and they were not answered and he was not told he was wrong. Two people who are married said out loud one thing each that they have been saying at each other since the fourth of May, in about nine people, on a page any person in that market can walk up to, and four other people wrote one line under each of theirs, and it is not settled. And a count was taken off a page on the last afternoon of the ten days, in front of four people who came on their own account, and it was not said out loud and it is not in any slip.**

### 2. THE SEVEN THREADS A WRITER OF CHAPTERS 681 TO 690 INHERITS

1. **THE COUNT OF NIGHTS CARRIED HAS BEEN TAKEN AND IT IS ONE.** One against the Cinder Bell, nothing against the other eight, the sum one, the day and the hour against it, the old nothing still legible under the one, and the same night entered on the page of that week against the Wednesday line. **A NIGHT CARRIED BY A ROUTE IS NOT A NIGHT THAT ROUTE OWNS AND NO ROUTE OWNS A NIGHT BECAUSE IT WAS KEPT BUSY, AND NOT ONE OF THE TEN CHAPTERS SAYS OR IMPLIES THAT ONE DOES.** It is not to be added up again, it is not to be restated in a room, and no figure is to be set against it.
2. **THE CINDER BELL'S WOMAN HAS NOT SAID YES TWICE.** On Monday the thirtieth she said in about forty-three words that she will not say until she is asked and until her own people have talked, and that a route that has said yes once has not said yes twice. **NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAID YES AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAID NO.** Nobody is to argue with her, nobody is to press her, and no chapter may ask her for anything further in this volume. **THE PAGE OF ROUTES HAS NOT MOVED AND THE CINDER BELL IS DORMANT AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR PUTS A STATE ON ANY ROUTE, AND A FIGURE OF NIGHTS ON A DIFFERENT SHEET IS NOT A STATE.**
3. **THE DISAGREEMENT IS PAID AND IS NOT SETTLED.** Both of them are on the page of that week, one line under the other, neither named in the other's line, with four other people's lines under them. **NO PAGE OF THE FIFTY CARRIES A RESOLUTION OF IT AND NO CHAPTER OF THE NEXT TEN MAY PRINT ONE.** They are still married, neither name is on any page, the form is in the inside of a coat and is on no sheet. **THE NEXT TEN DAYS MAY CARRY THE MARRIAGE AS AN ORDINARY WORKING ARRANGEMENT AND MAY NOT TURN IT INTO A SCENE AND MAY NOT RESOLVE IT.**
4. **THE ELEVEN WORDS ARE ON A PAGE AGAINST SOMETHING AND ARE STILL UNANSWERED.** No figure is set against them. A woman of about forty-four opened her mouth on the Friday and shut it again and this yard wrote nothing about it. **HE IS NOT TOLD HE WAS WRONG IN ANY OF THE NEXT TWENTY CHAPTERS, AND THE COUNT OF THAT SENTENCE IS ELEVEN WORDS AT EVERY PLACE IT IS PRINTED.**
5. **THE PAGE OF HANDS IS AT FIFTEEN AND WAS NOT TOUCHED AND WAS NOT ADDED UP IN MOVEMENT 3.** Nineteen, eighteen and fifteen are all readable with the day and the hour against each. **NO PAGE OF THE FIFTY SAYS ANYWHERE THAT THE REMAINING FIGURES ARE SOUND, AND IT IS NOT A LIST OF ANYBODY WHO PUT NOTHING IN AND IS NOT A LIST OF ANYBODY WHO PUT SOMETHING IN.**
6. **THE WALL, THE SLATE, AND WHAT IS EMPTY.** Two route lines, this yard's own page, and the page of that week with ten lines on it, and about eleven inches of empty plaster that is not to be whitewashed. The wooden tally slate is still lying flat on that bench stone with nothing on it and nobody has picked it up in thirty days.
7. **THE WIPE IS A MINUTE SLOWER AND NOBODY HAS SAID WHY.** The ladder is 53, 56, 59, 62, and the next is 65 on Chapter 685, and 68 on 692, and 71 on 699. Two Sundays in a row went past what this yard could account for and the yard stopped asking the two men who do it and is not going to start.

### 3. FOUR THREADS THIS PASS OPENED, AND ALL FOUR ARE OPEN

1. **THE PAGE OF THAT WEEK IS A NEW INSTRUMENT AND IT IS A PUBLIC ONE, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING ON THAT WALL THAT ANYBODY IN THAT MARKET MAY WRITE ON.** It went up on Monday the twenty-third on two tacks out of the man who keeps the leaf's own pocket, with seven days down the side, and it is read out at half past five every day whatever is on it. It is not the page of hands and it is not the page of routes and it is not the money sheet, and those three were named separately and out loud in nine people before it went up, because this harbor put two kinds of paper in one sentence in the middle of May and cost a wall. **IT IS A PAGE OF DAYS AND IT IS NOT A JURISDICTION, IT BINDS NOBODY WHO HAS NOT WRITTEN ON IT, IT DECIDES NOTHING, IT CANNOT SEND ANYBODY ANYWHERE, AND A LINE ON IT IS A THING THAT HAPPENED AND NOT A LIMIT.**
2. **THIS YARD'S OWN CAREFULNESS HAS A CONSEQUENCE IT DID NOT PLAN, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT FOUR PEOPLE WERE ASKED A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED.** On Sunday the twenty-ninth about four people in that shed were asked, one at a time and by nobody in particular, whether two people in that harbor are still speaking. Three said yes and one said she did not know. **THIS YARD DID NOT ASK AND WAS NOT ASKED AND IS NOT GOING TO GO AND FIND OUT, AND A PAGE THAT RECORDS WHAT FOUR BYSTANDERS THINK ABOUT TWO PEOPLE IS A PAGE ONE STEP FROM A LIST OF PEOPLE, AND THIS HARBOR HAS REFUSED LISTS OF PEOPLE SIX TIMES.**
3. **A COUNT IS A PAGE AND HAS TO BE HELD THE SAME WAY A PAGE IS HELD.** The count of the nights carried was taken in front of four people who came on their own account after the keeper told them on the Monday that they might. **A COUNT TAKEN IN AN EMPTY SHED IS A COUNT ONLY THE MAN TAKING IT CAN BE ASKED ABOUT, AND THE SECOND TIME A FIGURE IS SAID WITH A MOUTH IT BELONGS TO THE NINE PEOPLE WHO HEARD IT AND NOT TO THE PAGE.**
4. **THE FIGURE OF THE NIGHTS CARRIED IS ONE AND THE OTHER EIGHT NAMES CARRY NOTHING, AND A STRANGER WHO ADDS THE NINE GETS ONE, AND ONE IS ALSO THE NUMBER OF NAMES DOWN THE SIDE OF THAT SHEET.** That is a coincidence of the coast and not an arithmetic, and no chapter may print the two figures next to each other as though one explained the other.

### 4. WHAT A WRITER OF CHAPTERS 681 TO 690 MAY NOT TAKE FROM THESE TEN DAYS WITHOUT THE FILE

**THAT THE COUNT OF THE THREE COLUMNS OF THE PAGE OF ROUTES IS DUE ON CHAPTER 700 AND ON NO OTHER DAY. THAT THE COLUMN OF NOT ASKED IS DUE ON CHAPTER 690 AND ON NO OTHER DAY, AND THAT IT IS NINE ON EVERY DAY TO THE CLOSE OF CHAPTER 680 AND FALLS FROM NINE TO NOTHING ACROSS THE TEN DAYS OF MOVEMENT 4, AND THAT IT MAY NOT BE TAKEN OR COUNTED BEFORE THEN. THAT THE READ-BACK OF THAT LEAF IS DUE ON CHAPTER 700 AND ON NO OTHER CHAPTER. THAT THE ONE LINE THIS VOLUME AUTHORISES ON THE FITTING-OUT SHEET IS ON CHAPTER 689 AND ON NO OTHER. THAT NO FIGURE OF MONEY IS TO BE SET AGAINST THE AFTERTASTE, THE KNEE, THE THREE DAYS OF SLEEP OR THE HEARING, AND THAT THE TEMPORARY HEARING LOSS IS IN THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO AND IS NOT THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-NINE'S HEARING AND DOES NOT IMPROVE ANYTHING OF HIS.**

### 5. WHAT IS RULED AND CARRIED AND NOT REPAIRED, NAMED ONCE

**THE APPARATUS SHARE OF THESE TEN DAYS, WHICH IS THE HOUSE'S OWN FORM ACROSS FOURTEEN VOLUMES. THE LONGEST COMMON CONTIGUOUS RUN OF NINETY WORDS BETWEEN CHAPTERS 671 AND 678, BEING LOCK-REQUIRED ARITHMETIC AND STANDING APPARATUS, WHICH IS BELOW THE ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SEVEN WORDS THE INHERITED TWENTY CARRY AND BELOW THE NINETY-THREE WORDS VOLUME 13 CARRIED. THE FINDING AGAINST INHERITED `chapter-0668.md`, WHICH IS RECORDED AT THE HEAD OF `state/current.md` AND IS NOT REPAIRED HERE BECAUSE IT IS NOT THIS PHASE'S FILE.**

## Volume 13, Batch 0003 (Chapters 621–630) — **THE WRITING PASS OF MOVEMENT 3. NOTHING IN IT IS CLOSED AND NOTHING IN IT IS RESOLVED. EVERY THREAD BELOW STANDS.**

**THIS PASS OPENED NINE THREADS, CLOSED NONE AND ADVANCED FOUR. IT WROTE TEN CHAPTERS AND NOBODY WAS THANKED IN ANY OF THEM.**

### What Movement 3 now stands at

1. **THE COUNTER-PLAN IS KNOWN AND IT IS A METHOD AND NOT A BODY, AND IT BINDS A COMMUNITY THAT ADOPTS IT AND BINDS NOBODY ELSE. FOUR COMMUNITIES HAVE BEEN ASKED AND TWO HAVE AGREED AND TWO HAVE NOT, AND THE TWO THAT HAVE NOT ARE NAMED ON A PAGE BY THE NAME OF A PLACE AND ARE NOT TO BE ARGUIED WITH AND ARE NOT TO BE ASKED A SECOND TIME.** Unchanged by this batch.
2. **THE PAGE OF POSITIONS STANDS BESIDE THE SHEET OF FOURTEEN GAPS AND THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME SHEET. THE COUNT OF POSITIONS IS THREE AND IT WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN IN MOVEMENT 3.** **NEW IN THIS BATCH: on Monday the fourth of April the man who keeps the leaf put his thumb on that page at about two in the afternoon, moved it about four inches, took it off, and did not say the figure out loud. The count was taken once, off a page of days, and it was not taken again in ten days, and it is not said in a room and is not said in the half-past-five slip. The figure in the opened column against the sixteenth is still struck and still readable and is not one of the three. The row for the place about a mile inside that port is empty and stays empty.**
3. **THE FIFTH WORD IS RULED, AND THE RULING BINDS THE REST OF THE VOLUME. *KEPT* IS A FIFTH WORD WRITTEN ON THE BACK OF THAT PAGE AND IS NOT A FIFTH COLUMN, IS NOT ON THE SHEET OF POSITIONS, CARRIES NO FIGURE AGAINST ANY DAY, AND IS NOT COUNTED IN THE COUNT OF POSITIONS.** The four positions remain opened, refused, restricted and withdrawn and each keeps its column. **The revision of the method is carried forward through Movement 3 and is NOT SETTLED: the two drafts of Monday the twenty-eighth of March, the two lines of Wednesday the thirtieth and the fifth word all stand on that page, unstruck, unsigned, and nothing anywhere says settled.** It was paid in Movement 2 and it is still open on the fiftieth day.
4. **THE RELATIONSHIP DISAGREEMENT IS PAID A SECOND TIME AND IN PUBLIC AND IT IS NOT SETTLED.** On Saturday the ninth of April, in about nine people at the flat of that bench stone, Calder and Mara argued out loud for about eleven minutes about what a person is allowed to carry, in about 273, 243 and 160 words. Nobody arbitrated, nobody agreed out loud, neither of them gave anything up, nobody was thanked, and they are still married. **This is the other half of what Movement 2 paid: Movement 2 settled nothing about what a record may carry, and Movement 3 pays for what a person may carry. It is paid out loud in about nine people, it is not settled in a room with two people in it, it is not settled by secrecy, and neither of them gives up professional authority.** The keeper stood four paces off with a book under his arm and wrote nothing in a column, and said so out loud in the slip.
5. **A CROWN VESSEL WENT ON A BAR OF HARD SAND ON SATURDAY THE SECOND OF APRIL AND IT COST A SEASON'S WORK AND A HULL AND IT WAS PAID IN FULL BEFORE THE DAY CLOSED.** Nobody died, no body was named and no casualty figure was printed. **About six men carry it and they are on no sheet in this harbor and nobody in this harbor has a figure for what they lose between that afternoon and the first of June, and nobody is going to be asked about it.** The vessel is stated on the page not to be one of the nine hulls about two sea miles off that mole head, and nobody in this harbor has said that any of those nine has eased. **This is a fact about a bar of sand and it is not a line on the fitting-out sheet and it is not in a minute, and no volume close may read it as a thing that has been paid.**
6. **THE PAGE OF ROUTES IS A FOURTH SHEET AND IT NOW CARRIES THREE STATES IN TEN DAYS.** **THREE NAMES CHANGED IN ONE WEEK AND ALL THREE CAME FROM THE CREWS' OWN MOUTHS, UNASKED: THE ASHTIDE RUN WAS HELD AND WENT RESTRICTED ON WEDNESDAY THE SIXTH OF APRIL, THE LOWFEN REED WAS DORMANT AND WENT RESTRICTED ON FRIDAY THE EIGHTH, AND THE TERNWATCH PASSAGE WAS HELD AND WENT RESTRICTED ON SATURDAY THE NINTH. IN EVERY CASE THE EARLIER WORD WAS LEFT STANDING ABOVE THE NEW ONE AND IS STILL READABLE AND NOTHING WAS STRUCK. NO STATE WAS PUT ON ANY ROUTE BY A STORM, BY A LOSS OR BY A CROWN INSTRUMENT, AND NO ROUTE CREW WAS ASKED A STATE TWICE.** At the close of Chapter 630 the sheet reads **two held, four restricted and three dormant, and two plus four plus three is nine**, and the held column is the Morrow Line and the Saltmarch Weatherway. **A man of about fifty-six of the third lay who lands fish added the three figures with a leaf and a pencil in about a minute, got nine, read the nine names, and got nine again.** **THE COUNT IS WRITTEN DOWN TWICE IN THE FIFTY CHAPTERS, ON CHAPTER 630 AND ON CHAPTER 650, AND ON NEITHER DAY IS IT SAID IN A ROOM AND ON NEITHER DAY IS IT SAID IN THE HALF-PAST-FIVE SLIP.**
7. **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-THREE WITH A BOAT OF ABOUT FOURTEEN TONS SPOKE TWICE IN TEN DAYS AND WAS ANSWERED NEITHER TIME.** On Thursday the seventh of April he said in about three hundred and fifty-eight words that a day against a name on a sheet means a thing that happened and not a thing that was said, and that this yard has spent eleven weeks teaching people the difference and that board has it the other way round. Nobody agreed with him, nobody answered him, nobody thanked him and nobody told him he was wrong, and he was not told he was wrong. His eleven words are still on a page, unanswered, unthanked and with no figure set against them.
8. **THE FITTING-OUT SHEET STANDS AT NINETY-SEVEN THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE SHORT AND DID NOT MOVE, AND A RESOLUTION THAT COST SOMEBODY SOMETHING IS ON NO LINE OF IT.** **THE FIRST LINE OF THIS VOLUME GOES ON IT IN MOVEMENT 4 AND IT IS THE BILL FOR A STORM THAT IS NOT A WEATHER, AND A PAGE OF POSITIONS IS NOT A LINE AND AN HOUR SPENT ON IT IS NOT A LINE AND A HULL ON SAND IS NOT A LINE AND A RESOLUTION IS NOT A LINE.**
9. **THE NEW QUESTION WAS ASKED ONCE IN CHAPTER 600 AND ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND WAS NOT RE-ASKED IN THESE TEN DAYS AND WAS NOT ANSWED, AND THE WORD *SINGULAR* IS IN NO MOUTH IN VOLUME 13. THE QUESTION OF VOLUME 13 IS NOT ASKED IN ANY OF CHAPTERS 621 TO 630.**
10. **THE CIVIL CEREMONY WAS GONE THROUGH ON SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF FEBRUARY IN A ROOM THAT WAS LET OUT AND WAS NOT PAID FOR, AND THE SECOND AND THIRD OF ITS FOUR LINES SAY IN PRINT THAT IT DOES NOT MAKE HER RESPONSIBLE FOR HIS DIVING AND DOES NOT MAKE HIM RESPONSIBLE FOR HER RECORD, AND NEITHER NAME IS ON ANY PAGE AND THOSE TWO LINES WERE NOT REPRODUCED IN ANY MOUTH IN MOVEMENT 3.**
11. **No stage was taken, the word *stage* is in no mouth, the third column is empty and unappointed with a boy's hand at the head of it, his surname on no page, and he is not on the water. The boy was on the stool at the end of that stall on the fifth of April and nobody said a word to him about the water. The fourth column stands at one hundred and twenty-five with no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it, and the reason it took no line was entered once in an earlier volume and is not entered again. The bag is twenty-eight pence on all ten days.**

The fourth stands at one hundred and twenty-five, took no line, is not closed and is not struck, and the count of the twenty-eighth day of August across the ten is zero. **THE WHOLE OF THE AFTERNOON OF THE THIRTIETH WENT INTO THE SECOND COLUMN WITH THE HOUR AGAINST IT AND NOT ONE WORD OF IT WENT INTO THE FIRST, AND SO DID THE THREE ACCOUNTS THAT DO NOT AGREE, AND SO DID THE THIRTY-FIRST'S THREE QUESTIONS.**

**T8. THE HARBOR — POORER OR THE SAME, AND EVERY ITEM OF IT UNMOVED.** **THE WAGE COLUMN IN IT HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER, WHICH IS WHEN THE TWENTY-SIXTH LINE AND THE LAST FOUR MARKS WENT ONTO IT AND IT HAD BEEN TWENTY-FIVE LINES AND ONE HUNDRED MARKS THE WEEK BEFORE, AND ON THE SIXTY-SECOND WAGE TUESDAY, THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF DECEMBER, IT STOOD AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS WITH TWENTY ENVELOPES IN A CHEST, WAS READ OUT ON THE STEP AT THE BACK OF THAT MARKET AT TEN O'CLOCK BY A CLERK WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR AT THE FOOT OF THE READING IN FRONT OF ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE OF WHOM ABOUT TWENTY CANNOT READ THE COLUMN ON THE LID, DID NOT MOVE, PAID NOBODY A PENNY, AND LEFT A FURTHER WEEK FALLEN DUE BEING THE SIXTY-SECOND.** A twelfth week of that winter is in that column and a woman at the front of that step asked which twelfth and nobody answered her. The cistern was charged for the hundred and tenth, hundred and eleventh and hundred and twelfth times and walked on at all three, and the name at the top of that rota board is still off it. The wall came down bare behind a reeve's bench for the eighty-sixth time and went up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth. **THE FOUR HEADS ON THAT WALL HAVE NOT CHANGED AND NO FIFTH HEAD WENT ON IT ON ACCOUNT OF A COMMONWEALTH, A CONDITION, A LIST, A BUOY, A STAGE OR A VICTORY, AND THE FITTING-OUT SHEET IS ON NO WALL IN THAT ROOM AND THE TWO SHEETS WERE NAMED SEPARATELY AND OUT LOUD IN THAT ROOM ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH AND WERE NEVER IN ONE MOUTH WITHOUT BOTH BEING NAMED.**

**T9. THE LIVES — NOT IMPROVED, NOT ARGUED WITH, NOT FIGURED, NOT THANKED.** A man of about thirty-four of that port stated a condition and was not thanked for it and has not been thanked since. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO ANSWERED IT IN ELEVEN WORDS IN A ROOM AND WAS NOT RESTORED BY IT, WAS NOT MADE A HEAD OF ANYTHING, WAS NOT SET A FIGURE AGAINST, AND IS NOT CERTAIN WHICH OF THREE ACCOUNTS WAS HIS OWN.** The man of about thirty-four of the second lay still has a hole in the middle of a Tuesday and it is on the page of this movement only in the standing paragraph. The man of about thirty-eight who said no on the twenty-first kept what he is keeping, was not asked about it, and **is not to be confused with the man of about thirty-eight who works that compressor and went into about four fathoms on the thirtieth; they are two different men on the same harbor and nobody in that harbor connected the two things.** The man of about fifty-one out of a coast town four days down was in that harbor all ten days, read the buoys list on the Sunday and said nothing about it, was not sent for, was not asked whether he would come down that coast road, and has said nothing to anybody about a page of six names for a hundred and seventy days. The man of about twenty-nine can hear out of the left side of his head and it has been twenty-eight days and nothing anybody has done has made it into a thing he is better at. **THE BELLWRIGHT OF THAT HARBOR WAS NOT ASKED FOR A FIGURE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND GAVE NONE AND HIS CHEST IS SHUT AND THE EIGHT MARKS AND A DAY OF A BOAT ARE UNARGUED.** **THE COUNT OF *CHORUS* ACROSS CHAPTERS 521 TO 530 IS ZERO AND THE STAGE IS NOT NAMED, NOT PRE-FIGURED, TAKEN ONCE AND NOT DESCRIBED AFTERWARDS, AND NO PROTOTYPE WORK IS DONE IN IT.**

**T10. THE QUESTION AND THE PARTY.** The question a woman of about fifty-eight asked at a mole head on the second of December was not asked again on any of these ten days, was not used as a reason, and the count of it across Chapters 521 to 530 is zero. The question of Chapter 550 is not asked. **The word *singular* is not said of a person in any of these ten chapters.** **The party is no longer the body that decides where a boat goes in that harbor, and that is now on a page, in a yard's own mouth, and in the record of a room: four lines with his own name and an hour under each, and a buoys list with local crews' names at the head of it and his name nowhere on it.** **AND THE PARTY GOES DOWN THAT COAST ROAD ONCE, ON THE THIRTY-FIRST, THE LAST DAY OF THIS MOVEMENT, WHICH IS THE DAY IT LEAVES AND NOT BEFORE: on the twenty-third the two wagons and the handcart carried that yard's gear down the road ahead of it and came back up it empty before dark, and that gear is lying at the end of it under a tarpaulin with a chain and a padlock on it and nobody standing over it. EVERY ONE OF THE SIX PLACES ON THE TEN PAGES THAT NAMES A DEPARTURE NAMES THAT DAY.**

### What a later phase may not do with this movement

1. **MAY NOT ENTER THE CHORUS DIVER STAGE AGAIN, MAY NOT NAME IT IN ANY MOUTH, MAY NOT IMPROVE IT, AND MAY NOT HAVE ANYBODY GO DOWN IN ABOUT FOUR FATHOMS OFF THAT THIRD LAY TO HOLD A SECOND CHANNEL, A THIRD CHANNEL, OR A BETTER VERSION OF ONE.**
2. **MAY NOT ASK ANY OF THE THREE MEN OF THE THIRTIETH WHY THEY SAID WHAT THEY SAID, AND MAY NOT SETTLE WHETHER THAT FLOAT WAS HELD OR LOOSE.**
3. **MAY NOT ASK THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO WHICH OF THE THREE ACCOUNTS WAS HIS OWN AGAIN, MAY NOT IMPROVE IT, MAY NOT REPAIR IT, MAY NOT SET A FIGURE AGAINST IT, AND MAY NOT MAKE HIM A CASUALTY.**
4. **MAY NOT LIFT THE AFTERTASTE AND MAY NOT MAKE IT A CONDITION TO BE FIXED.**
5. **MAY NOT PUT THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO SAID NO ON THE TWENTY-FIRST INTO THE THREE OF THE THIRTIETH, AND MAY NOT ASK HIM WHY HE SAID NO AT ANY POINT IN THIS VOLUME.**
6. **MAY NOT GIVE THE BUOYS BACK, MAY NOT PUT A NAME OF THIS PARTY'S ON THE BUOYS LIST, MAY NOT ADD A FIFTH HEAD TO THAT WALL, AND MAY NOT HAVE THE PARTY BE THE BODY THAT DECIDES WHERE A BOAT GOES.**
7. **MAY NOT AGREE TO THE CONDITION FOR THAT COMMONWEALTH IN THAT HARBOR, MAY NOT MOVE THE THREE MARKS OFF THE NINTH OF NOVEMBER, AND MAY NOT SETTLE THE ENTRY.**
8. **MAY NOT READ THE PROOF OUT AGAIN, MAY NOT GET AN ANSWER OUT OF IT, MAY NOT OPEN THE DRAWER ON THE HILL, MAY NOT PUT A DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IN THAT ROOM ON A PAGE, AND MAY NOT USE THE SHEET OF ABOUT FOUR FEET TO DECIDE WHERE A BOAT GOES.**
9. **MAY NOT RE-ASK THE QUESTION OF THE SECOND OF DECEMBER, MAY NOT ASK THE QUESTION OF CHAPTER 550, AND MAY NOT SAY *SINGULAR* OF A PERSON.**
10. **MAY NOT SAY THAT A LINE OF BOATS HAS BEEN TAKEN AWAY OR HAS EASED BEFORE CHAPTER 550, AND MAY NOT LET THE CORDON IMPROVE A SINGLE PRICE ON A SINGLE BOARD IN THAT HARBOR.**
11. **MAY NOT KEEP, NAME OR COUNT A LIST OF ANYBODY WHO PUT NOTHING IN, AND MAY NOT ASK ANY OF THE THREE, THE FOUR, THE SEVEN, THE TWO MEN ON THE HIRED BOAT OR THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF THAT PORT AGAIN.**
12. **MAY NOT READ THE FITTING-OUT SHEET OUT IN THE ROOM OVER THAT MARKET, AND MAY NOT PUT IT AND THE FOUR HEADS IN ONE CLAUSE, ONE COLUMN, ONE ROOM OR ONE MOUTH WITHOUT BOTH BEING NAMED OUT LOUD.**
13. **MAY NOT TELL ANYBODY THAT A COMMONWEALTH'S CONDITION HAS BEEN KEPT AND THAT A HARBOR HAS THEREBY GOT SOMETHING CHEAPER. IT HAS NOT, AND CHAPTER 530 SAYS SO OUT LOUD, AND NO LATER CHAPTER MAY UNDO IT.**
14. **MAY NOT NAME A FIGURE OF A DEPTH GREATER THAN ABOUT FOUR FATHOMS ON THAT COAST, AND MAY NOT PUT THE CHAMBER WITH THE STOVE IN IT BACK ON A PAGE OF THIS VOLUME.**

### Still open, and unchanged

The cache is on the bottom in the racks and is on no page of this movement. The crate came up empty and is in that boat's forepeak. The one damp brown page is flat under a weight in a room over that market and is on no page of this movement. **The proof is in a locked case on a long table in that room and was not read out again on any of the ten days and no chapter of this movement got an answer out of it.** The three accounts of the floor of October past are not settled. The rail is not identified. The question a man of about thirty-four asked is still open. The third column is empty and the boy's hand is not scratched out. **The fourth column stands at one hundred and twenty-five with no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it.** Nobody was thanked for anything on any of these ten days, and the volume is thirty chapters old of fifty and is not closed. **The buoys are not this party's and the party is not the body that decides, and that is the midpoint and it is not reversed.**

## Volume 11, Batch 0002 (Chapters 511–520), Movement 2, *a supply boat at a figure, a commonwealth that will not sign, and a proof that a crew can refuse a channel and the route stays up* — as written, 29 September 2026. **THE MOVEMENT IS PAID. A LINE OF BOATS GETS A PRICE ON TOP OF IT. TWO PORTS ANSWER ON THEIR OWN TERMS AND ONE OF THEM SAYS NO TO A SIGNATURE. THREE LOCAL CREWS ARE ASKED TO HOLD ONE CHANNEL EACH OF THE SAME FORTY MINUTES AND ONE OF THE THREE SAYS NO OUT LOUD AT ABOUT TEN MINUTES TO THREE AND THE ROUTE HOLDS ANYWAY. THE CHORUS DIVER STAGE IS NOT ENTERED, NOT NAMED AND NOT PRE-FIGURED. NOTHING ON THE POVERTY LIST IMPROVED AND NOBODY WAS THANKED FOR ANYTHING.**

### Threads that advanced

**T1. THE CORDON — STILL OUTSIDE, AND IT NOW HAS A PRICE ON TOP OF IT.** Nine hulls lie about two sea miles off the head of that mole through the whole of this movement and did not swing at the half past the ebb on any of the ten days, and on the fourteenth **a boat of about two hundred tons, and not the one that came in on the fourth, came inside that line on the last of the flood and was moored at the north quay at about eleven and was not stopped by anybody in that harbor.** The paper with a seal and no figure is still nailed to the board at the head of that mole, not opened, not copied, not taken off, no key in that harbor. **STATUS: THE LINE IS OUTSIDE THE HARBOR AND STAYS THERE. IT IS NOT TAKEN AWAY, IT DOES NOT EASE, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME MAY SAY IT HAS BEFORE CHAPTER 550.**

**T2. THE PRICE — PAID, AND A PRICE IS NOT A COST.** The same victual this yard bought at sixteen hundred pence on the third of December and at one thousand nine hundred and twenty on the thirteenth was offered in that market on the fourteenth at **two thousand two hundred and forty pence for nine men for ten days, being fourteen marks**, being six hundred and forty more than the third and three hundred and twenty more than the thirteenth. **THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF CHALKED IT ON THE BACK OF A SLATE AT AN END STALL AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST ELEVEN AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT A SHEET WHICH CARRIES WHAT A MARKET IS CHARGING IS A PAGE OF WHAT OTHER PEOPLE THOUGHT THINGS WERE WORTH, AND IT IS ON NO SHEET IN THAT YARD, AND IT WAS STILL ON THAT STEP ON THE TWENTIETH AND ON THE TWENTY-SECOND.** Coal for eight days went on at two thousand and eighty pence, being thirteen marks, bought off that boat alongside the quay and not off a deck a man said something on. **STATUS: PAID. NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS ANY CHEAPER FOOD BECAUSE A LINE OF BOATS IS OUTSIDE IT, AND THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE FOR LAMP OIL DID NOT COME DOWN AND THE FIGURE OF THE FIRST OF JUNE WAS NOT TAKEN DOWN AND CANNOT BE.**

**T3. THE HARD AT ASHTIDE — ANSWERED ON SOMEBODY ELSE'S TERMS, AND NOT SETTLED.** A man of about fifty who fits boat bottoms and has been in that harbor nine weeks said out loud, in a room over that market, at about twenty past one in the afternoon of the thirteenth, that he is from that port, and gave the answer that has been standing at that hard since the ninth of November past, in about eleven words, on his own hook, with a condition attached: victual and coal off the outside at the top of the flood up to the cannery steps and nothing else off that hard, the first of anything else put back on the water where it was found and not opened by anybody at that port, and not one man of this harbor past the fish quay there. **THE THREE MARKS THAT STAND AGAINST THAT ENTRY ARE ON AN ANCHOR DATE THAT CAME IN ON THE ENTRY AND HAVE NOT BEEN RE-DATED AND DID NOT GO, AND THE ENTRY IS NOT SETTLED, AND NO FIGURE WAS SET AGAINST THAT PARTY OR AGAINST THAT PERSON, AND NOBODY WAS THANKED. THE CONDITION WAS READ OUT AGAIN, WORD FOR WORD AND IN HIS WORDS, IN THAT ROOM ON THE SUNDAY THE NINETEENTH WITH THE READER'S OWN NAME AND THE HOUR UNDER IT, AND ITS SIXTH SENTENCE SAYS THAT NOBODY HAS AGREED TO ANY OF IT AND THAT A CONDITION IS NOT AN OFFER.** STATUS: PAID AND NOT SETTLED. **A LATER MOVEMENT MAY CARRY THE CONDITION BUT MAY NOT SETTLE THE ENTRY, MOVE THE THREE MARKS OR RE-DATE THEM, AND MAY NOT HAVE A ROOM IN THAT HARBOR AGREE TO IT ON ANYBODY'S BEHALF.**

**T4. THE SEVEN AND THE FOUR — UNCHANGED AND STILL CLOSED AS A THING.** The four crews that did not write a name on the tenth of December were not asked again on any of the ten days of this movement, were not named, were not counted with anybody, and have no list. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR, WHO IS ONE OF THE FOUR MEN HIRED BY THE DAY, SAID NO IN THREE SENTENCES ON THE TWENTY-FIRST AND WAS NOT ASKED WHY AND WAS NOT ARGUED WITH AND IS NOT ASKED AGAIN IN THIS VOLUME, AND HE KEEPS WHAT HE IS KEEPING AND NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST HIM.** Three local crews were asked on the twenty-first whether they would each hold one channel of the same forty minutes of water, in seven sentences written before anybody was asked anything, one at a time and not in front of each other. **TWO SAID YES AND ONE SAID NO AND THE ROUTE HELD.** STATUS: PAID. **THE FOUR THAT SAID NO NOW STAND AT FOUR ACROSS TWO MOVEMENTS AND NONE OF THEM IS ASKED AGAIN.** **AND THE FISHER COMMONWEALTH THAT WOULD NOT SIGN IS THE ONE AT THE HARD ANSWERED IN MOVEMENT 2 AND IS NOT AT TERNWATCH, WHICH IS RULED AND RECORDED AS DIVERGENCE FIVE IN `outline/volume-11.md` AND IS BINDING ON MOVEMENT 3: L61 GOVERNS AND TERNWATCH IS NOT ENTERED BEFORE MOVEMENT 4, THE COMMONWEALTH IS ELEVEN MILES UP THAT COAST, AND IT IS THE SAME BODY THAT BRINGS ITS CONDITION IN CHAPTER 526. NO PLACE IS NAMED ON ANY PAGE — CHAPTER 518 SAYS *AT THAT PORT* AND THE QUEUED PROMPT SAYS *A PORT FOUR DAYS DOWN THAT COAST*.**

**T5. THE MARK — PAID, AND IT HAS AN EYE IN IT.** A float of tarred fir with a ring of chain round its waist, a cast bell under a board on four sticks and forty fathoms of two-inch stuff went onto the sheet at six hundred and forty pence, being four marks, with the seventh of December against it, and on the twenty-first **an eye was put into the stone under that float in about four fathoms off that third lay on the last of the ebb, by one man, under a slate, with a named tender on the surface, an independent line, a figure of thirty minutes, a reason in his own words and a cutoff that was pulled without anybody asking, and the clock closes at every figure in it.** The bellwright was not asked for a figure on any of the ten days of this movement and gave none and his chest is shut and the eight marks and a day of a boat are unargued. **THE BELL WAS STRUCK ONCE WHEN THE MAKING CAME HARD AT ABOUT FOUR O'CLOCK AND WAS NOT STRUCK TWICE, THE FLOAT WAS TAKEN UP ON ITS OWN LINE AND ON NO OTHER AT ABOUT TEN TO FIVE, AND THE BELL IS NOT STRUCK AT ANY HOUR OF ANY DAY.** STATUS: PAID. **A LATER MOVEMENT MAY TAKE THE BUOYS OFF THIS PARTY'S HANDS. IT MAY NOT TAKE A STAGE ON AN EARNED-WITNESS BASIS, AND IT MAY NOT HAVE ANYBODY GO BACK INTO THAT WATER AND DO THE TWENTY-FIRST AGAIN WITH A DIFFERENT MAN IN THE PLACE OF THE ONE WHO SAID NO.**

**T6. THE MONEY — PAID, ALL OF IT OUT, AND IT DID NOT BALANCE.** Seven lines out and nothing in on any line in any hand, being **7,520 pence, being forty-seven marks exactly**, and **the sheet is thirty-six thousand eight hundred and ninety-eight pence short at the close of the tenth, being two hundred and thirty marks, eight shillings and twopence**, against ten thousand six hundred and forty in. **NO PENNY OF ANY OF IT CAME OUT OF THE BAG, OUT OF THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT, OUT OF THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS OR OUT OF THE CROWN, AND NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT HARBOR WAS ASKED FOR ANY PART OF IT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS.** The bag is twenty-eight pence on all ten and is never zero. **THE MECHANISM IS ON THE PAGE AND IS THE YARD'S OWN, and on one line of the seven the day the work was done and the day the line was written are two different days, being the three hundred and thirty-six pence, which carries the sixteenth and moved the total on the eighteenth, and both days are on the face of the line.** STATUS: PAID. **THE SHEET IS NOT MADE TO BALANCE BY ASKING A HARBOR FOR THE DIFFERENCE AND IT WILL NOT BE, AND NO LIST OF ANYBODY WHO PUT NOTHING IN IS KEPT IN THAT TOWN AND NONE IS GOING TO BE.**

**T7. THE LEAF — PAID, AND IT IS TWENTY CHAPTERS FROM THE END OF THE VOLUME.** Ten more entries went in on the ten days, one against each of them, and the leaf stands at **two hundred and fifty-three, one thousand and one hundred and thirty-nine, none and one hundred and twenty-five** at the close of Chapter 520, and **243 + 10 = 253 and 1,089 + 50 = 1,139, which is the pair at the close of Chapter 520 and not the pair for Chapter 550, which `outline/volume-11.md` L37 fixes at 283 and 1,289, being 233 + 50 and 1,039 + 250, and the three later movements put the thirty and the hundred and fifty between those two pairs.** There was no read-back in this movement and the read-back is due in Chapter 550. The third column is empty and unappointed with a boy's hand at the head of it, his surname is on no page of these ten, and he is not on the water. The fourth stands at one hundred and twenty-five, took no line, is not closed and is not struck, and the reason it took no line was not re-entered and the count of the twenty-eighth day of August across the ten is zero. **THE WHOLE OF THE AFTERNOON OF THE TWENTY-FIRST WENT INTO THE SECOND COLUMN WITH THE HOUR AGAINST IT AND NOT ONE WORD OF IT WENT INTO THE FIRST, BECAUSE THE FIRST COLUMN IS A THING A STRANGER CAN COUNT AND THAT AFTERNOON WAS NOT A DAY.**

**T8. THE HARBOR — POORER OR THE SAME, AND EVERY ITEM OF IT UNMOVED.** **AND THE WAGE COLUMN IN IT HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER, WHICH IS TUESDAY AND IS WHEN THE TWENTY-SIXTH LINE AND THE LAST FOUR MARKS WENT ONTO IT, AND IT DID MOVE AFTER THE SEVENTH OF OCTOBER, WHICH IS WHY THAT DATE IS NOT CARRIED, AND THE REPAIR OF THAT FIGURE IN CHAPTER 520 IS RECORDED AT `state/continuity.md` § *The repair pass over Volume 11, Batch 0002* item nine, AGAINST VOLUME 04'S OWN CALENDAR AT `chapter-0194` AND `chapter-0195`.** No flour and none coming this month. No barley since the middle of September. No barrel of lamp oil since the twenty-ninth of August, four hundred and fifty pence still on a board with February's figure above it and both dates on it. No physic at fourteen pence. The mole-head light out and its lens out since the seventh of May. The north berth out. The hose dead until the spring. The tide gang four men short. One berth short on the third lay. Nineteen winters disputed. The hard at another port answered and not settled. The cistern charged for the hundred and seventh, hundred and eighth and hundred and ninth times and walked on at all three, and the name at the top of that rota board is still off it. The wall came down bare behind a reeve's bench for the eighty-fifth time and went up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth. **The wage column at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with twenty envelopes in a chest was read out on the step at the back of that market on the fourteenth and on the twenty-first, in front of about forty people of whom about twenty cannot read the column on the lid, and it did not move on either day, and nobody was paid a penny out of that chest, and the sixtieth and the sixty-first weeks stand fallen due at the closes of those two days, and the finding out was not a payment.** **THE FOUR HEADS ON THAT WALL HAVE NOT CHANGED AND NO FIFTH HEAD WENT ON IT ON ACCOUNT OF A LIST, A CONDITION, A COMMONWEALTH, A PRICE OR A FIGURE, AND THE FITTING-OUT SHEET IS ON NO WALL IN THAT ROOM AND THE TWO SHEETS WERE NEVER IN ONE MOUTH WITHOUT BOTH BEING NAMED.**

**T9. THE LIVES — NOT IMPROVED, NOT ARGUED WITH, NOT FIGURED, NOT THANKED.** **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO ASKED A WOMAN OF THIRTY OF NO OFFICE OUT LOUD, IN A ROOM, IN FRONT OF ABOUT TWENTY PEOPLE, FOR HER HELP WITH THE RECORD, AND DID NOT ASSUME IT AND DID NOT TELL HER WHAT SHE WOULD DO WITH IT, AND SHE SAID YES IN ONE WORD AND WAS NOT THANKED AND HE WAS NOT THANKED AND NOBODY HAS OFFERED TO.** The man of about thirty-four still has a hole in the middle of a Tuesday and is on the page of this movement only in the standing paragraph. The man of about thirty-eight kept what he is keeping and said no and is not asked about it. The man of about twenty-nine can hear out of the left side of his head and it has been fourteen days by the twenty-second and has not been made into anything. **THE PUMP HAND OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR ASKED WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE PLAN FAILS IN FRONT OF NINE PEOPLE, WAS GIVEN THE WHOLE OF THE ANSWER BY FIVE PEOPLE IN THEIR OWN TRADES, AND WAS NOT A MASCOT AND WAS NOT SENT FOR AGAIN ON ANY DAY OF THIS MOVEMENT AND IS ON NO LINE OF ANY SHEET.** **THE COUNT OF *CHORUS* ACROSS CHAPTERS 511 TO 520 IS ZERO AND THE STAGE IS NOT ENTERED, NOT NAMED AND NOT PRE-FIGURED, AND NO PROTOTYPE WORK IS DONE IN IT.**

**T10. THE QUESTION AND THE PARTY.** The question a woman of about fifty-eight asked at a mole head on the second of December was not asked again on any of these ten days and was not used as a reason and the count of it across Chapters 511 to 520 is zero. The question of Chapter 550 is not asked. **The word *singular* is not said of a person in any of these ten chapters.** The party is no longer the body that decides where a boat goes in this harbor: a man of fifty from another port answered a hard in a room full of people who cannot read, a man of about thirty-three read a Crown list out and told a room what he could not tell it, a working person of a fisher commonwealth said no to a signature and was not argued with, and three local crews held a mark that this party put there. **The surrender of that, in the yard's own mouth and in front of people who cannot read, is Movement 3's and is not paid here.**

10. **MAY NOT RE-ASK THE QUESTION A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT ASKED AT A MOLE HEAD ON THE SECOND OF DECEMBER, MAY NOT USE IT AS A REASON, MAY NOT ASK THE QUESTION OF CHAPTER 550, AND MAY NOT SAY *SINGULAR* OF A PERSON.**

12. **MAY NOT NAME WHO ALTERED THE FERRY'S PAPER, AT WHOSE INSTANCE OR WITH WHAT INTENT, MAY NOT OPEN THE DRAWER ON THE HILL, MAY NOT PUT A DIGIT OF ANY OF THE THREE NUMBERS IN THAT ROOM ON A PAGE, AND MAY NOT USE THE SHEET OF ABOUT FOUR FEET TO DECIDE WHERE A BOAT GOES.**

## Volume 11, Batch 0001 (Chapters 501–510), Movement 1, *a line of boats outside the mole, and a paper that says what may not come in* — as written and as repaired on re-dispatch, 29 September 2026. **THE MOVEMENT IS PAID. A LINE OF BOATS ARRIVES, A PAPER ARRIVES, A HARBOR GETS POORER, AND THE PARTY DISCOVERS ON THE PAGE, OUT LOUD, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH AND ONCE, THAT A ROUTE HELD BY NINE PEOPLE IS A ROUTE THAT STOPS WHEN ONE OF THE NINE STOPS. NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 10 NAMES ANY OF THAT AND NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 11 MAY NAME IT OUT OF THIS SHEET.** The sheet cannot answer it and Volume 11 has to find it somewhere else, and the finding has to cost a labor-based expedition or a political document whose limits the characters understand.

**T5. THE FOUR LINES AND THE NO — PAID.** At about two in the afternoon on the thirtieth the holder of that writ stood in a room over a fish market in front of about twenty people, about eleven of whom cannot read, to read four lines he had written himself, and was told no in about a quarter of an hour by a man of about forty-six who mends nets on the third lay and has never argued with him about anything, on the ground that a man who reads out a thing he has a stake in cannot be stopped by anybody standing in the room and that their whole power to stop him is one word and that word is not a stop. **He sat down at about ten past three. He was not thanked, the room was not satisfied, and nothing was settled.** Four lines were then read out loud by that same man with the holder's own name and an hour under each of them, and about eleven people who cannot read heard all four, and the name on each of the four is his own and he was not restored by any of them. STATUS: PAID AND NOT SETTLED. **THE HOLE IN THE RULE IS NOT PAPERED OVER AND MAY NOT BE PAPERED OVER IN VOLUME 11 EITHER, BY A SECOND LINE CALLED THE FIRST ONE, BY A VOTE, OR BY A ROOM WITH TWO PEOPLE IN IT.**

**T6. THE ROLL OF THE PEOPLE WHO PUT NOTHING IN — REFUSED AND CLOSED AS A THING THAT WILL NOT BE KEPT.** Proposed out loud in that room at about ten past three on the twenty-ninth, refused in about four words by a ropemaker of about sixty-one, refused again in the open by the holder of that writ, and **nobody wrote anything. There is no roll in that room, there is none in that harbor, and none is going to be.** STATUS: CLOSED AS AN OBJECT AND IT MAY NOT REOPEN IN A NEW FORM. No chapter of Volume 11 may keep one, name one, count one, or produce one in a different hand or on a different sheet. **The three who said no on the thirteenth and fourteenth of October past stand on the fitting-out sheet at the same size as every figure on it and none of the three was asked again in this movement.**

**T7. THE QUESTION — ASKED ONCE, ANSWERED BY NOBODY, RECORDED AS ASKED.** *If they are putting that old thing back together on that floor down there, how many harbors have to be joined up to it before a man can make it work?* Asked at about twenty to six in the evening on Thursday the second day of December at a mole head in Morrow Quay, in a woman of about fifty-eight with an end stall and a slate, naming no person, in about eleven people's hearing, **answered by nobody**, entered in that minute as asked with the hour against it, read back to the woman who asked it at her asking and not at her request, and not asked again. **THE COUNT OF THAT QUESTION, AND OF ANY FORM OF IT, ACROSS CHAPTERS 491 TO 499 IS ZERO AND ACROSS 491 TO 500 IT IS ONE. IT IS IN ONE MOUTH.** STATUS: OPEN AND IT IS THE HOOK THE SERIES RUNS ON INTO VOLUME 11. **VOLUME 11 MAY NOT RE-ASK IT IN THE SAME WORDS AND MAY NOT ANSWER IT.** Volume 12's question, named at `outline/series.md`, is a different question and is not this one.

**T8. THE CHAMBER AND THE MACHINE — STILL ON THE BOTTOM AND VISIBLE.** A chamber with a stove in it standing about ten foot off the last of fifteen frames on four pads of sawn fir, hung and seated on the thirty-first day of October past, stove drawn out, hatch shut, no door on the shore side, **a thing and not a ship, a fort, a station, a base or a claim, and nobody has been given a key to it that anybody else does not have.** Under it, a machine six centuries old with Crown man's marks set around it. **Nobody in that harbor has been given the machine and nobody in that harbor has been stopped from knowing about it, and the word that would name the seal on a warrant is in no mouth in that boat and in no mouth in that harbor.** STATUS: OPEN AND IT IS THE OBJECT OF THE WHOLE SERIES. **A CROWN MAN'S MARKS AROUND IT IS A CLAIM ON A FLOOR AND NOT A POSSESSION, AND NO VOLUME MAY CONVERT IT INTO ONE WITHOUT A LABOR-BASED EXPEDITION AND A COST.**

### Threads that are open and are not paid

**T9. THE FOUR HEAD-HEET IN THE ROOM OVER THE FISH MARKET. UNCHANGED.** Four rule-heads, four standing lines, a claim against the copy that it does not discharge, four lines saying what it is not, eleven names at the foot of it with eleven people who did not sign it. **It did not change on the thirtieth, and a fifth head was not going to be added to that wall by anybody on account of a Tuesday, and a head is not going to be added in Volume 11 on account of a blockade either.** It is a sheet of about three feet. It has no jurisdiction, no head, no seat, no roll and no money. **It may not be put on a wall in Morrow Quay as a chart, and it is not the fitting-out sheet and the two are never in one clause, one column, one room or one mouth without both being named out loud separately.**

**T10. THE WAGE COLUMN AND THE STANDING CONDITION OF THAT HARBOR. UNCHANGED AND NOT IMPROVED.** Twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, twenty envelopes in a chest, **fifty-eight weeks fallen due at the close of the thirtieth**, a further week fallen due at every wage Tuesday, and neither wage Tuesday in this movement moved it. No flour in that market and none coming this month, no barley since the middle of September, no barrel of lamp oil since the twenty-ninth of August with four hundred and fifty pence on a board at an end stall that did not come down, no physic at fourteen pence and none of it, the mole-head light out and its lens out since the seventh of May, the north berth out, the hose dead until the spring, the tide gang four men short, the hard at Ashtide unanswered, one berth short on the third lay, nineteen winters disputed. **THE HARBOR IS POORER ON THE SECOND DAY OF DECEMBER THAN ON THE THIRTEENTH DAY OF OCTOBER AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE COST, AND NOT ONE PRICE ON ANY LIST CAME DOWN.** A third cistern charge in this volume falls on a rota day in Volume 11 and is walked on at every charge.

**T11. THE THIRD COLUMN, THE BOY'S HAND AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT. UNCHANGED.** The third column is empty, nobody has been appointed to it, nobody has been scratched out, **the hand of a boy of twenty-two is at the head of it and his surname is on no page of that harbor and he is not on the water and nobody has asked him why.** The fourth column stands at one hundred and twenty-five and has taken no line, has no hundred and twenty-sixth line, is not closed and is not struck. **A man of about thirty-eight keeps what he is keeping and is not asked about it**, and the beat in Chapter 495 where he says he has a thing he is not going to be asked about and is not going to hand over is a refusal to know, not a disclosure, and is ruled as such in `state/continuity.md` § C8.

**T12. THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-NINE. UNCHANGED AND IMPROVABLE BY NOBODY.** He cannot hear out of the left side of his head, it did not lift on the twenty-eighth, the twenty-ninth, the thirtieth, the first or the second, **it lifts on the fourth day of December, which is after this volume**, and no chapter has said when it will in a working person's mouth and no chapter of Volume 11 may declare it improved or use it as a motive or put a figure on it. He stood at the front of that mole head on the second day of December and did not hear the question asked and nobody told him he had.

**T13. THE SIX ACCOUNTS AND THE THREE THAT DO NOT AGREE. UNCHANGED.** None of the ten is settled in these ten chapters, no eleventh is added that agrees with one of them, and none of the ten is removed. The three one-thing accounts of the seventeenth of October past do not agree, settle nothing, and **no chapter of Volume 11 may re-ask any of the three, settle them, or check any part of them.**

**T14. THE FOUR QUESTIONS OF VOLUME 09 AND THE QUESTION OF VOLUME 09'S LAST MOVEMENT. UNCHANGED.** None was asked in Movement 5 and none was answered in it, and the room over the west basin is not in these ten chapters. **The question a man of about thirty-four asked and was not answered — *how do you know it was the paper* — is still open, may be left open for the length of the series, may not be re-asked in the same words, and may not be answered in a room with two people in it.**

**T15. THE TWO MEN WHO ARE NOT ONE MAN. UNCHANGED.** Ollum Trevask, of about thirty-four, of the second lay, keeps the whole fouling ladder in that harbor in his own book, **has no chart and is not to be given one, has refused to put a number of centuries on anything four times, and no chapter of Volume 11 may ask him for another figure, for a year, or for his book.** The man of about thirty-one of the third lay with a chart in a bag is a different man, is not put in a room, is not asked for his chart and does not produce it. **Sabra Loach is a woman of about thirty-one who crews nothing and sells nothing and no later card may call her a man.** In Movement 5 she went down once, on the twenty-third, and said one thing about her own body and not one thing about what was in the room.

**T16. THE MASTER OF THAT BOAT OF ABOUT NINETEEN TONS. PAID AND CLOSED AS A COMMITMENT.** He came ashore on the twenty-seventh with his two men and his boy, was not thanked, nobody asked him why he came, nobody asked him to have come, nobody asked him for a date and he gave none, and **his boat is not put to sea again on any day of that trip.** His declaration of the eleventh of November is not a vote, is not a threat, and settled nothing. **No chapter of Volume 11 may put a date on it, may ask him to stay, or may thank him.**

**T17. THE CROWN'S MAN ON THE SHELF. CLOSED FOR VOLUME 10, NOT RESOLVED.** A setter of marks of about thirty-six named Corwin Tace, who laid out survey for a living and worked for whoever pays, was on that floor for about three weeks under a warrant with a seal on it and no figure on it, was given nothing, was thanked by nobody, and **said that he was setting marks and that setting marks is what he does.** He is not a villain, not a general, not a face, not a plan and not a speech, and nobody said the word out loud to him. **He is not on the trench floor in Movement 5 and nobody asked why. WHAT HE IS DOING ON THAT FLOOR IN VOLUME 11 IS OPEN AND IS NOT A FIGURE ANYBODY HAS ASKED HIM FOR.**

### The standing condition of the volume as it now stands

**A machine six centuries old is on the bottom of a trench in about twenty-two fathoms under a bell-shaped chamber with a stove in it, with Crown man's marks set around it, and nobody in that harbor given it and nobody in that harbor stopped from knowing about it. The only copy of the best evidence this party ever had is in the racks in a room behind that machine. A room over a fish market holds a piece of paper with a broken impression and a name on it, in a locked case, with four limits on the face of the reading and a record of the reading in that room's own book. A man of about thirty-two has a hole in the middle of a Tuesday, an aftertaste, two hands that are not steady and a stretch of his own afternoon he cannot put in order. A man of about twenty-nine will not hear out of the left side of his head until the fourth day of December. A man of about thirty-four has been told no in a room and has not been restored by it. A man of about thirty-eight is keeping a thing. A boy of twenty-two's hand is at the head of an empty column and his surname is on no page. A woman of thirty-one of no office knows exactly where one damp page is and has said so out loud once. A ropemaker of about sixty-one put nothing in and is not on a list. A man of about fifty who wrote on a wall in October put a roll on the table and was told no in four words and did not answer. A bellwright of that harbor has not been asked for a hundred and two days and was not asked. A sheet of about four feet is in the inside pocket of a coat in a room over a fish market and has not been used to decide anything. A woman of about fifty-eight asked a question at a mole head and it is in a minute and it has no answer. The bag has twenty-eight pence in it. The harbor is poorer.**

### The next phase, and what it may not do

**THE ONE PHASE QUEUED IS `workspace/volume-11/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, BEING CHAPTERS 501 TO 510 AND THE OPENING OF VOLUME 11, *The Cordon*, IN WHICH THE CHORUS DIVER STAGE IS VOLUME 11'S. `outline/volume-11.md` DID NOT EXIST AND WAS CREATED BY THIS PHASE, IN THE HOUSE'S OWN FORM, WITH ITS OWN LOCKS, ITS OWN ARITHMETIC AND ITS OWN CALENDAR.** NO CARD FILE WAS INVENTED, `outline/batches/` IS UNCHANGED, NO MARKER FILE WAS WRITTEN, AND `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.opencode/agent/`, `AGENTS.md`, `PHASE_SYSTEM.md`, `REPO_PLAN.md`, `OUTLINE_GUIDE.md`, `opencode.json` AND `state/phase-ledger.json` WERE NOT EDITED. **THE LEDGER STILL READS `phase-000-bootstrap` AND `status: running` AGAINST A MANUSCRIPT AT CHAPTER 500, WHICH IS THE CONTROLLER'S FILE, AND IT IS THE EIGHTH TIME A WRITER PHASE HAS ESCALATED IT AND IT IS THE ONE DEFECT ON THIS LIST THAT NO PROSE CAN FIX.**

**AND VOLUME 10 IS NOT CLOSED AND NOT AUDITED. THE VOLUME 10 CLOSE AND THE VOLUME 10 AUDIT ARE STILL OWED, AND THE PHASE THAT WRITES THEM IS NOT YET QUEUED, BECAUSE A BATCH PHASE QUEUES ONE PHASE AND THE ONE IT OWED WAS THE OPENING OF VOLUME 11. THAT IS A REAL GAP AND IT IS NAMED HERE SO THAT THE NEXT PHASE TO RUN SEES IT: `state/current.md` AND `state/continuity.md` BOTH RECORD THAT VOLUME 10 IS WRITTEN TO CHAPTER 500 AND NOT CLOSED, AND THE VOLUME 10 HAND-OVER TO VOLUME 11 HAS NOT BEEN WRITTEN BY ANYBODY.**


# Open Threads

**Volume 01, Batches 0001–0005, Chapters 1–50, are written, closed and audited.** Every promise below is marked **PAID** (a chapter settled it), **PART** (a chapter moved it and named it on the page), **CARRIED** (unchanged and still owed), **RULED** (an author-level decision the volume audit settled on 26 September 2026), or **OPEN BY DESIGN**. A thread is closed only when a written chapter pays it off. The Batch 0001 block is followed by the Batch 0002 block, then the Batch 0003 block, then the Batch 0004 block, then the Batch 0005 block and the audited volume-close accounting, then the standing volume-by-volume and character promises, which are unchanged.

**The *Author-level decisions deferred to a later outline phase* list below is RULED IN FULL. Every item is now a decision, not a deferral, and each carries its ruling and the date 26 September 2026.** The full reasoning is in `reviews/volume-01/volume-01-close.md` Part 2 and the consolidated rulings are in `state/continuity.md` under *Rulings of the Volume 01 volume audit*. **Nothing in this file is waiting for a planning phase to decide.**

## Opening batch promises (Volume 01, Batch 0001, Chapters 1–10) — as paid

- **PAID — Ordinary work and cost (Chapters 1–3).** Chapter 1 opens on a paid pump repair that Calder refuses to patch, with a second crack he eats, a chandler's note eleven weeks into six, and a fouled chain that takes his shoulder. The mole haul, the anchor hook finding a real edge, and the fouled ground line give the ordinary work its whole weight before any glass is named.
- **PAID — Legitimate claim (Chapters 2–3).** The shard arises from a paid job; Calder cannot buy the claim and does not try to. He submits a labor log, an anchor position mark, and crew names, and Kest grants a **four-day disputed claim window** because Calder's work generated the recovery, not because Kest trusts him. **That window closed when the objects were surrendered.**
- **PAID — Jurisdiction on paper (Chapters 1–4).** Every dive in the batch is inside the harbor line under a named instrument: the claim window, and a separate **work permit** naming the inner edge of Gannet Shoal for **two dates** with a forty-mark bond. Kest says aloud in Chapter 3 that it does not reach the wreck's outer marks, the cutter's recorded mooring ground, or the keel line beneath the shoal. Chapter 4 pays that off: the marker line stops Calder a few fathoms short of the rib's outer end and he turns back. **The permit is spent.**
- **PAID — The first transparent hull (Chapters 3–4).** The pale run on the shoal bottom is established as a vessel-scale transparent hull with a continuous keel line and eleven keys, not a dropped panel. It is **not dated or attributed in Chapter 4**; its age and civic origin are Chapter 5's discovery and belong to the **plate** alone. The plate lifted in the same dive is transparent glass from that structure, not *Gannet* iron and not a *Gannet* artifact.
- **PAID — Two anchors, never fused (Chapters 1, 4, 8, 10).** The drifted mole anchor that held the shard is tagged and left bedded, marked with Kest's own float mark, and released back to the harbor authority for a proper lift. The freed shoal iron is a different piece, is ordinary, and stays on the Free Keel stack. Calder writes the distinction into the record in Chapter 4 (*anchor, shoal, port quarter of the Alder Reach — not the mole iron*) and both irons are named separately wherever either appears. **Neither is glass and neither was affected by the seizure.**
- **PAID — Two objects, two provenances (Chapters 5, 8, 9).** The **nine-line builder's mark is on the plate** (Chapter 5) and the **joinery match to a Crown yard case specification is on the shard's cut edges** (Chapter 9). The public provenance duplicate states both separately, and Chapter 9's second document is a separate, labelled, unverified account of the echo, kept physically apart from the physical findings. The shard is never declared pre-Dominion civic glass.
- **PAID — The two paid working days (Chapters 4–5).** One dive day and one bench day, the bench day being the permit's second date, spent building the cradle, the air limit, and the cutoff while two men were out slinging and the yard earned nothing. Both are on the record in Mara's book and in the crew's book.
- **PART — First echo cost (Chapters 6–10).** All six preconditions are spoken aloud in order, a named tender, an independent line, a fixed air limit, a seated physical anchor, a pullable cutoff, and a written reason. The costs are paid and are still active: rope-burn reenactment, tinnitus with a second bell a third of a second late, hearing confusion that survives into Chapter 10, and a line in the crew's book. **Still owed:** the two clean daylight looks before any further entry, and the twenty-four-hour minimum off the water.
- **PAID — Mara's independence (Chapters 2, 5, 8, 9).** She cannot enter an echo, certify truth, or become an assistant, and she does not. She produces the eastern rope district, refuses to certify a tidy provenance, refuses to read a builder's mark as consent, refuses to let the aperture be opened in a shed, holds the Registry's original custody log while Calder holds only a marked public copy, and writes her own stated reason for the entry. **Her refusal to certify has not yet cost her anything on the page; that cost is still owed and belongs to a later volume.**
- **PAID — Batch loss (Chapter 8).** Both glass objects leave the yard in one witnessed surrender and are entered separately in the Morrow circuit custody room. The crew keeps the freed shoal iron, the measurements, the repair-seam records, the scaled drawing, the anchor-bearing sheet, the names, the countersigned labor log, and the public provenance duplicate. **No glass stays in Calder's hands past Chapter 8, and the batch contains no loophole.**
- **CARRIED — The unaccounted plate note (Volume 4 pay-off).** The repairer's note about a plate cut from the *Gannet*'s own iron plating remains public in the copy of Alden's signed report, and Calder has now read it twice in front of his father. Alden gave one sentence in Chapter 9 — that he saw many things leave the pile in a storm in the dark and could not tell one plate from another — and no more. It is never fused with the transparent plate, and it still closes in Volume 4 with the removed file page.
- **OPEN BY DESIGN — First echo witness.** The *Vigil* rating who carried the case is still unnamed, unlocated, and uninterviewed, and the gloved hand with the caulking callus is still something the witness saw. Calder may believe it was Oren's and may not show it; the prose makes him choose not to write the heel-note down at all. See the deferred decisions list below.
- **PAID — No teacher for the entry (Volume 1 lock).** The six conditions were assembled in the yard out of Tobias Wren's secondhand memory of the Veyr cutters thirty-one years ago, Nessa's engineering, and Mara's paperwork, and the prose says so in Calder's and Nessa's own voices. No master arrived. The entry worked because the conditions were met.
- **PAID — The *Vigil* arrives as paperwork (Chapters 8–10).** A Registry seizure order, a filed naval salvage claim over the whole shoal, a cutter taking a berth at the naval pile, an officer's paper with a four hundred yard limit, and a tender setting floats on the bearing. There was no boarding, no gunfire, no physical seizure, no face-to-face meeting with Holt, and no vessel-to-vessel action of any kind.
- **CARRIED — The compartment measurement (Volume 1 midpoint pay-off).** Chapter 9 put the survey's ninth page, the public case specification, and a case length and breadth given as a **range** in the same room for the first time, laid two bearings over a public mooring line, and read the three-second gap out loud. The contradiction is now available to anyone holding four documents. **It is not proved, and no earlier chapter may treat it as proved.** The measurement at the site belongs to the Volume 1 midpoint, and the ground is under a naval claim.
- **PAID — Earned forward pull (Chapter 10).** The batch ends on **Calder's own spoken decision**, in front of Nessa, Bevin, Tobias, and Mara, after the cutter's order has arrived: he keeps investigating under naval scrutiny with no glass, no permit, no second entry, and a bell he cannot trust, gives Nessa the standing shutdown and Bevin the logbook job, and prefers to be slow and straight about it. The tender's line is the price in the scene; the last beat is his own pencil and his own sentence.
- **CARRIED — Route clue.** A broad west-southwest bearing only. Three independent bearings agreeing inside four degrees, the *Vigil*'s public mooring line, and Orison named once by Tobias at seventy fathoms down, which is the depth in `bible/world.md` and `bible/terminology.md`. **No map, no route, and no purpose.**

## Batch 0002 promises (Volume 01, Chapters 11–20) — as paid

- **PAID — Poor month economics (Ch11–13, 16, 18).** Ordinary jobs refuse a seizure crew; a technically good Free Keel strop-share encumbers the shoal iron; a Marr-name direction kills a week's scrubbing unless Calder attacks his father's report, which he refuses. One honest buoy job pays twenty-six in full and the crew eats, and the Saturday tide job on the 22nd pays twenty-four, which is what funds the ten printed copies and the bond. Air, rope, tallow, pump hire, wages, cradle, and the note stay on the page, and the mark-by-mark chain is locked in `state/continuity.md`.
- **PAID — Hearing room distinguished (Ch14, 19).** Claim window (spent recovery permission), work permit (named site and dates, spent), and one-season charter (wider seasonal permission, not held) are told apart without a glossary. The extension runs **from the 24th to the 14th of next month** — Kest's offer in the room was "twenty days further," and the term as entered is twenty-one — on twelve marks plus held gear and a harbor eighth, not ownership.
- **PAID — Shutdown exercised (Ch12).** Nessa calls "Enough" on a surge dive with the patch half seated; Calder obeys with air unspent. Hearing misplacement is operational and compensated by call-backs thereafter, including the number at the ladder whether or not it matches the diver's own count.
- **PAID — Refusals that stand (Ch13, 17).** Alden refuses work-witnessing for roof reasons (not the report), costing a job. Mara refuses provenance certification and a custody-room line and is right; both stand, and the hearing imposes the same limit on the bearing sheet without her asking. Kest in Ch14 bars the mole and gives pump packing in the same scene.
- **PAID — The family name in the hearing (Ch13, 19).** The harbor clerk uses it in Ch13 as a countersign refusal. The batch's hearing uses it as well: the naval officer asks whether the harbor authority will found an instrument on the figures of the yard that signed the *Aster Gannet* report, Calder refuses to defend his father's report, answers with Kest's own countersigned log, and the officer's note stands in the record as his question. **This is the volume's Movement 2 beat and it is spent. It may not be re-run.**
- **PAID — Mole anchor lifted by harbor (Ch14, 16).** Ordered Tuesday for Thursday's slack water; crane, chain, slip's crew, harbor cost, Kest's mark, watched from the fish dock rail because Calder was barred from the wall. Free Keel never touches it. Drifted iron is now municipal and up.
- **PAID — Public record priced (Ch18–19).** Ten crew-only copies printed for twelve marks out of Saturday's wage without Mara's name; the bond tin deliberately not opened for paper; bearing sheet and plate drawing withheld; duplicate stays public by ruling. Consent's first form stated: a record serves working hands.
- **CARRIED — Defense to the 14th, bond gear, eighth share, iron third, Venn forty, slip tides, spring cradle, ungloved arm, empty tin.** All survive into Ch21+ as debts.
- **CARRIED — Compartment, nine-line mark, Oren mark, delayed note, custody numbers.** None resolved; all restated under existing locks.

## Batch 0003 promises (Volume 01, Chapters 21–30) — as paid

- **PAID — Ordered chain, at a distance (Ch21, Ch23, Ch28).** The wreck chain is shown to be **ordered rather than scattered**, and it is shown **without touching it**: three points on one bearing, first to second a mile and two hundred yards and second to third a mile and two hundred and ten yards, a difference of ten yards, a foot and an inch of bottom in one figure out of thirty-six on two miles of a course the harbor authority itself sounded. Order shown; **purpose withheld — no chapter in the batch says the run was laid, and the word *placed* survives only inside the hearing record.** No map, no route, no line drawn between the points by the reeve's ruling. **This answers the volume's new-volume question in its first half and leaves the second half — who controls the missing links — untouched.** *(Batch 0003's review flagged one deliberate deviation from the card here: `outline/volume-01.md` Movement 3 says the vessels are **positioned**, not scattered. The chapters stop at order. Recorded in `state/continuity.md` under proposed canon changes for the volume auditor, not resolved in prose.)*
- **PAID — A fourth document and a second witness (Ch22).** The harbor authority's own 13-year-old wreck entry for the *Aster Gannet* records *number four, port side aft, grating in place, not cleared, contents not removed*, which is custody language in a harbor's hand and which explains the silence: the space was never emptied on any record in this harbor, so it was never measured. Kest is the second witness, from his own memory and his own search. **Adds a reason; proves nothing; the compartment is still unproved and the measurement remains the Volume 1 midpoint's.**
- **PAID — Training the tender (Ch23, Ch25).** Bevin Rook is the bottom man under Nessa; Calder tends with bad ears; the call-back is now a written rule that the tender's count goes in and the diver's own count goes in only if he says it aloud; and when Calder's head turns under load he is *told what the bell was* rather than left to find out. The line-diver, the pump, the fall and the board are reassigned in writing.
- **PAID — The bad descent, and its price (Ch24, Ch25).** A southerly, a borrowed boat, a shackle under the authority's own foundation stone, a chain that comes tight, and a left hand crushed in a bight. Un-recuperable on the page: two fingers, six weeks of a boy's wages, twenty-four marks the yard does not have, the Free Keel's inside-the-line rescue cover withdrawn for the winter by the crew that gave it, a stove in somebody else's boat, and a harbor that paid eighteen of twenty-six. **The crew is poorer and the tender is gone.**
- **PAID — Contagion used against its author (Ch26, Ch27).** The circuit office quotes Mara Venn's handling note of the 14th word for word, draws four clauses from it, and argues in its fourth clause that a line of joined construction is not a scatter. Her words are used **correctly and about a different subject** — the note is about a join, the notice applies it to a position — and the purpose it quotes has been stripped of the sentence in which the yard said **it had no measurement of the assertion it was making**, which is not the purpose's closing sentence but the one the whole of Chapter 22 turns on. She answers with a second note that is correct, narrow, refuses to say *safe*, refuses to say *unsafe*, and carries the **date of the 22nd, eight days after the defense lapses**. **The contagion argument is lodged and the public panic Volume 9 will later exploit has a real paper behind it.**
