THE FAIR COPY IN THE ROOM OFF THAT MARKET WAS NOT ENTERED, NOT ASKED ABOUT AND NOT READ AGAIN BY ANYBODY, AND THE SLIP OF PAPER WAS NOT LOOKED AT ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH AND IS STILL IN A DRAWER WITH A SHEET IN IT WITH A FIGURE ON IT AND NO NAME ON IT.** No document of anybody's changed hands on the water on any of the ten days, the man of about twenty-six is not back on a line of boats, and no chapter of this batch gives him a copy of anything.
2. **THE COST IN FLOUR, AND THE SECOND COST IN A MUNICIPAL BOX. THE FLOUR DID NOT MOVE AND THE BOX IS FULL. PAID, AND THE SECOND COST IS NOW THE FIRST LEGAL CONSEQUENCE OF THIS YARD'S OWN SILENCE IN THE VOLUME.** Seven boats of a tow of eight are still lying off the point at about a mile with about twenty-six tons of flour in them, and the two lights of them have not moved in twelve days at the close of this batch, being counted from the hour they were first seen on the evening of the first of August, and nobody in that harbor has hailed them. The lighter of about thirty tons was broken up in nine foot of water against the wall of that quay on the fourth of August with her frames out by eleven and nothing landed out of her at any hour, which is a different water from the four foot at the edge of the fairway. **AND ON THE ELEVENTH A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY SAID THAT THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF JULY IS IN THE BOX ON HIS TABLE IN HIS OWN HAND WITH HIS OWN HOUR, WRITTEN ON MONDAY THE THIRD AT ABOUT NINE, AND THAT HE WROTE WHAT HE KNOWS AND DID NOT WRITE WHO WAS IN THE BOAT, AND THAT HE HAD BEEN WAITING ELEVEN DAYS TO FIND OUT WHETHER THIS YARD WOULD ASK HIM AND HAD NOT, AND THAT THE FOURTH BOX ON THE OTHER PAPER IS EMPTY AND IS THE ONLY BOX IN THAT OFFICE HE HAS NEVER ONCE WANTED TO FILL, AND HE SAID SO OUT LOUD IN A DOORWAY AND IT GOES NO FURTHER THAN THAT DOORWAY. ON THE NINTH HE HAD ALSO DECIDED THAT THE NINTH OF AUGUST IS NOT GOING IN THAT BOX BECAUSE A BOAT THAT CAME IN AGAIN IS NOT A DAY. THE HOLDER ASKED HIM NOTHING AND WROTE NOTHING DOWN BECAUSE HE COULD NOT CHECK A HAIR OF IT. IT IS NOT PAID FOR BY ANYBODY ASKING FOR IT AND IT IS NOT TO BE REVERSED.**
3. **THE MUNICIPAL PAPER OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF JULY AND THE DOOR IN VEVR. CARRIED, USED, AND NOT RESOLVED.** **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WITH A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTEEN TONS AND NO MUNICIPAL PAPERS OF ANY KIND USED THE SIXTH CLAUSE OF THE NOTICE TWICE IN THESE TEN DAYS, ON THE NINTH OF AUGUST GOING OUT AND ON THE ELEVENTH OF AUGUST COMING IN, AND HE DID IT ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT AND WAS NOT SENT AND WAS NOT PAID AND WAS NOT THANKED, AND HE SAID HE CAME TO TELL AND NOT TO ASK, AS HE SAID ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JULY, AND HE WAS TOLD NOTHING AND ASKED FOR NOTHING.** A master of about thirty-three with no papers on him was put in last off the point on the eighth of August for exactly that reason, and came in on the eleventh on the same clause because there was nobody at the outer water to ask him. The herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own still will not use them for a company of boats, was not asked about it on any of the ten days, and said nothing to anybody in that shed except a word about the autumn in July. **WHO LEFT THAT PAPER ON THAT TABLE IN THE ROOM IN VEYR IS STILL UNKNOWN AND NOBODY HAS ASKED, AND THE SAYING SO IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN ON THE FIRST DAY OF THIS BATCH AND IS NOT A FIFTH PLACE.**
4. **THE APOLOGY, PAID, AND THE PROCEDURE, ASKED FOR INSTEAD. CARRIED, AND IT COST TWO QUESTIONS AND A SILENCE.** No leaf was written under the procedure in these ten days and no paper using her hand was shown in any room. **What she did: she came up that hill on the fourth of August and sat on the bench at the back and asked nothing at all, being the eleventh time she has come up that hill; she came up on the eleventh and stood in the doorway and listened to what a man of about fifty said and asked him nothing and asked the holder nothing; and on the thirteenth she was in that shed at four for the reading and asked the only question asked in it, being whether he would take them out on the day he named, and was told no, and said then that is a decision and not a finding, and the reason against the line is that he knows the hour and is not going to be at it.** SHE DID NOT FORGIVE HIM AND DID NOT THANK HIM AND NOBODY IMPROVED ON ANYTHING, AND THE FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD IS NEITHER REDUCED NOR PAID, AND THE COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP DID NOT BEGIN.
5. **THE TENDER, THE THIRD CHANNEL, AND THE THINGS MOVEMENT 3 SAID WERE NOT MEASURED. THE TENDER STAYED PUT AND THE THIRD CHANNEL WAS NOT MEASURED AND NO FIGURE OF WATER WAS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH AT ALL.** The tender of about ninety tons was at the head of eight boats inside the line on the morning of the twenty-seventh of July and was still there on the thirteenth of August, and that is eighteen days, and she was not entered, no man was put aboard her, nobody hailed her on any of the ten days, and no chapter of this batch names what she is waiting for. The third channel is still nobody's measurement and the borrowed pinger went back up that coast on the Tuesday of the thirteenth and has not come down and no hand on that coast has it. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF THE SECOND LAY WAS NOT ASKED ABOUT A HAND LEAD ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, AND THE REASON WAS GIVEN OUT LOUD TO A MAN WHO CAME TO ASK A QUESTION, BEING THE YARD'S OWN REASON AGAINST ITS OWN INTEREST.**
6. **THE MONEY, WHICH MOVED FOUR TIMES AND CLOSED LOWER THAN IT OPENED. PAID.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence in on the fourth and one hundred and sixty-eight pence in on the ninth, being a day's work with a boat and two men at a berth on each, at the figure in chalk on the slate at the end stall. One hundred and sixty-eight pence out on the tenth, being a day of a caulker of about twenty-three at the mole head, and forty-four pence out on the twelfth, being three shillings and eightpence for a loaf and a half and a candle and a pot. **The bag closes at three hundred and twenty-eight pence, being two marks and eightpence, which is a hundred and twenty-four pence more than it opened at, and the figure short of the wage of four marks is three hundred and twelve pence, being one mark twelve shillings and eightpence, one day in the ten being the ninth, on which the bag was five hundred and forty pence and the figure short of the wage was one hundred pence, being eight shillings and fourpence.** THE CHEAPEST OIL DID NOT MOVE, NO FIGURE WAS SAID OUT LOUD IN THE FRONT STREET OF THAT HARBOR ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, A MAN WENT PAST THE CHANDLER'S COUNTER WITHOUT STOPPING, AND THE MOLE-HEAD LIGHT IS OUT.
7. **THE STANDING FIGURES, ALL FIVE, AND THE NEW DAYS OF THEM. PAID.** One wipe, being the sixty-sixth on Monday the ninth, and the next being the sixty-seventh on Monday the sixteenth, which is outside the next span. Three cistern rota days charged and walked on none, being the seventieth on Thursday the fifth, the seventy-first on Monday the ninth and the seventy-second on Thursday the twelfth, and the fourth, sixth, seventh, eighth, tenth, eleventh and thirteenth of August are not rota days and no charge is placed on any of them. One wage Tuesday, being Tuesday the tenth for the forty-second week, the column unmoved on it, so that forty-two weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them at the close. **The notice is at eighty-eight days on the thirteenth; the bellwright is not asked for ninety days on the thirteenth; the two objects of nobody's are four hundred and twenty-eight days old on the thirteenth; the bench under that pump is bare for the hundred and ninety-fourth night on the thirteenth; the two lights are unmoved in twelve days; and the hundred and fifteenth line is the last line in that ledger's fourth column and the column is not closed, and the third column is empty and unappointed with a boy's hand at the head of it and his surname on no page.**
8. **THE FOUR NAMES AND FOUR HOLDS UNREACHED, THE PLATE NOT LOOKED AT, THE CHANDLER'S NOTE, THE DELAYED NOTE, THE FOUR RETURNS, THE FIRST ECHO'S WITNESS, THE SECOND SEAM, THE CAN UPON A STAKE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR. ALL FOUR HOLDS STILL UNREACHED AND TWO OF THEM STAGED.** Ashtide's three marks; the bellwright's eight marks and a day of a boat, chest shut, NOT ASKED IN NINETY DAYS, no digit printed; the five bells and the four people and their limit; and the custody room and the three items and the live question no paper answers, being a woman of about seventy and a man of about forty on a bench in a corridor, the man cannot read, **the room is not entered and no digit of any of its three numbers is on any page, and a municipal claim on one of them cannot be taken back without a request nobody in that harbor is going to make.** The plate at the fifth seam is in eleven feet and its note was not advanced in this batch and it was not named on any of the ten days. The chandler's note at thirty-one with its three counts at twenty-two, thirteen and eleven, unadvanced and not re-written, and its holder was not asked a third time by anybody and a man went past his counter without stopping. The delayed note at eleven and two, unmeasured, the call not named. The four returns and no fifth. The first echo's witness. The second seam fouled about a foot and seven inches where it was on the nineteenth of May, use closed at four figures and no fifth, ladder in another man's book, not Fisk, and the mark four hundred yards off it of a make nobody in that harbor makes, both seasons nine marks, neither paid. The can upon a stake. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR IS BACK ON THE WATER AS A BOAT'S MAN AND NOT A MASTER, AT A TILLER AND NOT AT A CAULKING IRON, NOT PAID AND NOT ASKED TO PAY, AND ON THE TWELFTH OF AUGUST HE CAME UP A HILL TO TELL THE YARD IT HAD BEEN RIGHT TO REFUSE HIM A NAME ON A LEAF AND WAS NOT THANKED AND WAS TOLD HE WOULD BE ASKED AGAIN ONE DAY AND SAID THAT WOULD BE FAIR. THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE HAS A STONE IN HIS OWN POCKET AND A PAGE ON A MOLE AND NO FIGURE AND NO BOAT AND NO WAGE.**

### Threads opened by Batch 0004

- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING ANY PERSON IN THAT HARBOR HAS EVER BEEN ABLE TO TELL IT ABOUT A COMPANY OF BOATS — THAT A COMPANY OF BOATS DOES NOT STOP BECAUSE SOMEBODY DECIDED IT SHOULD STOP, AND THAT IT STOPS ON A DAY WHEN THE PERSON WHO WAS GOING TO BE THERE IS NOT THERE, AND THAT THE BOATS DO NOT KNOW.** Said once, in his own mouth, by a caulker of about twenty-three on a mole head stone at about four in the morning on Tuesday the tenth of August, and not asked for again and not thanked for and not improved on. **IT IS ENTERED IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST, WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE BEING THAT A MAN STANDING ON A STONE AT FOUR IN THE MORNING CANNOT BE CHECKED BY A STRANGER WITH A LEAF AND A PENCIL, AND IT IS A THING A MAN OF THIS HARBOR SAID AND NOT A THING A SHED FOUND OUT, AND IT MAY NOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO ANYBODY ELSE IN THE LAST MOVEMENT AND IT MAY NOT BE IMPROVED ON IN ANYBODY'S MOUTH.**
- **OPEN — THE FIVE THINGS, FOUR OF WHICH CAN BE BOUGHT AND THE FIFTH OF WHICH CANNOT, ON A LEAF WITH NO MAN ON IT.** A spare warp; a man who can read a clock and not a watch; somebody awake ashore at the other end at the hour; a hand lead and a line and somebody who can use one; and, NOT ON THE LEAF, a person who is there on the day. **A SHIPWRIGHT OF ABOUT SIXTY REFUSED THE QUESTION OUTRIGHT ON THE FOURTH AND SAID THAT WHAT IS WANTED IS A BOAT THAT HAS BEEN KEPT AND THAT HE DOES NOT KNOW HOW ANYBODY PRICES BEING KEPT, AND NOTHING OF HIS IS ON THE LEAF, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT ANSWERED THE THIRD WITH A DOG AND A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-ONE ANSWERED THE FIFTH WITH THREE TIMES HE HAS BEEN IN COMPANY AND TWICE GOING WRONG. NO FIGURE IS ON THAT LEAF AGAINST ANY BOAT AND NO NAME IS ON IT AGAINST ANY PERSON AND IT IS NOT A CREW AND IS NOT A MUSTER AND IS NOT A ROSTER AND IT IS NOT ON ANY WALL.**
- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE AUTHOR-LEVEL DECISION OF THIS BATCH — THE PERSON WHO IS THERE ON A TUESDAY.** A caulker of about twenty-three named Isaac Fell, of the third lay, of no boat, of no crew, of no lay's crew, not on the stone, not one of the six men of that harbor who are ashore with no boat, of no office, who has been on that mole head stone at about half past three every morning he has not been able to sleep for nine years and on none of them in nine years had anybody in that harbor been on it at half past four. He was paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence on the tenth for a day, in coin, on the flat of the stone, out of that yard's own figures, being the figure in chalk on the slate at the end stall and not that yard's figure. **HE IS ON A DAY AND A WAGE AND AN HOUR AND ON NOTHING ELSE, AND HE WAS NOT PUT ON A BOARD AND WAS NOT THANKED, AND HE SAID HE HAD BEEN ON A BOARD ONCE AND WOULD RATHER BE ON A DAY, AND HE SAID THAT IF THE HOLDER WANTS A TUESDAY HE HAS TO ASK FOR A TUESDAY ON A DAY AND PAY FOR THE TUESDAY, AND THAT THE DAY HE DOES NOT ASK IS THE DAY THERE IS NOT ONE. NO LATER CHAPTER MAY PAY HIM TWICE, MAY PUT HIS NAME ON A LIST, MAY CALL HIM A MAN OF ANY OFFICE, OR MAY HAVE ANYBODY ELSE SAY THE THING HE SAID ON THE TENTH.**
- **OPEN — THE SIX MASTERS OF THE THIRD LAY, AND THE ONE WHO SAID NO.** Six were asked one at a time on the eleventh of August what a company of boats out on a flood and back on a flood with a paper between them naming each master and each man would be. Four said yes in the first hour and the master of about fifty-five said yes with a second half about a second spare warp he has not got. **THE MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE SAID NO, GAVE A REASON ABOUT A LOCKER IN A HOUSE IN ANOTHER STREET WITH THREE THINGS IN IT THAT ARE NOT PAPER, AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR THE REASON TWICE, AND THE NO IS ON THE SAME LEAF IN THE SAME HAND AND IN THE SAME PLACE AS THE YESES, AND THE REASON IS NOT ON THE LEAF AGAINST HIM IN ANY FORM.** Five masters of a third lay are five boats and a foot. The third lay fills on the first of April and one berth is short and is still short.
- **OPEN — THE SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS, AND WHAT SHE ASKED AND WHAT SHE WAS TOLD.** A lever of nineteen at her tiller read the sixth line of his own board with his thumb on the line and not his finger, and put six ticks in a list, and said nothing to anybody. On the seventh and eighth of August she put six masters of that harbor in one at a time, about half an hour each, on a question of whether their papers were in order. On the ninth she was at the other end of a tow of flour boats a mile off the point. On the eleventh she was not at that harbor's outer water at all. **ON THE THIRTEENTH SHE CAME ROUND THE POINT AT ABOUT ELEVEN WITH TWO BOATS IN HER AND WENT DOWN-COAST, HAVING ASKED WHERE THE COMPANY OUT OF THAT HARBOR SAILS AND ON WHAT DAY, AND BEEN TOLD THE FLOOD BY A MASTER OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE WHO SAID SO IN ORDER THAT THE HOLDER WOULD HEAR IT OFF HIM AND NOT OFF A SHEET.** NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WAS TOLD WHAT SHE IS FOR, NOBODY WAS TOLD A TRANSPORT WAS DUE ON THAT REACH, AND NOBODY ENTERED HER.
- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE HINGE OF THE VOLUME — THE TIMING HE CHOSE, WHICH HE NAMED OUT LOUD AND WHICH HE KNEW WAS THE TIMING OF SOMEBODY ELSE.** A flood is the only tide that harbor can make and a flood is the only hour a loaded transport can come down that reach going that way, and he chose it, and he said so in a shed with the door shut on the thirteenth of August, and he said nobody made him name the day and nobody put it in his mouth and that he did not ask what else goes down a reach on the flood because he did not ask. **THE ATTACK ON THE CIVILIAN TRANSPORT IS NOT PAID, IS NOT SOFTENED, AND WAS NOT FORESHADOWED IN ANY MOUTH IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND THE FLOUR OF THAT TRANSPORT DID NOT ARRIVE AND NO MAN DIED ON THE WATER. HE HAS ALREADY SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE WILL NOT TAKE THEM OUT ON A FLOOD, AND THAT WAS SAID TO A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY ON A QUAY ON THE TENTH AND WAS SAID AGAIN IN A SHED ON THE THIRTEENTH, AND NEITHER OF THOSE IS THE ADMISSION AND THE ADMISSION IS MOVEMENT 5'S AND IS NOT SOFTENED HERE.**
- **OPEN — A ROUTE OUT HE KNOWS AND DOES NOT HAVE.** A reach below the foul that comes out a mile and a half inside the point, a channel in it he has never been down, three soundings off a hand lead in a leaf a stranger with a lead could take again, a third channel that is nobody's measurement, a pinger that went up that coast on the Tuesday of the thirteenth and has not come down, and the one thing in the man of about thirty-four's own book that he did not name and was not asked for and is not going to be. **KNOWING WHERE A ROUTE IS AND NOT HAVING IT ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND BOTH OF THOSE ARE TRUE AND NEITHER OF THEM CANCELS THE OTHER, AND THAT SENTENCE IS THE FOURTH COLUMN'S HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH LINE AND IS THE LAST LINE IN THAT LEDGER.**
- **OPEN — WHAT WAS REFUSED IN TEN DAYS, IN A LIST, BECAUSE THE LIST IS THE MOVEMENT'S CHARACTER AND IS NOT A LIST OF VICTIMS.** A man of about fifty-five's spare warp, which he did not give away and did not promise and was not asked for. A man of about forty-four's name on a leaf in a drawer, refused the second time and refused a third time in advance, with the same reason and the same words, against the yard's own interest. A master of about thirty-three's paper, by his own refusal. A man of about thirty-one's chart in a bag, not asked about and not to be cited in a room. A fouling man's second thing, unasked. A chandler's counter, walked past. A bonesetter's hand, not taken to him and not taken anywhere else. **AND A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE'S TUESDAY, WHICH WAS NOT ASKED FOR ON THE TENTH AND WILL NOT BE ASKED FOR BY ANYBODY, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO WENT OUT TWICE ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT AND WAS NOT THANKED EITHER TIME, AND NEITHER OF THOSE IS IN THE LIST OF REFUSALS BECAUSE NEITHER WAS REFUSED.**

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE CONDITION IS SAID BY THE HOLDER, ON THE FOURTH OF AUGUST, IN HIS OWN MOUTH, OUT OF FOUR ANSWERS AND THE FIFTH MAN'S BEING LEFT OFF A LEAF, AND THE STAGE IS NOT NAMED AND IS NOT ENTERED BY BEING NAMED.** It is a trade and not a power. It is a beginning and not a stage, and it stops when the people looking after it stop. Fixed at `state/continuity.md` § 5 and at `state/current.md`.
2. **THE PERSON WHO IS THERE ON A TUESDAY IS A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE AND IS PAID ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE FOR A DAY OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES, ON THE MORNING THAT YARD DID NOT PAY ITS OWN WAGE OF SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, AND NO PART OF IT IS PAID BY THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS OR BY THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT.** The sixth term of seven terms stands, and the term is not numbered in any mouth. Fixed at § 2 and § 6.
3. **THE SIX MASTERS OF THE THIRD LAY ARE TAKEN IN BY A SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS WORKED BY A LEVER OF NINETEEN, WHO IS A WORKING MAN AND NOT AN OFFICER, AND THE ANSWER IS GIVEN BY THAT MAN OUT OF HIS OWN BOARD AND NOT BY ANY OFFICE AND NOT BY ANY ROOM.** Five of six come in under the notice's sixth clause, which is free, and the sixth, who has no papers on him, comes in on the eleventh on the same clause because there was nobody at the outer water to ask him. Fixed at § 5.
4. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT IS USED TWICE, ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT, AND IS NOT USED AS A HERO AND IS NOT THANKED EITHER TIME, AND THE FACT THAT HE HAS NO PAPERS IS WHAT MAKES A PAPERS QUESTION UNANSWERABLE IN HIS DIRECTION AND IS ALSO WHAT PUTS HIM INSIDE IT.** This is the only time in this volume a man with no papers has been useful to anybody, and it is useful because nobody could ask him a question, and it is not a reward and is not on a ledger and is not a name on a list.
5. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY IS STAGED ONCE, IN A DOORWAY, AND THE HOLDER REFUSES ON THE PAGE TO SAY IN A ROOM THAT HE CAME UP THE HILL.** The lock that he may not be cited in a room in this volume or any other is held by putting the refusal on the page and not by leaving him off it.
6. **TOBIAS WREN SAYS ONE SENTENCE IN THIS VOLUME AND IT IS ABOUT A BOAT BEING KEPT, AND HE IS NOT ASKED WHICH ONE, AND IT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN, AND NOBODY IMPROVES ON IT.** That is the correct use of him under L27a and it is his first true sentence in the volume.
7. **THE FOURTH COLUMN'S LINES ARE THE HUNDRED AND SIXTH THROUGH THE HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH, ONE A DAY, NO DAY IN TWO OF THEM, AND THE HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH IS THE LAST LINE IN THAT LEDGER.**
8. **THE FLEET OF SEVEN BOATS LIFTING THINGS OUT OF CIVILIAN HULLS IS NOT STAGED AGAIN AND THE TENDER IS NOT ENTERED AND THE SLIP IS NOT SHOWN AGAIN AND THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-SIX IS NOT PUT BACK ON A LINE OF BOATS.** The only movement-three thing that is on the page in these ten days is the shape of the board, said once in a shed about a shape and not about a sheet.
9. **THE CISTERN'S THREE ROTA DAYS AND THE WALL'S ONE WIPE AND THE ONE WAGE TUESDAY WERE COUNTED OFF THE FACE OF CHAPTER 380 AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY BOOK, AND THE FIFTH STANDING COUNTERS WERE COUNTED THE SAME WAY.** The day-counts were corrected twice in the writing pass, once in a bellwright's figure and once in a bench figure, and both repairs are at `state/continuity.md` § 12 items 1 and 2.

### What the next volume inherits, in one place

**This is a hand-over from a batch and not a volume close, and it opens nothing that is not already open. It is owed eight things and nothing more.**

1. **THE CONDITION, PAID AS A BEGINNING, AND THE FIFTH THING, WHICH IS A PERSON AND IS NOT ON A LIST.** A company of boats is no use at all except in the water somebody is looking after between it and the next tide. Four things on a leaf that can be bought, and a fifth that cannot, and a master of about thirty-three who has been in company three times and had it go wrong twice for the same reason, and a caulker of about twenty-three who has been on a mole head stone at half past three every morning he cannot sleep for nine years. **The word is in no mouth, the stage is unwritten and named nowhere, and the last movement may not take it, may not name it, may not improve the Faultreader, Bellwright or Storm-Reader stages, may not enter an echo, surface a practice trace, or make a thing in the water answer a question.**
2. **THE CONVOY AS IT NOW STANDS, AND IT IS A FOOT.** Six masters of the third lay were asked one at a time on the eleventh of August; five said yes, one of them with a second half; one said no and gave a reason and was not asked twice. Five masters of a lay are five boats. There is a paper with no name and no figure on it in that shed's own keeping, and it is not a crew and not a muster and not the beginning of one, and the third lay fills on the first of April and one berth is short. **The man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers, who used the sixth clause twice on his own account and was not thanked, is available to the last movement and may be used and must not be used as a hero.**
3. **THE PATROL, THE TIMING, AND THE SENDING.** A small boat of about twelve tons, a lever of nineteen at her tiller, six masters put in one at a time on a papers question, six ticks in a list in a working man's own hand, and then the point on the thirteenth of August with two boats in her, gone down-coast. **The holder chose the day and knew it was the flood and said so in a shed with the door shut, and the transport on that reach is not named on any page and nobody in that harbor was told it was coming.**
4. **THE SENDING'S CONSEQUENCE, UNPAID.** The flour of a civilian transport did not arrive and no man died on the water in these ten days and the attack is not paid, is not softened, and was not foreshadowed in anybody's mouth. **The admission on a mole in about sixty people's hearing is the last movement's and is not softened here and is not to be softened in the last movement either.**
5. **THE SHAPE OF THE FORM, SAID ONCE IN A SHED ON THE THIRTEENTH ABOUT A SHAPE AND NOT ABOUT A SHEET, AND THE FOUR THINGS THAT CAME OFF THE WATER IN MOVEMENT 3 AND ARE NOT ON THE PAGE AGAIN.** A board with a word at the head of it, eleven marks in a column from the eighth of May to the twenty-second of July, two impressions at the foot of which he read neither, and a date cut into the timber being the fourteenth of February, ninety-two days before the notice went up. **No document of anybody's changed hands, no copy exists in that yard's keeping, and the slip of paper is in a drawer with a sheet in it and may never be named, headed, priced, invoiced or paid.**
6. **THE MONEY, WHICH CLOSED LOWER THAN IT OPENED.** Three hundred and thirty-six pence in on two days, two hundred and twelve pence out on two days, the bag at three hundred and twenty-eight pence, being two marks and eightpence, the figure short of a wage of four marks at three hundred and twelve pence, being one mark twelve shillings and eightpence, and the wage column unmoved on its forty-second Tuesday so that forty-two weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. **Not one of the seven standing debts is paid, reduced, advanced or improved, and no part of this batch's money came from the person who wanted the thing looked at.**
7. **THE STANDING FIGURES, ALL FIVE, AND THE NEW DAYS OF THEM, COUNTED OFF CHAPTER 390 AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANYBODY'S PROMPT.** THE NEXT SPAN IS SATURDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF AUGUST TO FRIDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD, BEING DAYS SIXTY-ONE TO SEVENTY OF THE NINETY, AND THE FORTY-THIRD WAGE TUESDAY IS TUESDAY THE SEVENTEENTH, WHICH IS THE FOURTH DAY OF THAT SPAN, AND THE NEXT WIPE AFTER THE SIXTY-SIXTH ON MONDAY THE NINTH IS THE SIXTY-SEVENTH ON MONDAY THE SIXTEENTH. **THE CISTERN'S NEXT ROTA DAYS INSIDE THAT SPAN ARE THE SEVENTY-THIRD ON MONDAY THE SIXTEENTH, THE SEVENTY-FOURTH ON THURSDAY THE NINETEENTH AND THE SEVENTY-FIFTH ON MONDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND, THE ROTA BEING A MONDAY AND A THURSDAY, AND NO CHARGE IS TO BE PLACED ON ANY OTHER DAY OF THAT SPAN.** The notice is at ninety-eight days on the twenty-third, the bellwright is not asked for one hundred days on the twenty-third, the two objects of nobody's are four hundred and thirty-eight days old on the twenty-third, and the bench under that pump is bare for the two hundred and fourth night on the twenty-third. **THE HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH LINE IS THE LAST LINE IN THAT LEDGER'S FOURTH COLUMN AND THE COLUMN IS NOT CLOSED, AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS EMPTY AND UNAPPOINTED WITH A BOY'S HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT AND HIS SURNAME ON NO PAGE.**
8. **THE FOUR NAMES AND FOUR HOLDS UNREACHED, THE PLATE NOT LOOKED AT AND ITS NOTE UNADVANCED, THE CHANDLER'S NOTE AT THIRTY-ONE, THE DELAYED NOTE AT ELEVEN AND TWO, THE FOUR RETURNS AND NO FIFTH, THE FIRST ECHO'S WITNESS, THE SECOND SEAM CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES, THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE WITH A STONE IN HIS OWN POCKET AND A PAGE ON A MOLE AND NO FIGURE, THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR AT A TILLER AND NOT AT A CAULKING IRON, THE FAR BENCH AND ITS ONE SHOE, AND THE CAN UPON A STAKE.**

**CARRIED FORWARD AND NAMED HERE SO THAT THE HAND-OVER STAYS AT EIGHT: the harbor's poverty, worse on the thirteenth of August than on the fourteenth of May; the municipal box on the west basin that is no longer empty and the other one that is and that a man of about fifty wants left empty; the sixth clause, which has now been used three times by this harbor, and once by a Crown convoy, and which has never once asked anybody anything; the one day lost on the first of July past with its reason and no name and no figure, and no second lost day entered against that line; the two-calendar fault, inherited, not noticed, not repaired, with ten weekday-and-date pairs on the page of this batch and zero mismatches against the house grid; and, carried by this batch rather than by its predecessor, the fact that a small boat of about twelve tons was seen on the eleventh of August to be at the other end of a tow of flour boats a mile off that harbor's point, which is a position and not a fact about anybody, and which nobody in that harbor recorded against anybody.**

### The flags, carried and not restated in a new place

### The eight threads handed in from the Volume 08 Batch 0004 hand-over, and where each of them moved

1. **THE CONDITION AND THE FIFTH THING, WHICH IS A PERSON AND IS NOT ON A LIST. **KEPT TO AND NOT NAMED, TWICE, IN THE HOUSE'S OWN TERMS, AND NOT IMPROVED ON. No chapter of these ten names the condition and no chapter enters it by naming it, and what is paid of it here is only that the holder would not take a company out on a day when the man whose day it is had not been asked for that day by name and paid for it. **THE CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE WAS ASKED FOR THE SEVENTEENTH BY NAME ON THE MONDAY, ASKED FOR THE TWENTY-FIRST BY NAME ON THE MONDAY AND THE TUESDAY, AGREED TO IT ON THE THURSDAY, AND PAID ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE STONE AT FOUR O'CLOCK ON EACH OF THE TWO DAYS OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES, AND THE FIGURE IS THE FIGURE IN CHALK ON THE SLATE AT THE END STALL AND NOT THAT YARD'S. HE WAS NOT ASKED FOR THE TWENTY-SECOND OR THE TWENTY-THIRD AND DID NOT OFFER, AND HE TOLD THAT YARD ON THE TWENTY-FIRST THAT HE WOULD NOT BE ON THE STONE ON THE SUNDAY AND THAT THE DAY HE IS NOT ASKED IS THE DAY THERE IS NOT ONE.** He was not paid twice, not put on a list, not put on a board, not thanked, and not called a man of any office. The four things that can be bought were said out loud in a boat on the twenty-first to about thirty men, and the fifth, which is a person, was said out loud with them and was off the sheet and off the leaf and off every board in that harbor. **A MOLE HEAD STONE WAS EMPTY AT FOUR IN THE MORNING ON THE NINETEENTH AND WENT IN NO COLUMN OF ANY LEDGER AND WAS TOLD TO NOBODY.**

### Threads opened by Batch 0005

- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE HINGE OF THE WHOLE THING — THE COST, WHICH IS A SHEET THAT STILL EXISTS AND IS NOT IN THAT HARBOR.** A man of about thirty-one with a satchel and a board under his arm left a boat's boat at about ten knots at about twenty past ten on the twenty-first of August and went up the reach, and he was not stopped and was not asked where he was going and was not thanked, and he is not mentioned again in a room by anybody in this series, **AND THE COST IS THAT NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR'S SHED HAS THE FORM AND NEVER WILL HAVE IT UNLESS SOMEBODY ELSE DOES SOMETHING.** It is in the second column of Chapter 399 and in the second column of Chapter 400 and it is not in the first column of either, because a stranger with a leaf and a pencil cannot check what a man did not do. **IT MAY NOT BE CONVERTED INTO A RECOVERY, A RETURN, A CONFESSION OR A VICTORY BY A LATER VOLUME, AND IT MAY NOT BE DESCRIBED AS A DEFEAT EITHER.**
- **OPEN — A SQUADRON WITHOUT A SHIP, AND A MAN WHO WENT UP-COAST IN A BOAT'S BOAT WITH A BOARD UNDER HIS ARM.** A ship of about sixty tons with the squadron's own boats in company went up that coast in the night of the twenty-first and the small boat of about twelve tons went in front of her, and neither has been on that reach since, and the work on that reach stopped at about eleven and did not start again that day. **SOREN VEY'S FLAGSHIP AND HIS COMMAND ARE LOST, HE IS IN NO ROOM AND ON NO MOLE AND IN NO MARKET AND IN NO MOUTH, HIS NAME IS ON THE FACE OF ONE INSTRUMENT IN MOVEMENT 1 AND ON NO OTHER PAPER IN THAT HARBOR, AND THE ONLY MAN WHO SAID ANYTHING ABOUT IT WAS A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A SCREW-STEAM PACKET OUT OF BRAMBLE STAIR WHO WAS ON THE REACH AND SAID WHAT HE SAW AND SAID HE WAS NOT HERE TO SAY WHAT IT MEANT AND WAS NOT THANKED.** It is not a lesson, not a fall, not a comedy, not a ducked man and not the comfort the volume gets out of it, and nobody in that harbor is to be pleased about it.
- **OPEN — THE NINE-LINE SHEET WITH A SEAL ON IT IN THE FRONT STREET SINCE THE FOURTEENTH OF AUGUST.** It proposes that every concern which takes work out of a hull and keeps no account of what it has taken be entered in one register, and that a concern not entered in that register is a concern whose accounts are not to be produced to anybody. **IT NAMES NO PERSON AND NO HARBOR AND PUTS NO FIGURE ON IT AND HAS NO PRICE AT THE END OF IT AND ASKS NOTHING OF ANYBODY STANDING IN THAT STREET, IT IS TRUE ENOUGH ON THE FACE OF IT THAT NOBODY WHO READS IT CAN GO UP THE STREET AND SAY IT IS A LIE, NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR PUT IT UP AND NOBODY HAS TAKEN IT DOWN AND NOBODY HAS ANSWERED IT, AND IT IS THE BEST PAPER THE CROWN PRODUCES IN THIS VOLUME AND IT IS THE ONE THAT OPENS VOLUME 09.** It was read twice at a quarter to four on the nineteenth and its reader said nothing at all about it out loud to the street and to nobody else. **IT IS ANSWERED BY NOBODY IN THESE FIFTY CHAPTERS AND IT MAY NOT BE ANSWERED BY BEING CALLED A LIE, AND IT IS NOT A NOTICE, AND IT IS NOT A THREAT, AND IT IS NOT A SHERIFF'S SUMMONS.**
- **OPEN — THE PAPER ON THE CUSTODY ROOM DOOR, AND THE SEAL LINE AT THE FOOT OF IT.** Two people permitted at an hour named, one person present in the room for the whole of it, a look at one thing out of three and not a taking, nothing out in any hand, an hour that is the end of it and not the middle of it, and a figure on that paper which is a time and a place and an arrival and **is the only figure in fifty chapters of that yard that is not a price anybody paid.** The third of the three is not on it and the claim on the third is not withdrawn and nobody has asked for it to be withdrawn. **THE ROOM IS NOT ENTERED IN CHAPTER 400 AND WAS NOT ENTERED ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH, NO DIGIT OF ANY OF ITS THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE, AND NOBODY WAS IN THAT ROOM WHEN THE HOLDER STOOD IN THE CORRIDOR.** At the foot of the paper: *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, Registrar of Recovered Accounts.* **THE OFFICE IS NAMED ONCE, IS IN NO MOUTH, IS NOT READ OUT, IS NOT EXPLAINED, IS NOT ON A WALL IN THAT HARBOR, IS NOT USED AGAIN IN THIS VOLUME, AND FROM VOLUME 09 ONWARD HE HOLDS IT, PER `outline/volume-08.md` § *Concrete resolution* item 4 AND § *Divergences* item 3, WHICH IS A PLANNING DECISION AND NOT A CANON CHANGE.**
- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S SEED AND IT IS NOT ANSWED — THE MUNICIPAL PAPER OF THE EIGHTEENTH OF JULY AND THE DOOR FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST.** It still names two boats and three men and a tide, nobody has written a day on it, and the door it names is still open with nobody at it. A herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own said no to a company of boats on the fourteenth and again on the eighteenth and was not thanked either time, and a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers used the sixth clause twice in that month on his own account and came on his own account to the foot of that mole and looked at a page and went away, and neither was shown to be in the wrong. **WHO LEFT THAT PAPER ON THAT TABLE IN THE ROOM IN VEYR IS STILL UNKNOWN, NOBODY HAS ASKED, THE MAN WHO KEEPS THAT ROOM WILL NOT BE ASKED FOR A NAME IN IT, AND THE SAYING SO IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND IS NOT A FIFTH PLACE. IT IS THE FIRST THING A VOLUME 09 INHERITS AND IT IS NOT ANSWERED BY ANYBODY'S PERSONALITY.**
- **OPEN — A QUESTION, ASKED ONCE, ANSWERED NOWHERE.** *If the Navy cannot own the sea by force, is the Crown going to try to own history by making it legally singular?* Asked out loud, once, by a man with no office, in a room with a clerk of about sixty in it, at about ten to six on Sunday the twenty-second of August, naming no person. The clerk's whole answer was that he has not got a book for it. **NO CHARACTER IN THESE FIFTY CHAPTERS ANSWERS IT, NOBODY PROPOSES ANYTHING IN ANSWER TO IT, NOBODY NAMES A CENTRAL BODY, A COMMITTEE, AN ASSEMBLY, A FLEET, A WING OR A GUARD, AND A DENIAL IS NOT AN INSTANCE. IT IS THE FIRST THING VOLUME 09 INHERITS AND IT IS NOT ANSWERED BY THE FORM AND NOT ANSWERED BY THE SEAL LINE AND NOT ANSWERED BY ANYTHING ELSE IN THIS VOLUME.**
- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE ONE THING A LATER VOLUME MAY NOT INHERIT AS A TASK — A COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP, BEGUN ONCE.** On the crown of that mole at about six on Sunday the twenty-second, in a few sentences, with the stone bare and neither of them saying one word about it. He is going to be told before and not after; she is not going to ask; if she does not like it that is what happens and she will not make a scene about it in the shed either. **It is not a marriage, the marriage is Volume 12's and is public, the work is not merged, she is not restored, forty marks first after food is neither reduced nor paid, neither of them is paid for the other, it is not the apology, she has not got the apology and is not asking for it, it is not a rescue and not a reward for a mole, nobody in that harbor is going to be told, and neither of them is going to be thanked for it.** The yard has entered it in no column and is not going to, and no word of it has been said twice.

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE PUBLIC ROOM IS A ROOM OVER THE FISH MARKET, LET OUT ON A SUNDAY TO ANYBODY WHO WANTS IT, THE MONEY IN A BOWL ON THE STEP, AND NO CLERK IN IT AND NO BOARD ON THE WALL OF IT AND NO LIST.** It was established on the page in Chapter 399 for one reason: the volume's whole argument is that a thing said in a shed in a town is a thing a man in a room can write down as a thing somebody said in a shed, and the eleven weeks and the shape had to be said in a room and in front of people and with no office behind the room. **THE ROOM WITH A CLERK IN IT, WHERE THE VOLUME'S NEW QUESTION WAS ASKED, IS A DIFFERENT ROOM, BEING THE OFFICE ON THE WEST BASIN, AND THE TWO ARE NOT CONFLATED ANYWHERE.**
2. **THE INQUIRY'S TERMS GIVE THE ACCESS AND THE ACCESS IS STAGED AS A PAPER ON A DOOR AND NOT AS AN INSTRUMENT HANDED OVER.** A man of about fifty in the office on the west basin refuses to hand the paper over on the ground that asking would be a request and a request is a claim, and gives its shape; the paper itself is on the door of the custody room and was put there by nobody this yard knows and was not taken down. **THE ROOM IS NOT ENTERED AND THE ACCESS IS A DOOR WITH A MAN STANDING AT IT AND NOT AN OPENING, AND THE HOUSE'S OWN SENTENCE IS USED ABOUT IT ONCE IN CHAPTER 400'S SECOND COLUMN.**
3. **THE ONE PERSON NAMED AS PRESENT ON THAT PAPER IS A WORKING MAN AND NOT A FACE OF ANYTHING, BEING SAUL DRURY, A COPYING CLERK OF THE CIRCUIT OFFICE, ABOUT FORTY, WHOM NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS SEEN.** He is not a witness, not a courier, not an antagonist, and is available to Volume 09. **NO OFFICER IN THIS VOLUME IS A FACE, AND NO MINISTER IS IN A ROOM, AND THE ONLY SEAL LINE THAT NAMES A NEW OFFICE IS AT THE LAST PAGE.**
4. **THE ADMISSION IS ONE SPEECH AND IT IS ONCE, AND IT NAMES FIVE THINGS IN THIS ORDER: the cost, the timing, the two foot, the four thousand seven hundred yards, and the harbor that is poorer.** **THE TWO FOOT AND THE FOUR THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED YARDS ARE BOTH PUT IN THE ADMISSION AND BOTH ARE REFUSED IN THE SAME BREATH AS EXPLANATIONS** — the first because it is nobody's arithmetic and he will not put it against the flour, and the second because a mole being long is a thing everybody knows and is not an answer to a boat's fore hatch. Neither is softened and neither is improved on afterwards by anybody, and the man of about thirty-six's one sentence on that mole is the only other thing said there and the holder agreed with it and added nothing.
5. **THE FIGURE OF FOUR THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED YARDS IS THE LENGTH OF THE SECOND SEAM OF THAT MOLE AND IT IS NEW TO THIS BATCH.** It comes off a board in the office on the west basin, it is a figure of a stone line and not a figure of water, and no man in that harbor has walked that seam this year. **IT IS A DIMENSION AND NOT A MEASUREMENT, IT MAY NOT BE TURNED INTO A READING, AND IT IS NOT ONE OF THE STANDING FIGURES.**
6. **THE THREE STATEMENTS ON THE MOLE HEAD ON THE LAST PAGE ARE THE VOLUME'S OWN THREE, BEING ABOUT THE WATER SAID BY THE SHIP'S HAND, ABOUT THE HARBOR SAID BY THE WOMAN OF NO OFFICE, AND ABOUT THAT YARD SAID BY THE HOLDER, AS AT CHAPTER 350.** They were chosen over an admission, because the admission is Chapter 399's and may not be improved on and may not be said twice, and because the last page of a volume in this house is a record and not a speech.
7. **THE READ-BACK WAS DONE ON THE MOLE HEAD AT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING AND NOT IN THE SHED AT FOUR, BECAUSE THE OUTLINE'S FIXED FINAL IMAGE PUTS THE MOLE HEAD, THE LIGHT OUT, THE READ-BACK AND THE CUSTODY ROOM DOOR ON ONE PAGE AND IN ONE HOUR, AND BECAUSE THE STONE IS WHERE THE FIFTH OF THOSE FOUR THINGS IS.** The stone was bare and no man had been asked for that day, and neither he nor she said one word about it.
8. **THE FOURTH COLUMN'S LINES ARE THE HUNDRED AND SIXTEENTH THROUGH THE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIFTH, ONE A DAY, NO DAY IN TWO OF THEM, AND THE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIFTH IS THE LAST LINE IN THAT LEDGER AND THE LAST LINE OF THE VOLUME AND THE COLUMN IS NOT CLOSED.**

### What the next volume inherits, in one place

**This is a hand-over from a batch and not a volume close, and it opens nothing that is not already open. It is owed eight things and nothing more.**

1. **THE CONDITION, PAID AS A BEGINNING AND NOT AS A STAGE, AND THE FIFTH THING, WHICH IS A PERSON AND IS NOT ON A LIST.** A company of boats is no use at all except in the water somebody is looking after between it and the next tide. Four things on a leaf that can be bought, and a fifth that cannot, and a caulker of about twenty-three who is on a day and a wage and an hour and on nothing else and who told that yard he would not be on the stone on the Sunday. **THE WORD IS IN NO MOUTH, THE STAGE IS UNWRITTEN AND NAMED NOWHERE, AND VOLUME 09 MAY TAKE IT AND MAY NAME IT AND THE FIRST WORD OF IT IS ITS OWN.**
2. **THE CONVOY, WHICH IS SEVEN BOATS AND A FOOT, AND A SHEET WITH EVERY MAN IN THEM ON IT, AND FOUR BLANK LINES.** About eleven masters asked in the same words across ten days, seven yes and four no with a reason each and no name against any of the four, and the cost of the four being a man's day and not a figure. Seven boats went out on a breach of the first clause on the twenty-first and came in on the sixth clause, and one man in one of them would not have his name written and his master wrote it, and one man who cannot read put a mark at the foot of it with a pencil that was not sharpened for it. **The man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers used the sixth clause twice in that month on his own account and was not thanked, and is available to Volume 09 and must not be used as a hero. The third lay fills on the first of April and one berth is short and is still short.**
3. **THE SHAPE OF THE FORM, READ ALOUD IN A PUBLIC ROOM ON THE TWENTY-SECOND IN THE ORDER THE ELEVEN DATES WERE SIGNED, WITH THE FORM'S OWN SHAPE READ AFTER THEM AND NOT BEFORE THEM.** The word, the two columns, the eleven marks, the two impressions neither read, and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber, being ninety-two days before the notice went up. **HE HAS NOT GOT THE FORM, HE HAS NO COPY, NO DOCUMENT OF ANYBODY'S CHANGES HANDS IN THAT HARBOR, THE SLIP OF PAPER IS IN A DRAWER AND IS NOT PRICED AND IS NOT HEADED, AND THE FAIR COPY IN THE ROOM OFF THAT MARKET IS NOT ENTERED AND NOT ASKED ABOUT.**
4. **THE COST, WHICH IS A SHEET THAT STILL EXISTS AND IS NOT IN THAT HARBOR, AND A SQUADRON THAT HAS LOST A SHIP, AND A MAN WHO WENT UP-COAST IN A BOAT'S BOAT WITH A BOARD UNDER HIS ARM.** Neither may be converted into a recovery or a defeat. **A LOSS OF FLOUR AND A LOSS OF TIME AND A THING DONE TO A HULL, WITH NOBODY HURT, NOBODY NAMED AND NOBODY COUNTED, AND NO CASUALTY FIGURE ON ANY PAGE.**
5. **THE CUSTODY ROOM AND THE PAPER ON ITS DOOR, AND THE SEAL LINE, AND THE NEW OFFICE.** Three things in it, no digit of any of the three numbers on any page, none returned and none asked for, and a look at one of them named for ten in the morning on Tuesday the twenty-fourth of August with a copying clerk of that office in the room for the whole of it. **The room was not entered, the third is not on the paper, the claim on the third is not withdrawn and no request for it has been made, and the only figure on that paper is a time and a place and an arrival and is the only figure in fifty chapters that is not a price anybody paid.** *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, Registrar of Recovered Accounts.* **Named once, in no mouth, not read out, not explained, not on a wall in that harbor, and from Volume 09 onward he holds it.**
6. **THE MONEY, WHICH CLOSED LOWER THAN IT OPENED.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence in on the eighteenth at a berth and three hundred and thirty-six pence out on the seventeenth and the twenty-first, being a day of a man of about twenty-three on each at the same figure out of that yard's own money, the bag at one hundred and sixty pence, being one mark, the figure short of a wage of four marks at four hundred and eighty pence, being three marks, and the wage column unmoved on its forty-third Tuesday so that forty-three weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. **The forty-fourth falls on Tuesday the twenty-fourth of August, which is the first day after this volume, and the harbor is poorer on the twenty-third of August than it was on the fourteenth of May, and not one of the seven standing debts is paid, reduced, advanced or improved.**
7. **THE STANDING FIGURES, ALL FIVE, AND THE THREE STANDING COUNTS, AND THE NEW DAYS OF THEM.** Two wipes in the ten days, three cistern charges walked on none, one wage Tuesday with the column unmoved, the notice at ninety-eight days, the bellwright not asked for one hundred days, the two objects of nobody's at four hundred and thirty-eight days, the bench bare for the two hundred and fourth night, the two lights unmoved in twenty-two days **— SUPERSEDED, THAT FIGURE IS ON NO PAGE AND THE CHAPTERS' LAST FIGURE FOR THAT RUN IS NINETEEN DAYS, ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 397, AND THE FIGURE A LATER PHASE CARRIES IS THE ONE AT THE HAND-OVER BELOW —**, and the ninety at seventy days with no seventy-first. **THE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIFTH LINE IS THE LAST LINE IN THAT LEDGER'S FOURTH COLUMN AND IS NOT CLOSED, AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS EMPTY AND UNAPPOINTED WITH A BOY'S HAND AT THE HEAD OF IT AND HIS SURNAME ON NO PAGE AND THE THREE NOTS OF THE EIGHTH OF JUNE PAST STANDING UNASKED FOR A SIXTH WEEK.**
8. **THE FOUR NAMES AND FOUR HOLDS UNREACHED, THE PLATE NOT LOOKED AT AND ITS NOTE UNADVANCED, THE CHANDLER'S NOTE AT THIRTY-ONE, THE DELAYED NOTE AT ELEVEN AND TWO, THE FOUR RETURNS AND NO FIFTH, THE FIRST ECHO'S WITNESS, THE SECOND SEAM CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES, THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE WITH A STONE IN HIS OWN POCKET AND A PAGE ON A MOLE AND NO FIGURE, THE FAR BENCH AND ITS ONE SHOE, AND THE CAN UPON A STAKE.**

**CARRIED FORWARD AND NAMED HERE SO THAT THE HAND-OVER STAYS AT EIGHT: the harbor's poverty, worse on the twenty-third of August than on the fourteenth of May, with no flour in that market and none coming this month; the municipal box on the west basin that is no longer empty and the other one that is and that a man of about fifty wants left empty; the sixth clause, which has now been used by that harbor three times in that month and once by seven boats at once, and which has never once asked anybody anything; the nine-line sheet with a seal on it in the front street since the fourteenth of August, which nobody put up and nobody has answered; the new-volume question, asked once in a room with a clerk in it on the twenty-second and answered nowhere; the municipal paper of the eighteenth of July with its door still open four days up that coast and nobody at it; and, carried by this batch rather than by its predecessor, the fact that a transport of about a hundred and forty tons went down that reach on the twenty-first with her fore hatch open, and that about half of what she had was in the water by one o'clock, and that no sack of it came ashore and no claim has been laid and nobody has been made whole and no figure of any person came ashore with her, and that the paper of her own company says nothing about the four hours between the half past ten and the one o'clock and that nobody in that harbor has asked for a copy of it.**

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE RETURN IS A MUNICIPAL RETURN AND NOT A YARD INSTRUMENT, AND THE COUNT GOES IN THE FIRST COLUMN BECAUSE A MAN ON A MOLE CAN COUNT LINES ON A SHEET WITH A PENCIL.** RULED. The first column is for things a stranger can check, the second is for things a stranger cannot, and neither changed its job because nine people in that harbor were waiting for a number.
2. **THE COUNT IS THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE, AND IT IS NOT A THOUSAND, AND NO CHAPTER SAYS A THOUSAND, AND THE VOLUME'S NAME IS NOT THE FIGURE.** RULED AND BINDING ON THE REST OF THE VOLUME.
3. **THE COUNTING MAN IS NAMED ON THE PAGE, IN THE FRONT STREET, ON A DAY HE NAMED IN ADVANCE, AND HIS NAME IS NOT PUT AGAINST THE FIGURE IN THE LEDGER.** RULED. He named himself to the holder of that writ and not to a clerk in an office, and a ledger is not a list.
4. **THE COST OF THE HOUR IS A FIGURE OF HOURS AND NOT A FIGURE OF MONEY, AND IT IS SEVEN, AND IT IS THAT OFFICE'S FIGURE AND NOT THE TRUTH.** RULED. A bench in a building works at a rate, and a bellwright who comes down off a western reef line in a later movement works at her own rate, and the house does not bind the next movement's arithmetic.
5. **THE SEAL LINE ON THE FIRST PAPER IS DESCRIBED AND NOT REPRODUCED, AND THE OFFICE AT THE END OF IT IS NOT READ OUT IN A MOUTH IN MOVEMENT 1.** RULED. The naming of that office in a mouth is said once, by a working man reading the foot of a paper out loud in a room, in the last movement, and it is not this batch's.
6. **THE FOURTH COLUMN TAKES NO LINE IN THIS VOLUME AND THE REASON IS ENTERED ONCE IN THE SECOND COLUMN, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH CARRIES AN ITALIC FOURTH-COLUMN LINE AT ALL.** RULED AND CHECKABLE, the count of that line across the ten chapters being zero.
7. **THE AFTERTASTE IS TOLD OUT OF TWO BODIES AND NOT OUT OF A PAPER, AND THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT MATCHED AND ARE NOT GOING TO BE MATCHED IN THIS MOVEMENT.** RULED. It is a real bodily thing this book has been carrying since a bell went down over a wreck in June, and about a third of what came off that wreck came off a wreck, and neither of those two facts is a name for what is on the shelf in that room.
8. **THE HOUSE'S OWN SENTENCE IS SAID EXACTLY ONCE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, IN A COPYING CLERK'S OWN HAND, AT THE FOOT OF A PIECE OF PAPER, ABOUT SEVEN HOURS AND ONE HOUR, AND NOBODY REMARKS ON IT.** RULED AND BINDING.
9. **THE PROHIBITION IS KEPT BY SAYING WHAT DID HAPPEN, AND THE DECLARATION-OF-ABSENCE FORM IS THE HOUSE'S OWN FAULT AND WAS CUT FROM FOUR PLACES IN THE WRITING PASS.** RULED. **AND THE COUNT OF THAT FORM ACROSS THE TEN CHAPTERS WAS NOT ZERO WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN AND IS ZERO NOW: THE SAME THREE-ITEM CATEGORY ENUMERATION STOOD IN THE SECOND BOLD BLOCK OF ALL TEN DAILY APPARATUS BLOCKS, WHERE THE WRITING PASS HAD NOT LOOKED, AND ALL TEN HAVE BEEN REPLACED WITH WHAT THE MAN OF SIXTY-ONE DID ON THAT DAY.** A SWEEP THAT reads bodies and one ledger column is not a sweep.
10. **A SWEEP FOR THE TERMS THE HOUSE NAMES BY NAME IS NOT A SWEEP, AND THE WIDENED SWEEP FOUND FOUR INSTANCES IN TEN CHAPTERS THAT THE TWELVE-TERM SWEEP DID NOT NAME, AND SIX WRONG WEEKDAYS AND ONE IMPOSSIBLE PIECE OF INTERNAL ARITHMETIC WERE FOUND BY COUNTING RATHER THAN BY SWEEPING.** RULED AND BINDING ON EVERY LATER BATCH. ### Threads opened by Batch 0002

1. **THE PUBLIC BOOK, THE ROOM IT IS IN, AND THE THIRTY-ONE HEADS.** A bound volume begun on the twentieth of April past, on a long table in a room over a joiner's shop at the top of Fish Street, which is let out on a Sunday and is shut on a week day and has no board on its wall and no list and no name over its door. Its head is five lines and the second of those five has been rubbed at the end for about forty years of an elbow on a table, and the man who keeps the room gave his reason for not saying why, being that the first year is not this year and is not his telling. Four lines go under every head. **Thirty heads on the third of September and thirty-one on the twelfth, and thirty of the thirty-one carry four lines and one carries three.** Twenty-two of the thirty are pieces of glass out of wrecks. Three are a lamp, a door plate and a box of tally sticks. One is a whole bell with a man paid a shilling a week to wipe it, and that is the only wage in the whole volume on that page. Four are two doors off a house, a barometer off a chandler's counter, a hatch cover off a fishing boat and a looking-glass off a lodging house. The nineteenth is two boats of a man of about forty-four who said no on the seventh of June. The thirty-first is the figure of lamp oil, refused in a room in front of about twenty people and entered at the same size as the rest. **A later movement may add to that book and may not reduce it, may not strike a line out of it, may not put that yard's own figures, its four columns or its method on it, and may not put the count of three hundred and ninety-one on it or on any wall in Morrow Quay.**
2. **THE TWENTY-SECOND HEAD, THE DASH, AND THE FINDING.** A panel of worked glass about eleven inches by eight out of a hull landed at the third lay on the fourth of June past, on shelf four in a store on the second lay where no keeper is paid, with a note of four lines pinned to the lid since that day, signed with a name and not an office, and with a person in it about four inches high standing a little way inside a door. Its head carries three lines and the third ends in a dash. **The finding is four lines in pencil on the inside of the back cover of that volume, in the hand of a man of about thirty-one who writes figures on a slate for a buyer at a fish stall and has done for nine years, dated the twelfth of September, saying that of thirty-one heads thirty carry four lines and one carries three and that the head of the book says four, and that it is the twenty-second, and that it was found with a pencil on his own hand.** **The omission is not anybody's hand and is anybody's fault, and it is checkable, and it is not to be repaired, and it is not to be taken off that page, and no later movement may put a name against the dash or name the man who left it. The man who found it said out loud that he was not in that room on the eighteenth of June and is not going to say who was, and four people stood in that room while he said it and not one of the four put the question to him. The finding costs nothing to make and it cannot be un-made.**
3. **THE FOUR LINES ON THE DOOR, THE ELEVEN, AND THE TWENTIETH OF SEPTEMBER.** A paper about the length of an arm at the top left of that door, a drawing-pin under a fold of oiled paper, up since the thirty-first of August past, saying that a lamp of about four inches was found burning in that room on the night of the nineteenth of August at eleven and there was nothing in the room with it; that on the days following eleven people of that harbor were asked one at a time whether they had been in that room on that night; that one of the eleven was; that the person who found the lamp will not say which and has been asked by two persons of that street to say and has not said; and that anybody found to have been in that room on that night is to take himself, or herself, off out of that harbor before the twentieth of September next. Put up by a man of about forty-one who is the night man at the fish market steps, who has the eleven written down in his own hand in his coat in the order he asked them in, who has shown them to nobody and has not destroyed them, and who has been asked twice to take it down and has not. **A mark in chalk about two inches across under it was made on the night of the fourth of September by a boy of about nineteen who had been told in a taproom that the paper was a lie, and that boy was never found and is not to be found. THE ELEVEN HAVE BEEN TOLD ONLY THAT THE PAPER IS THERE, BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX, ONE AT A TIME, IN DAYLIGHT, ON THE EIGHTH OF SEPTEMBER, AND THE REASON IS IN HIS OWN MOUTH AND IS HE HAD BEEN ON THE WRONG SIDE OF A PAPER HE COULD NOT READ AT NINE YEARS OLD IN THAT HARBOR AND HAS THIRTY-SEVEN YEARS OF NOT KNOWING, FORTY-SIX LESS NINE. NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR IS TO TELL ANY OF THE ELEVEN WHAT IS ON THAT PAPER, AND IT HAS BEEN ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND IS NOT TO BE ANSWERED BY ANYBODY IN THIS VOLUME, AND THE TWENTIETH OF SEPTEMBER IS MOVEMENT 3'S.**
4. **THE ELEVEN PEOPLE, AND THE COUNT, AND HOW IT WAS ARRIVED AT.** Six counted by a woman of about fifty-eight in her own trade on the Thursday the twenty-eighth of August, five counted by a man of about twenty-six on the quay on Monday the first of September, six and five is eleven. **A count of people and not a figure of money, not a constituency, not on a sheet, not named, and the day a yard writes down the names of the people who cannot read is the day that yard has a list.** The count was made for a reading and not for anything else, and the two people who counted were not asked to count anybody twice and did not, and none of the eleven was sent for.
5. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WHO READS IT, AND WHAT IT COSTS HIM, AND WHAT HE REFUSED AND WHY.** A net-mender of the third lay, forty-six, in that harbor since he was nine, who can read, who reads every head-note off that table on a Sunday and writes his own name and the hour at which he finished each head under it in his own hand on the day, and who is not paid for it, is not going to be paid for it and is not going to be thanked for it. What it costs: two hours and twenty minutes a Sunday, a shilling not earned, a bowl on a step that has to be made whether anybody is in the room or not, and a Sunday he does not mend nets. **What he refused, in his own mouth: to read the four lines off that door aloud in that room on a Sunday, because those eleven would never hear a head-note there again if they were sitting at that table waiting for the paper, and because he had been on the wrong side of a paper he could not read at nine years old in that harbor, with his mother reading it to him out loud in a kitchen, and has thirty-seven years of not knowing whether she made any of it up, and said that was a selfish reason and that he had not got a better one. A later movement may not soften the reason, may not improve it and may not make him a teacher, a door, a symbol or a man with a motive given to him by somebody else.**
6. **THE AFTERTASTE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FORTY-ONE WHO HAS IT.** A cold in the teeth since about three o'clock on the twelfth and a taste of iron like a nail and hands that have not been right since about three o'clock, in a man who is not a fanciful man, who has carried a barrow of shavings down that passage in the dark about four hundred times, who was not looking at the panel the whole time and said so, who could go out and lift a barrow of shavings, and who knows the number of his son's fingers. **And a man's own body not knowing which of two doors he came out of, so that he had to go back up and put his hand on the frame of the door at the top to find out.** It is not a fever and it is not a complaint and it is not glass and it is not an illness and it is not a contagion and it is nobody's fault. **It is not the same thing as the window with a board across the outside of it, and it is not the same thing as the tar and the hot iron and the woman counting in the dark, and it is not to be offered to the man or the woman of no office as an explanation of anything, and neither of them is to be asked what they make of it.**
7. **THE TWELVE-TERM SWEEP AND THE ADDING, NOT THE RE-READING, AND WHAT THIS BATCH FOUND BY COUNTING.** **THE HOUSE'S RULE IS THAT A SWEEP FOR THE TERMS THE HOUSE NAMES BY NAME IS NOT A SWEEP, AND IT IS NOW WIDENED A THIRD TIME AND RUN ON FOUR PLACES — BODIES, EVERY LEDGER COLUMN, THE DAILY APPARATUS BLOCK AND THE CLOSING BLOCK. THIS BATCH FOUND ELEVEN INSTANCES THAT A SIX-TERM SWEEP WOULD NOT HAVE FOUND, AND FIVE OF THE ELEVEN WERE WRONG MONEY GLOSSES, THREE WERE DAY-COUNTS, TWO WERE WEEKDAYS, AND ONE WAS A BATCH'S OWN CLOSING TOTAL WHOSE PRINTED EQUATION DID NOT EVALUATE WHILE THE DAY-BY-DAY CHAIN ON THE SAME PAGE WAS RIGHT. A TWELFTH WAS A COUNTED FIGURE THAT COULD NOT BE TRUE, BEING A HUNDRED AND FORTY WRITES OF A PAGE BY THE SIXTH OF SEPTEMBER, WHICH IS A HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE DAYS AFTER THE BOOK WAS OPENED. EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS FOUND BY ADDING UP AND NOT BY RE-READING, AND THE RULE FOR THE NEXT BATCH IS: ADD EVERY DAY, ADD EVERY MONEY LINE, ADD EVERY HEAD, AND READ ONCE.**
8. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR WHO WAS IN THAT ROOM IN JUNE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-ONE WHO PUT A PAPER ON THAT DOOR, AND WHAT WAS SAID BETWEEN THEM.** A man of about thirty-four was in that room when the man of about forty-four's no was entered in June and did not know there was a no in it, and Hobb Lee told him in a room with about twenty people in it, and he went down the stairs. On the seventh of September he came up a second time and asked Hobb Lee to read the door paper aloud in that room on a Sunday, and was refused in Hobb Lee's own mouth. On the Wednesday the eighth of September he came up a third time and asked whether anybody had answered that paper, and was told no, and was then told, after the man who put the paper up had been told, that two people in that harbor had been in that room on Sundays and had gone away and told nobody, and that a man who has been twice to a room and told nobody is not in a position to go into a taproom and say a paper on a door is a lie. He went down the stairs and said one word and has not been up them since. **Neither of those two men is a villain and neither is a face and neither is an office, and no character may say that the paper on that door was put up for a reason that either of them has stated, and neither of them is to be made into the thing that caused it.**

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE ARCHIVE IS A TABLE, A BOOK AND A ROOM AND NOT A BUILDING, AND IT DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM, BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT SIGN IT, HAS NO BOARD ON ITS WALL, NO LIST AND NO NAME OVER ITS DOOR, AND KEEPS NO LIST OF WHO CAME IN.** RULED. The man who lets the room out takes the money in a bowl on the step at two o'clock and carries it in at six and has never written one of the people who came up that stair down, and gave the reason in his own mouth, being that a list in a room anybody can pay half a penny to walk into is a list of everybody in that harbor who could not afford half a penny.
2. **THE ROOM IS LET OUT ON A SUNDAY AND THE TEN DAYS OF MOVEMENT 2 CONTAIN TWO OF THOSE, BEING THE FIFTH AND THE TWELFTH, AND THE READING AND THE PANEL AND THE FINDING ALL HAPPEN IN THEM.** RULED AND BINDING ON MOVEMENT 3'S OWN ROOM BOOKING, IF IT BOOKS ONE. The whole of the movement's argument is paid inside two afternoons in a room that anybody may walk into for a penny.
3. **LOCK L25 IS SATISFIED BY NAMING THE READER AND THE HOUR ON THE FACE OF THE PAGE, AND IT IS SATISFIED IN EVERY ONE OF THE THREE READINGS ON THE PAGE, INCLUDING THE READING OF A REFUSAL.** RULED. The name and the hour go under the head in the reader's own hand on the day, and a person who cannot read cannot afterwards prove what was said to them, and that is the whole of why it is written there.
4. **THE BOOK IS WRONG ON ITS OWN FACE BY AN OMISSION AND NOT BY A LIE, AND THE OMISSION IS CHECKABLE BY COUNTING HEADS AND COUNTING LINES UNDER THEM, AND NOBODY HAS TO BE A CONSERVATOR OR AN OFFICER TO FIND IT.** RULED AND BINDING. A dash is true and a dash is a hole, and the finding is arithmetic and not an opinion, and the finding is made by a working man on his own hand in about four minutes.
5. **THE FINDING IS NOT ASKED WHO PUT IT THERE AND THE PERSON WHO MAKES IT IS NOT TOLD, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DELIBERATELY DID NOT COUNT IT HIMSELF AND SAID SO OUT LOUD, WITH A PENCIL PUT DOWN TWO INCHES FROM HIS OWN LEDGER.** RULED. A man with a stake is not a count and is a complaint with a number at the end of it, and the holder of that writ would rather have a finding he did not arrange than a count he owns. **THE FIGURE OF THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE AND THE FIGURE OF THAT VOLUME'S HEADS ARE BOTH STRANGER-CHECKABLE AND ARE BOTH ENTRUSTED TO STRANGERS FOR THE SAME REASON, AND A YARD THAT COUNTS ITS OWN GRIEVANCES IS A YARD WITH A SHEET.**
6. **THE PANEL NELL CARROW MADE AND THE PANEL OUT OF THE HULL ARE TWO DIFFERENT PANELS AND ARE NOT MERGED, AND THE ONE SHE MADE IS NOT ENTERED IN THAT VOLUME.** RULED. The book is a book of what that harbor recovered and a thing a person made with her own hands at about nineteen is not recovered, and the man who keeps the room told her so in one sentence and did not change the book for her.
7. **NELL CARROW IS ASKED ONE THING, ONCE, BY A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX ON THE NINTH, AND SHE ASKS HIM ONE BACK, AND THE VOLUME DOES NOT ASK HER A SECOND THING AND DOES NOT THANK HER AND DOES NOT MAKE HER A SYMBOL.** RULED AND BINDING ON MOVEMENT 3, WHICH OWES HER BEING PUT OUT OF A ROOM SHE HAS HAD FOR ELEVEN YEARS. She said out loud that if anybody in that room says a kind thing to her she will walk out, and the man who reads told about twenty people on the Thursday that she had said so on the Thursday and would not soften it. **NOBODY HAS THANKED HER AND NOBODY IS TO, AND HER ROOM ON THE THIRD LAY, AT NINE MARKS A YEAR, IS STILL HERS AND IS NOT HER GETTING ANYTHING BACK.**
8. **WHAT CAME OFF THE PANEL IS AFTERTASTE AND IS TOLD OUT OF A MOUTH AND NOT OUT OF A PAPER, AND THE PANIC IS PAID WITH A REAL WITNESS AND A REAL CONSEQUENCE AND IS NOT FAKED, NOT SOFTENED, NOT EXPLAINED AWAY AND NOT A PLOT DEVICE.** RULED. It is a cold in the teeth and a taste of iron and a man's own body not knowing which of two doors it came out of, in a room of about twenty people of whom eleven could not read, and it has not gone in anybody on any of these ten pages, and the woman of about sixty-one is not made whole and nobody is charged and the room empties without a sound anybody in that street heard.
9. **THE HOUSE'S OWN SENTENCE IS SAID EXACTLY ONCE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND IS ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE, BEING A FIGURE READ OUT IN A ROOM, IN A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE'S OWN MOUTH AT THE BOTTOM OF A STAIR, AND NOBODY REMARKS ON IT.** RULED AND BINDING. It is not said about the seven and the one, and it is not said about the two halves of what came off the thing on the hill, and nobody remarks on how often it has been said.
10. **THE PROHIBITION IS KEPT BY SAYING WHAT DID HAPPEN AND NOT BY PRINTING A LIST OF WHAT DID NOT, AND THIS BATCH'S DAILY APPARATUS CARRIES A NEW SENTENCE ON A STANDING FIGURE THAT NO EARLIER BATCH'S DID: THE THIRD COLUMN'S OPEN LINE OF THE THREE NOTS OF THE EIGHTH OF JUNE, A TENTH WEEK, PRINTED ON ALL TEN DAYS AND ENTERED ON NONE.** RULED. It is a way of keeping a prohibition without a declaration of absence, and a later batch is to print it the same way or not at all.

### Threads opened by Batch 0003

1. **THE SIX-LINE SHEET ON THE WALL AT THE BACK OF THAT END STALL, AND THE FIGURE IT IS PUT UP ON THE OUTSIDE OF.** A printed sheet of six lines with a date at the head and a charge at the foot, naming no person and no town and no office, put up on the fifteenth of September past on the outside of a slate carrying a figure of four hundred and fifty pence with the first of June against it and three hundred and seventy-eight pence standing visible above it with the first of February against it, **and that figure was not taken down first and cannot be taken off again.** The first line is true and is what came off a panel in a room; the second says it is not a fever and not a disease and will sit in a market the same as it sits in a room; the third says every person who has been in a room with such a piece is to be entered in the claim book at the counter of the harbor authority of the town where he stands; the fourth says a book is not a court; the fifth says no person and no town is named and that it is put up on the outside of this figure; and the sixth gives the charge for lodging one claim as one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, and says a claim so lodged is read out in the room where the public book of that town is kept, on a Sunday, by a man at the end of the table, and that a man who cannot read may be there and hear it. **A later movement may not knock it down, may not take it off that wall, may not name the man who printed it, may not answer it, may not move the oil figure, and may not print the date at the head of it out loud beside anything.**
2. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OFF THE SCREW-STEAM PACKET OUT OF BRAMBLE STRAIT, AND THE GANGWAY, AND THE REST OF THE SACK.** He is not of this harbor, is not an officer, does not belong to anything, was not asked a question and was not thanked, and is not the man who sent it. He was given the lot at the top of a gangway by a man behind a counter with a book open who did not ask his name and did not ask what it was for; he read the first four lines four hundred miles away and cannot put them down; he could not say it was a lie; and he went out on the evening tide on the fifteenth and is not coming back to that harbor this month. **The rest of the lot is standing against the back boards of the end stall at the end of that market with a stone on it and has not been opened, and nobody in that yard is going to open it for him.**
3. **THE CLAIM PAPER ON THE COUNTER OF THE OFFICE OFF THE WEST BASIN, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WITH TWO PAPERS ON A TABLE, AND THE BOX HE WANTS LEFT EMPTY.** Four lines, dated the seventeenth, no name on it, no seal at the foot of it, no office at the end of anything, saying that a claim has been entered under the sheet, that a person who has been in a room with a piece of worked glass with a scene in it is to be entered in the claim book of that harbor under his own name, and that until he has been entered a claim window held by him is held, and that a claim window is not ownership and expires on the day it says it does. **The box is still empty and something is still to go into it in this volume against his wish, and nobody in that yard is to ask him about either.**
4. **EMMET SLADE, OF ABOUT THIRTY, OF THE THIRD LAY, WHO CANNOT READ, AND THE WORD *OFF*.** A boat of about nine tons, a claim window on a wreck off the point, and a sheet with his name at the top of it under the sheet of the seventeenth. He was told at a counter on the eighteenth that the word on it is off, and said that off is a different word to held, and was told that off is the word that is on the paper and that he was not going to be given another one. He was told by a boy on the twenty-first that it is stopped and that he is to hand in a third of anything landed, and he said out loud there is no third of anything, and that he has now got it twice and both times a bit different, and he went home and did not take his boat out. **HIS WINDOW HAS NOT BEEN REINSTATED AND IS NOT TO BE BY ANYBODY OUTSIDE THAT OFFICE, AND THE HELD WORD IS *OFF* AND NOT *HELD*, AND THE PAPER ON THAT COUNTER HAS NOT BEEN READ TO HIM BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR AND IS NOT TO BE READ TO HIM BY ANY PERSON OF THAT YARD.**
5. **DILL CARDEW, A BOY OF ABOUT SEVENTEEN, AND THE HOUR HE CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR.** He lost a message in a street on the fourteenth and stood on a step for about twenty-five minutes, and on the twenty-first he was the boy who carried the word to a man who cannot read. **Nobody in that harbor has asked him where he was on the fourteenth and nobody in that yard is going to, and the reason is in his own head and not in anybody's mouth: a boy who cannot account for an hour is a boy who does not get sent anywhere again.**
6. **NATE PRY, OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR, AND THE CHANDLER'S COUNTER, AND THE GIRL OF ELEVEN.** Eight fathoms of tarred rope at four shillings, being forty-eight pence, refused on the seventeenth by a chandler of about fifty whose wife keeps the count, and the reason is in the chandler's own mouth and it is not cowardice and it is not malice and it does not improve: he is not going to stand in his shop and ask a man whether he has been in a room with a piece of glass, and he has a wife and a girl of eleven behind that counter. **There is no other rope seller in that harbor, the rope went back onto his own shoulder and lay in the bottom of his boat until the middle of October, and his seine was still open where it had been open since June.**
7. **RUBEN PRIEST, OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT, WHO TAKES THE RENTS IN TWO HOUSES ON THE THIRD LAY, AND WHAT HE ASKED AND DID NOT ASK.** He put a woman of about sixty-one out of a room she has had for eleven years and he asked her nothing, and gave the reason in his own mouth, and said he had no other room and was not going to look for one for her because a room found for her now would be a room somebody stood at in a month asking why she was in it. **He is not a villain and is not a face and is not to be made into the thing that caused it, and no character may say the paper on a wall in the front street was put up for a reason he has stated.**
8. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WITH A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTEEN TONS AND NO PAPERS, AND THE BERTH, AND THE HARD AT THE BACK OF THAT LAY.** The berth was held on the eighteenth by a sheet tied to the peg with a piece of line and dated the seventeenth, and he said the sixth clause lets me in and does not give me a berth, and he put her on the hard for three hours with about four other boats and took a cup of tea off somebody else's stove, and he went out on the sixth clause that evening and came in past the outer marks at about five the next morning and the paper was off the peg and the peg was still there. **He is not on the sixth clause's books, he has no papers and has never had any, and the sixth clause has not asked him anything.**

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE NOTICE IS THE CROWN'S AND IT IS ON A WALL IN THAT FRONT STREET AND IT IS NOT ANSWERED, AND IT IS THE OUTERMOST ANTAGONISM IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS: A SHEET, A DATE, A MECHANISM AND A CHARGE.** RULED AND BINDING ON MOVEMENTS 4 AND 5. Its first clause is true and is what came off a panel; its extension is false; it names no person and no town; it has a charge at the foot that is a day's work at a berth and that a poor man cannot pay; and it went up on the outside of a figure that was not taken down first and cannot be taken off again. **A later movement may not knock it down, may not name the man who printed it, and may not say out loud that one half of it is false and one half is true.**
2. **THE FALSE HALF IS CARRIED ON THE SHEET AND IS NOT ANSWERED BY ANY CHARACTER, AND THE TELL IS ON THE FACE OF THE SHEET AND NOT IN ANY MOUTH.** RULED. The tell that a stranger with a pencil can take is that the sheet's own sixth line says it is put up on the outside of a figure, and a stranger standing at that wall can see that it is. **The other tell is that the date at the head of it is the eighth of May, and the yard's own leaf carries eleven dates, and NO PAGE OF THIS VOLUME PUTS THE TWO TOGETHER AND NO CHARACTER PUTS THEM TOGETHER OUT LOUD.**
3. **THE REVERSAL IS PAID IN TWO HALVES AND NEITHER HALF IS THE ANSWER TO THE OTHER AND NO CHARACTER IS ALLOWED TO SAY THAT ONE IS.** RULED AND BINDING. The witness is real and the terror is real and it is aftertaste and not a disease and not glass and not an illness and it is told out of a mouth. The story that the glass itself is contagious is on a wall and is false, and the crisis came from a claim that was planted through a working man who was given a sack on a gangway. **The one place a mouth came closest to resolving it was a woman in a half circle in that market on the fifteenth who said she was in the room and that she was not going to say a thing she did not know, and that was written and the rest was cut, and the cutting is recorded at `state/continuity.md` § 12 ITEM 5.**
4. **THE AFTERTASTE REACHES ONE DIVER AND REACHES HIM AS A BODY.** RULED AND BINDING ON MOVEMENT 4. It is a cold in the teeth, a taste of iron like a nail, hands that are not right, and a man not knowing which of two hatches he came up out of. It is not a vision, not a reading, not a practice trace and not a faultreader use, and the Faultreader stage is not re-taken to produce it. **He tells two men on a berth and two people in a shed and a market, and there is no figure for it and he is not on a page.**
5. **THE CHARGE AT THE FOOT OF THE NOTICE IS THE FIGURE OF A DAY'S WORK AT A BERTH, AND THAT IS PRINTED IN THE SECOND COLUMN WITH THE SHIP'S OWN REASON, AND IT IS NOT SAID AGAIN ABOUT THE OIL FIGURE.** RULED. One hundred and sixty-eight pence for a claim, being the figure in chalk on a slate at an end stall. A man with nothing can put a sheet up on a wall and can pay a penny for a sheet of paper and cannot pay a mark and eightpence for a claim, and that is the first time in about a year that a figure has been written that a poor man cannot get at, and the man it is written for is not a man in that market.
6. **A BOY WHO LOSES A MESSAGE LOSES THE HOUR HE WAS GOING TO BE SOMEWHERE ELSE IN, AND A SECOND PAPER DOES NOT PUT IT BACK.** RULED AND BINDING ON LATER MOVEMENTS. A boy cannot say where he has been without saying what he was doing, and the only reason he was going was in his hand. **And that is why nobody in that harbor has asked him where he was on the fourteenth, and why the same boy carrying a word to a man who cannot read six days later is not a plant and is not a coincidence and is a trade.**
7. **A MAN WHO CANNOT READ THE PAPER ON HIS OWN CLAIM WINDOW IS TOLD ABOUT IT BY A BOY WHO WAS TOLD IN TURN, AND HE HEARS IT TWICE AND WRONG.** RULED AND BINDING. The first telling is at a counter and gives him the word that is on the paper, which is *off*, and he says that off is a different word to held and is told that off is the word that is on the paper. The second is from a boy and gives him *stopped* and a third of anything landed, and there is no third of anything. **THIS IS THE ONLY WAY ANY WORD OF THAT PAPER REACHES HIM AND IT IS A TELLING AND NOT A READING, AND LOCK L25 IS NOT SATISFIED BY IT AND IS NOT GOVERNING IT.**
8. **THE ROPEMAKER IS FOUND OUT BY A MOUTH AND NOT BY AN OFFICE, AND THAT IS THE VOLUME'S ARGUMENT AGAINST ITSELF ON THE FACE OF ONE CHAPTER.** RULED.
