6. **THE TENDER IS PAID BY A DIFFERENT OWNER FROM EVERY PERSON IN THE BOAT AND THAT IS WHY HE ALONE CAN STOP THE WORKING.** **RULED AND BINDING. NOT ONE PENNY OF HIS CAME OUT OF THAT BAG AND THERE IS NO FIGURE OF IT ON ANY SHEET IN THAT HARBOR.**
7. **A REASON FOR PUTTING A MAN INTO THE WATER IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE HE GOES DOWN AND NOT AFTER HE COMES UP.** **RULED AND BINDING ON EVERY SMALL SUPERVISED DIVE IN THE NEXT MOVEMENT. A RECORD THAT IMPROVES A MAN'S ACCOUNT OF HIS OWN HANDS IS NOT A RECORD, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT WHO SWEPT OUT THE FISH STREET ROOM WENT DOWN ON THE FIRST OF OCTOBER AND CAME UP AND SAID HE COULD NOT TELL ANYTHING AT ALL, AND THAT IS WHAT HE SAID AND IT IS IN THE BOOK AT THE LENGTH HE SAID IT.**
8. **LOWFEN AND TIDEWATCH WERE ENTERED AS WORK AND WERE NOT VISITED.** Ollum Trevask said how a heel is fitted in Lowfen and said he has never been there; Sedge Rundle said how he finds that channel and said he would not put a chart of that ground on paper because in ten years the reeds will have moved the point and the paper would be a lie with his name on it; Mina Kett brought about forty pieces of lead off a nail in a workshop door frame at Tidewatch and said they are not for this coast and are not to go on a wall. **RULED AND BINDING. NOBODY WENT TO EITHER PLACE, THE COUNT OF *VISIT* IS ZERO, AND NO FINAL ROUTE IS NAMED.**
9. **THE HOUSE'S OWN SENTENCE IS SAID ZERO TIMES IN ITS FULL FORM ACROSS THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND NOBODY REMARKS ON IT.** The woman of no office said once, on the second day of October, that what is hers and what is anybody's has to be written down and is not that yard's book, and that the four columns and the figure and the method do not go on the table in Fish Street or on any wall, and that her name does not go on a sheet and that forty marks first after food is not reduced by any of it. **THAT IS THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC BOUNDARY BEING DRAWN IN WORDS AND THE RULE ITSELF IS FOR THE ACCOUNT IN THE NEXT MOVEMENT TO PRINT ON ITS FACE.**
10. **THE BAG FELL INSTEAD OF RISING, AND THE TEN DAYS END WITH A YARD THAT HAS DONE FOUR DAYS OF WORK IN COMPANY AND IS FURTHER FROM THE WAGE THAN IT WAS.** **RULED AND BINDING. NO ITEM ON EITHER COST LIST IS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND THE NEXT MOVEMENT MAY NOT IMPROVE ANY OF THEM EITHER, AND THIS HARBOR IS POORER ON THE LAST PAGE OF THE VOLUME THAN IT IS ON THE PAGE IT IS READING NOW.**

### The eight threads handed in from Batch 0004, and where each of them moved

1. **THE WRECK, THE CONVOY, THE TIDE AND THE BANK FOUR HUNDRED YARDS DOWN THE FOUL. CARRIED AND CLOSED ON ITS OWN TERMS, AND NOBODY DIED.** A boat of about nineteen tons named the *Alewife*, of the third lay, lying in about nine foot of water with her port bilge up, a new piece on her keel and about eleven feet of caulked joint, was got off that bank at about half past two in the afternoon on Monday the fourth day of October, and a joint that has been wet once is not a joint yet and has to be wet twice and dry once between, which is about four days of tide whatever the weather does. **She came off upright, the new piece went into the water first, and about eleven feet of caulked joint went under together and held.** A chain weight came over a rail at about ten past three with an hour and a reason written against it. About thirty men and seven boats and a small steam tender of about forty tons were round her. Nobody was paid for the morning, a caulker who came out and looked at the joint was not paid for looking at it, nine men got a mast in in about forty minutes and were not paid for that either, and the owner of that boat said out loud that she had got off and that nobody had got her wetter. **She is alongside the stone at the head of the third lay at the close of the volume. A later phase may not lose her to a stroke of weather, may not float her off without a tide, and may not print a figure on her.**
2. **THE CONSENT, THE ONE NO, AND THE NINE WORDS. CARRIED UNCHANGED, AND THE NINE WORDS USED A FIFTH TIME ON A DIFFERENT BOOK.** Eleven masters, one at a time, in the same eleven sentences, with a name, an hour, a boat and a yes or a no on every line; ten yes and one no, and the no is Rowan Teel's and it is on the page with his hour against it and it stayed on the page through these ten days. **A later movement may not take that line out and may not let anybody take it out, and the nine words that refused four requests to strike a line out are not going to be softened into a longer refusal or a shorter one.** On the eighth of October a man of about forty-four put his own words against the fifth line of a public account and the account was not changed, and on the eleventh both were read out again in the same room at the same hour, and that account's head says the person who entered it does not get to strike a line out of it, which is the same nine words worked on a public sheet and is the closest thing in this volume to a rule being used twice.
3. **THE THREE COSTS, EACH WITH ITS FIGURE. CARRIED, NOT IMPROVED, AND ONE OF THEM MOVED ONTO A NEW OBJECT.** **Shared liability:** the bill of iron clamps and a plank of white oak four inches by nine and eleven feet long and roves and copper at one hundred and sixty-eight pence, not charged to the owner of any of the seven boats, who was not asked to pay it and did not offer — and who on the fourth of October stood in six inches of water at the end of that yard's own baulk for about an hour and ten minutes because he had said out loud on the Friday before that he was going to hold that baulk next time, and was not thanked, and did not ask, and the baulk was still on that run of hard water at dark and on the last day of the ten. **Material expense:** the bag went from one hundred and ninety-six pence at the open of these ten days to twenty-eight pence at the close, being one thousand six hundred and eighty pence in on ten days and one thousand eight hundred and forty-eight pence out in eleven payments on ten days, and it is short of the wage of four marks by six hundred and twelve pence, being three marks eleven shillings, and it was never not short of it. **No right to erase:** the nine words, four times in the last movement, and four words under the fifth line of a public account that the person who entered it cannot strike out. **NONE OF THE THREE MAY BE SUMMED INTO A VICTORY AND NONE MAY BE PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED.**
4. **THE BELLWRIGHT AND THE TWO PLACES. CARRIED, AND PAID ON THE LAST DAY OF THE VOLUME.** Mina Kett, of about thirty-four, of Tidewatch on the western reef line, was asked one question in a building on a hill on the fifth day of October and the question was whether she could cut a lead. **She cut a line about four inches long with nine notches in it, three of them deeper than the other six, in about thirty-five minutes, and she was not thanked for being in that room and she did not ask to be.** She left a place about the size of a thumb out of the line on purpose and gave the reason in her own mouth: a cut that carried a place where the pressure changed would be an opinion cut into a thing that would go on saying it for two hundred years. She was paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence in coin on the flat of the bench stone at about four in the afternoon on the twelfth day of October, asked for that day by name at about ten that morning, on no other day of the ten, **against her own five shillings, being sixty pence, which she named once out loud on the twenty-sixth day of September past and did not say again on any day of these ten.** **SHE WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION ABOUT THAT HARBOR'S OWN BELLWRIGHT AND DID NOT ASK HIM ONE EITHER, HIS HUNDRED AND FIFTIETH DAY FELL ON THE TWELFTH DAY OF OCTOBER, THE CHEST IS SHUT, THE EIGHT MARKS AND A DAY OF A BOAT HAVE NOT BEEN ARGUED, AND NO DIGIT OF ANYTHING HE EVER SAID IS ON A PAGE.** Lowfen was not entered in these ten days and neither was Tidewatch and neither place was visited by anybody and no final route was named and the word *network* is in no mouth.
5. **THE STAGE, THE WORD, AND THE THREE ACCOUNTS OF ABOUT TWO FOOT OF PLANK. 6. **THE FOUR COLUMNS, THE BAG, THE MONEY CHAIN, THE STANDING COUNTS AND THE THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE. CARRIED AND THE FIGURES ADVANCED BY THE RULE.** **The first column takes one entry against each of the ten days, the second takes five, the third takes none and is unappointed with the boy's hand at the head of it and his surname on no page, and the fourth takes no line and has no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it.** The bag went from one hundred and ninety-six pence to twenty-eight pence. **THE COUNT OF THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE WAS CARRIED, UNUSED, NOT RE-COUNTED, AND IS ON NO WALL, ON NO BOARD AND IN NO MOUTH IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND A LATER PHASE MAY STILL NOT PUT IT ON A WALL IN MORROW QUAY OR ON THE WALL OF THE ROOM OVER THE JOINER'S SHOP.**
7. **THE FOUR NAMES AND FOUR HOLDS UNREACHED, THE PLATE NOT LOOKED AT AND ITS NOTE UNADVANCED, THE CHANDLER'S NOTE AT THIRTY-ONE, THE DELAYED NOTE AT ELEVEN AND TWO, THE FIRST ECHO'S WITNESS, THE SECOND SEAL CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES, THE MAN UPON A STAKE, THE CUSTODY ROOM, AND THE FOURTH BOX. ALL CARRIED, TWO OF THEM PAID, NONE IMPROVED.** **THE COUNT OF *PLATE*, OF *COMPARTMENT* AND OF *MANIFEST* ACROSS THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS ZERO AFTER THE REPAIR PASS AND WAS TWO, TWO AND TWO BEFORE IT.** The chandler's note is at thirty-one and is not re-written. The delayed note is at eleven and two and the call is not named. The second seam is not looked at on any of the ten days. The far bench is occupied from ten until four on nine of the ten days and is not empty again until after four on the ninth, and the one shoe that is not his is on the floor beside it at four o'clock on the last day. **THE CUSTODY ROOM WAS ENTERED ONCE IN THESE TEN DAYS AND ONCE ONLY, AT TEN IN THE MORNING ON THE FIFTH OF OCTOBER, UNDER THE SECOND PAPER, WITH A COPYING CLERK IN IT THE WHOLE HOUR, AT ONE THING OUT OF THREE, AND THERE WERE FOUR PEOPLE IN IT WHEN THE PAPER NAMES THREE, AND NO DIGIT OF ANY OF ITS THREE NUMBERS IS ON ANY PAGE, THE THIRD OF THE THREE WAS NOT LOOKED AT AND WAS NOT NAMED, ITS MUNICIPAL CLAIM WAS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO REQUEST FOR IT WAS MADE BY ANYBODY, THE ORIGINAL WENT BACK UNDER THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOTHING WENT OUT OF THAT ROOM IN ANY HAND. THE FOURTH BOX IN AN OFFICE OFF THE WEST BASIN IS NOT EMPTY.**
8. **THE TWO FIGURES THAT WERE THE MOST LIKELY TO BE RE-USED AND WERE NOT, AND THE PROHIBITION FORMS.** The eighth of May past and the eleven dates were not put on any page of these ten chapters in any form, in a mouth or in an apparatus, and the six-line sheet was not read out in full again and nobody compared it with anything. The nine-line mark and the nine-line sheet were kept apart and were never put in one clause, one column or one room in any of the ten. **THE FAULT FORM WAS FOUND THREE TIMES, ALL THREE WERE REWRITTEN TO SAY WHAT HAPPENED, AND ITS COUNT IS ZERO.**

**CARRIED FORWARD AND NAMED HERE SO THAT THE HAND-OVER STAYS AT EIGHT: the harbor's poverty, worse on the twelfth day of October than on the third, with no flour in that market, no barley in that market since the middle of the month, no barrel of lamp oil in that harbor since the twenty-ninth day of August, the light out, the north berth out, the tide gang four men short, the hose dead until the spring, nineteen winters disputed and unpaid, the hard at Ashtide unanswered, and the cheapest thing in that harbor up six shillings on the first of June and not come back down; a claim entered in a book at a counter off the west basin against a made thing, not granted, not refused and not withdrawn; the eleven people on the paper in Fish Street, who have been told nothing further by anybody in that harbor; the sheet of thirteen lines from an earlier volume, which is on no page of these ten; and the plate in eleven feet, the compartment and the manifest, which are on no page of these ten and are not going to be on one.**

### Threads opened by Batch 0005

1. **THE PIECE OF WORKED LEAD ABOUT THE SIZE OF A MAN'S PALM, IN A DRAWER IN A BUILDING ON THAT HILL.** It carries a line about four inches long and nine notches, three of them deeper than the other six, an office's mark, a hand, a person of about thirty-four's own mark cut small and off to one side, and a place about the size of a thumb left out of it on purpose. **It carries no figure and no number of any kind, and a stranger with a pencil can hold it up and find that every one of those six things is true of the lead itself and not of anybody's word about it. IT IS A MADE THING AND NOT A TRANSCRIPT, IT IS STABLE, IT CARRIES A ROUTE AND NOT A SCENE, AND IT DID NOT COME DOWN THAT HILL.** A later phase may not have it come down that hill, may not put it in a boat, may not put it in a hand, may not put it on a wall in Morrow Quay, and may not say that it is a copy of the thing it was cut from.
2. **THE THUMB-SIZED PLACE LEFT OUT OF THE CUT, AND THE SEAM IN THE ORIGINAL.** The original has a place about three inches long where the pressure on one side is not the pressure on the other, and a bellwright could feel where it was through a cloth and said she could not tell anybody what it meant and that neither could anybody else who is not a fool, and that she was telling three people and a clerk in front of a bench that her cut was not going to carry it. **IT IS NOT ON THE CUT AND IT IS NOT SETTLED AND NOBODY SETTLED IT AND THE ACCOUNT SAYS IN ITS OWN WORDS THAT IT CANNOT.** A later phase may not carry that place in the cut, may not explain it, may not name who was on which side of it, and may not say which of the two witnesses the room came in for.
3. **THE ACCOUNT OF ABOUT FOUR FEET, IN A DESK AT A DOOR, WITH NINE BOUNDARIES ON ITS FACE.** What a thing is, what a thing is not, where it came from, what it does not show; the refusals on it at the same size; the line that may be answered in the room where it is read out, with a name and an hour, and that the person who entered it does not get to strike. **Its seventh boundary names a person who is alive and is not named, its eighth says two holds stand against two men in that harbor and are not given back by anything on that sheet, and its ninth is a charge of one hundred and sixty-eight pence on a wall that has not been paid.** A later phase may not add a line to it, may not take a line out of it, may not move it out of that desk, and may not enter it in the Fish Street volume, which is a bound volume of thirty-one heads and not a place to put anything.
4. **THE FOUR WORDS UNDER THE FIFTH LINE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR WHO WROTE THEM.** A route is a route if it is there twice and he had been on it once and there was nothing on the stone. **Both are printed, the account was not changed, both were read out again in the same room at the same stated hour on the eleventh, and a woman of about thirty-one stood up in that room at about half past three and said she had been asked to hold a piece in a room in that town in the summer before last and was not going to say anything else about it there, and nobody asked her a question and nobody asked her to say it again.** A later phase may not strike those four words, may not rule the challenge down, may not ask that woman a second question about a piece, and may not turn that room into a court with a net-mender at the head of it.
5. **THE SHEET OF ABOUT THREE FEET WITH FOUR HEADS ON IT, IN A ROOM OVER A FISH MARKET, AND THE CLAIM IT CARRIES.** Claims, refusals, restricted records, public correction; no route, panel or account is represented by anybody who has not asked to be represented; the refusals are on it and are not smaller than the rest; a community may withdraw from a route; the council turns. **And a claim entered in a book at a counter off the west basin on the seventh of October, not granted, not refused and not withdrawn, carried on that sheet at the size of the four heads and not discharged by it.** A later phase may not discharge that claim, may not reduce it, may not hold a meeting of anything, and may not add a fifth head.
6. **THE MINUTE, AND THE TWO QUESTIONS IN IT.** A minute is a document and a document says what happened. **It says that a question was asked at about twenty past twelve in the afternoon of the tenth of October in a room over a fish market, that nobody answered it, that three people began to and stopped, and that a man of about thirty-four said he did not know. It says that a second question was asked at about half past twelve in the afternoon by a man of about forty-four who crews in no boat and holds no office, and that no rule was written on that sheet about it, and that no office was made for it and no seal line was cut for it.** A later phase may not answer either question, may not re-ask either, and may not let a character say the word *singular* of a person.
7. **THE LINE RULED UNDER A HEAD IN THE FISH STREET VOLUME AND LEFT EMPTY, AND THE REASON AT THE FOOT OF THAT PAGE.** The head is *a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure against it.* **The reason is that there is nobody in that harbor the man at the end of that table can ask for that line, and that he is not going to write one and put a name against it, and that he left it ruled and empty so that anybody who comes in can see that there is a place on that page where nobody was asked.** A later phase may not fill that line, may not name a person against it, may not tell the man of about fifty-one on the crown of that mole that anybody wrote a line for him, and may not put a name beside it. **THIS IS A FIFTH AND LAST SMALLER-FORM LINE IN THE VOLUME AND A LATER PHASE MAY NOT ADD TO IT.**
8. **THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE, AND THE SIX-LINE SHEET ON THE OUTSIDE OF IT, READ ALOUD TWICE TO TWO MEN WHO CANNOT READ.** On the eleventh day of October a man of about thirty-three read the six printed lines twice to two men beside him and then read them the figure off the slate on the same square of wall, and the three of them stood there about a quarter of an hour, and the man said he could not say it was a lie and did not say it was not, and one of the two said he had a brother in a boat that went for pieces in April and said nothing else, and the other said nothing at all, and nobody took the sheet off that wall and nobody wrote on it and nobody answered it. **A later phase may not knock it down, take it off, answer it, reprint it, move the figure under it, name the man who put it up, or put anything beside it.**

### Author-level decisions taken in this batch

1. **THE COPY IS A CUT IN LEAD AND NOT A COPY ON PAPER, AND THE REASON IS THE TIME ON THE DOOR.** A copying clerk put a figure of seven on a door in September — a copy of that thing, marked with where it came from, is seven hours at that bench and a pair of hands — and gave the party one hour, and the second paper's whole argument is that one hour is one. **A bellwright's cut is not a bench copy: a line is not a scene, a line is the same line in a hundred years, and a scene is nine inches of somebody being afraid and cannot be cut with a knife without deciding what they were afraid of.** RULED AND BINDING ON THE CLOSE. **THE COPY IS STABLE, IT IS MADE THING AND NOT A TRANSCRIPT, IT CARRIES A ROUTE AND NOT A SCENE, AND THE COST OF THAT IS THE SEAM, WHICH IS NOT IN IT.**
2. **THE SEAM IS THE PRICE OF THE ROUTE AND IT IS NOT RESOLVED.** A bellwright could feel where the pressure changed through a cloth, said she could not tell anybody what it meant, and left a thumb-sized hole in the line rather than cut an opinion into a thing that would go on saying it for two hundred years. **A STRANGER WITH A PENCIL CAN SEE THAT THE PLACE WAS LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THE COPY SAYS ABOUT THE SEAM.** RULED AND BINDING.
3. **THERE ARE FOUR PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM WHEN THE PAPER NAMES THREE, AND IT IS ON THE FACE OF THE CHAPTER.** The clerk put a fourth stool at that bench and did not write the fourth one in his book, said so out loud, and said he would write the irregularity down in a different book at the end of the day and would not have written anything about her at all. **THE REASON IS THE CLERK'S OWN: THE DOOR CARRIES A FIGURE OF SEVEN HOURS AT THAT BENCH AND A PAIR OF HANDS, AND THE DOOR NAMES A PARTY AND DOES NOT SAY A HAND MAY NOT COME INTO THE ROOM.** RULED AND BINDING. **THE HOUR NAMED ON THE PAPER WAS THE END OF IT AND NOT THE MIDDLE OF IT AND THE ROOM WAS EMPTY AT ELEVEN.**
4. **THE BOUNDARIES ARE PRINTED ON THE FACE OF THE ACCOUNT AND NOT ON A SEPARATE PAPER.** A person who cannot read is going to be told that account by a man with it in his own hand, and if the limits of a thing are on a different piece of paper from the thing then the limits are the first thing that does not get read out. **THE SIXTH BOUNDARY, ABOUT THE MISSING CLAUSE ON THE TWENTY-SECOND HEAD, IS ON A PAGE OF ITS OWN BECAUSE A PERSON WHO CANNOT READ WILL BE TOLD IT BY A MAN WITH IT IN HIS OWN HAND AND A PAGE THAT CARRIES BOTH WILL GET THE OTHER ONE SHRUNK.** RULED AND BINDING.
5. **THE ROTATION IS FOUR NAMES AND A WEEK TURN, AND IT IS NOT AN OFFICE AND NOT A DEPUT AND THE FIGURE IN CHALK DOES NOT APPEAR ON IT.** Two of the four asked to be on it and were named; two asked for a turn from the sixth day of October and two from the tenth, and a person whose turn it is may be asked once and not twice. RULED AND BINDING.
6. **THE TITLE WAS SAID BY THE MAN WHOSE BOAT THAT YARD'S OWN BAULK HOLED.** A man of about fifty, of a boat of about twenty-two tons, eleven feet of caulked joint, a bill he was not charged for, an hour and ten minutes in six inches of water holding that yard's baulk, and no thanks for any of it. **HE SAID IT ONCE AND WROTE IT AT THE HEAD OF THE SHEET HIMSELF IN A HAND THAT IS NOT A CLERK'S HAND AND PUT THE PENCIL DOWN, AND THE TWO PEOPLE NEAREST HIM DID NOT TAKE IT UP.** RULED AND BINDING.
7. **THE SHEET HAD NO NAME AT THE HEAD OF IT FOR FORTY MINUTES AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO BE THE ONE TO WRITE ON IT.** A page with a name at the head of it is a page somebody has already decided the name of. RULED AND BINDING.
8. **A CONFESSION IS A THING A MAN SAYS AND NOT A THING A YARD KEEPS, AND THE REASON IS GIVEN IN A MOUTH.** Four sentences, no fifth, no log, no name of the man who put anything in his hand, no reason that makes them smaller, nothing written down, and the reason it is not written down is that what a man said once in a shed is not something that yard did and is not something that yard is going to write down, and that if it were written down then a person in that harbor would find out one afternoon what a man said in a shed. **NOBODY THANKED HIM AND NOBODY FORGIVED HIM AND THE THIRD COLUMN AND THE SECOND COLUMN OF THAT LEAF HAVE NOTHING IN THEM ABOUT IT.** RULED AND BINDING.
9. **A LINE CUT IN AN ACCOUNT IS NOT THE SAME AS A LINE STRUCK OUT OF A LEDGER, AND THE RULE IS THE SAME RULE.** A stranger with a leaf and a pencil can count that a man was in the water on the eighth of October and cannot count what a man can put a name to about the twenty-ninth of June, and a figure in the first column against that would be a lie in a book that has never had one in it. **RULED AND BINDING ON THE VOLUME CLOSE, WHICH MAY NOT PUT THE AFTERNOON OF THE TWENTY-NINTH OF JUNE INTO THE FIRST COLUMN.**
10. **THE BAG FELL AND THE HARBOR DID NOT RISE, AND THE FIGURE ON THE BOARD DID NOT COME DOWN.** Ten days, ten payments in and eleven out, one thousand six hundred and eighty pence in and one thousand eight hundred and forty-eight out, and a bag at twenty-eight pence, being two shillings and fourpence, against a wage of six hundred and forty pence, short by six hundred and twelve. **A HARBOR IS POORER ON THE TWELFTH DAY OF OCTOBER THAN ON THE THIRD, AND THAT IS THE STANDING CONDITION AND NOT A FINDING.**

### The day-counts to hand on, which run on one a day and nothing turns on a round figure

The notice of the seventeenth of May past is on its wall for one hundred and forty-eight days. The bellwright of that harbor has not been asked for one hundred and fifty days. The two objects of nobody's are four hundred and eighty-eight days old. The bench under that pump is bare for the two hundred and fifty-fourth night. Two lights off that point have not moved in seventy-two days. A man of about fifty-one has said nothing to anybody about a page of six names for ninety days. The six-line sheet at the back of that end stall is on that wall for the twenty-seventh day. The paper of four lines in Fish Street is on that door for the forty-second day. The nine-line sheet with a seal on it is in that front street for the fifty-ninth day. Fifty-one weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. The wall came down bare twice in the last ten days and the cistern was charged three times and walked on none of it, and the seven days that are not rota days are the third, fifth, sixth, eighth, ninth, tenth and twelfth days of October. **A WEEK COUNTER MAY NOT MOVE ON A DAY THAT IS NOT A WEEK, AND THE THIRTEENTH WEEK RAN FROM SUNDAY THE FOURTH OF OCTOBER TO SATURDAY THE TENTH, AND THE FOURTEENTH BEGAN ON SUNDAY THE ELEVENTH.**

Who is it that gets into the big Crown wrecks, asked at about half past twelve in the afternoon on the same day by a man of about forty-four who crews in nobody else's and holds no office, and no rule written about it, no office made for it, no seal line cut for it. **A later phase may not answer any of the four, may not re-ask any of them, and may not let a character say the word *singular* of a person.**
3. **THE TITLE, AND WHERE IT IS AND IS NOT. SAID ONCE, BY A WORKING MAN, ON THE DAY THE SHEET WAS WRITTEN, AND THE COUNT ACROSS THE FIFTY CHAPTERS IS ONE AND IT IS IN THAT MOUTH.** Said at about ten past eleven in the morning on the tenth day of October in a room over a fish market, by a man of about fifty whose boat of about twenty-two tons that yard's own baulk holed, who stood in six inches of water at the end of that baulk for about an hour and ten minutes and was not thanked, and who was not charged for the bill and did not offer. **He wrote it at the head of that sheet himself in a hand that is not a clerk's and put the pencil down, and the two people nearest him did not take it up, and nobody said it after him. NOBODY PROPOSED A BODY BEFORE THAT DAY AND NOBODY PROPOSED ONE AFTER IT EITHER, AND THE THING THAT FORMS HAS NO JURISDICTION, BINDS NOBODY WHO DID NOT SIGN IT, DECIDES NO CONTESTED CLAIM, SETTLES NOTHING, HAS NO HEAD, AND IS NOT THE BEGINNING OF A FLEET.**
4. **THE SIX ACCOUNTS IN THAT LEAF THAT DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. 5. **THE FIVE COSTS OF THE CLIMAX AND THE STANDING CONDITION BEHIND THEM, AND NONE OF THEM MAY BE SUMMED INTO A VICTORY.** The copy and the original in the building on that hill; a stated hour and a custodian of that office at a door; a claim in a book at a counter off the west basin that is not withdrawn; a name of a person of no office on a public sheet and on a sheet of four heads that nobody took off and nobody thanked; a diver's afternoon of the twenty-ninth of June that he can put a name to and nothing else, in the second column with the reason against the line; a ropemaker of about sixty-one who does not get her room back at any page of this volume; and a figure of four hundred and fifty pence on a board in a front street that did not come down. **The harbor is poorer on the twelfth day of October than on the third.**

1. **THE MACHINE, AND WHAT IT IS FOR. THE REVERSAL IS PAID IN CHAPTER 474 AND NOWHERE ELSE, AND IT IS PAID BY ITS OWN GEOMETRY, WEAR, MAKERS' MARKS AND DATE.** Fifteen frames in rows beyond the forty racks, about nine feet by four, bar and not rolled metal, corners cut and not welded, three rivets, two inches of silt banked on the north side and not the south; nine holes in each frame with a short length of newer metal in a collar and a nut, each about three weeks old and not three days, each with a bright ring round its base with silt lying in the top of it; a channel about the width of a hand between every two frames with a curved thing set into the floor, the shape of a cupped hand with a hole bored through the middle of the cup, worn deep at the rim and bright across the middle. **The same mark on every frame, a hammer and a square crossed with a chisel, cut and not stamped, and the same figure beside it, being six hundred and eleven, with no year cut on any of them and no name beside any of them. The frame is a great deal older than what stands on it and both facts are in the same place on the same afternoon.** It is a machine, it is not a monster, it is not a curse, it is not a god, it is not a tomb and it is not a ghost, and **no character in any of the fifty chapters of this volume may say that a machine took a memory because a machine wanted one.**
2. **THE THREE ACCOUNTS OF WHAT IT IS, AND THAT THEY DO NOT AGREE, AND THAT NONE OF THEM WAS ASKED TO SAY IT AGAIN AND THAT NOBODY VOTED.** A man of about fifty-one out of the coast town four days down: a machine for taking an account off a living person and standing one account up where nine used to be, built by people who had nine communities arguing about a disaster for two years and who wanted one version everybody could put a finger on, and wanting one thing is not wickedness, it is an answer, and it is a bad answer and it is still an answer. A woman of about thirty-one, **as the chapter now stands after the repair pass of 29 September 2026**: it does not matter in the least whose hands it was in; she counted the cups from the ladder and said out loud that the counting is on the face of that floor and that a man on a mole could have it off a plan, and that there is no sense in nine of them sitting on a deck being clever about an arithmetic that anybody can do; **what she is not going to write down is what the nine were for**, and she said out loud that the difference between a number and a reason is that the number costs nothing to keep; there are nine of them on the boat. The holder of that writ: the honest reading of the geometry is that it held nine accounts at a height where a man could walk round them; the frame is the old part and the fittings are the new part; and he will not write down which of the two readings he hopes for. **A later phase may look at the machine again, may not settle the three, may not have any of the three re-asked in the same words, and may not explain the machine again in a fourth chapter of the movement that opened it.**
3. **THE CUT, WHICH CANNOT BE UNDONE, AND THE PIECE THAT WILL NOT COME UP.** There is an older hole under each of the nine fittings. One fitting was cut at the neck on the tenth day of November because a hole under a fitting cannot be read while the fitting is on it. **The piece is about three inches of iron with a collar on it and it does not go through a round hatch in a bell-shaped chamber with a stove in it, and cutting it smaller would have left a piece nobody could ever read again, and the man who did the cutting said so out loud before he went and would not do it.** It is on that floor and is not coming up on this trip. **The holder of that writ said out loud in front of all nine of them that he had just taken the only state that floor will ever be in off it, and gave his reason, and the man who did the cutting said that a thing done for a reason is a thing somebody has to be answerable for and that what is lost is lost whether he was proud of the cutting or not. Nobody thanked either of them, nobody said the word brave to either of them, and no figure is set against either.**
4. **THE OLDEST THING ON THAT SHELF, AND THE FIVE THINGS SAID ABOUT IT.** Nine short lines joined at one point, each about an inch and a half, cut to the same depth with a graver, on the third plank from the head of about thirty feet of curving hull planking set into the north wall of a long hall on iron brackets, fastened with metal and not with glass, with no figure, no year and no name beside it. **And the five things a woman of thirty of no office said out loud on a deck before anybody could say them about her: it is a builder's mark and not a name; it was cut before any claim was laid over that ground; it is not a seal, being pressed and rimmed and put on by somebody saying out loud that they are answerable for it; it is not a limit of anybody's consent, no person put it there and no person can take it off; and it is not proof that anybody agreed to anything.** Nobody argued, nobody agreed, nobody thanked her, and **nobody in that boat compared it with anything, because there is a drawing of a mark in a book in a shed two days' sail off and a drawing is not a mark.**
5. **THE BUILT WAY, AND THE WALL WITH ONE DOORWAY IN IT.** A built thing about two fathoms off the bottom out from the mouth of that trench, about nine fathoms of water over it off a line, flat, about thirty feet wide where it is clearest, two kerbs, a gutter about a foot and a half wide down the middle running with the fall of the thing, the fall being to the west, silt banked against the west kerb and not the east one. **A man of about thirty-four says it is a way and not a wreck, made for things with wheels, with a gutter because a way without a gutter is a way that rots, and gives no year for it and does not give the name of the thing that made it.** At the far end of it, a built wall about fourteen feet high with one doorway about five feet six inches wide and six feet two high, being the only opening in about sixty feet of it. **The party stopped at that doorway on the eighth and did not go through it, and a later movement may go through it.**

### Opened by this batch, and owed

1. **THE CACHE, IN A CRATE, AND IT IS THE BEST EVIDENCE THIS PARTY HAS EVER HAD IN ITS HANDS, WHICH A WOMAN OF THIRTY-ONE SAID OUT LOUD ON THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER.** A second opening in a wall at the far end of that floor, about four foot wide and five foot high, past the last of the fifteen frames and not the doorway of the eleventh; behind it a room that was dry and had been dry a very long time, with a foot of level floor and racks in it. Four racks against the back wall and one long one down the side, the four alike and the long one not, **every shelf of every one of the five with a raised lip about two inches deep along the back of it.** The paper is brown and folded twice and stiff at the folds, with a parted string through two holes at the head of the fold, a head ruled on it, a column of figures ruled under the head, a short stroke of the same length beside every figure, a small cramped hand that is not a hand any man on that boat has seen before, **no name and no year on the face of it, and nothing on the face of it that anybody on that deck could read out as the name of anybody.** It went into a crate and matting and a lid on the seventeenth, the lid was battened and a line put round the whole of it, and **it is going into a crate and not into anybody's hand, and the day it is carried to that harbor by a man in a boat with a coat on his arm is the day it becomes something else. A later phase may not put that cache in a hand and may not settle that.**
2. **ONE DAMP PAGE IS NOT IN THAT CRATE AND IS ON NO SHEET.** Brown for about three inches across the whole width of the bottom edge and gone into the fibres; it will not sit flat and will not fold; **it was not cut.** A woman of thirty of no office named it out loud once, on the eighteenth, as the third thing off the second shelf of the rack against the back wall on the north side of that room, and said that the only way anybody will know where it is is if somebody on that boat remembers it. A man of about fifty-one said out loud that he has cut about four hundred pieces of paper in nineteen years and cut every one of them because the man who owned it was standing there telling him to, and that nobody on that boat owns a page out of that room including himself. **The man who keeps the leaf said no to putting it in the second column. It lies flat under a weight on a tarpaulin about two foot from where she stood on the twenty-second. A later phase may not put it in a crate whole, may not cut it, and may not put it on any sheet.**
3. **THE THREE ONE-THING ACCOUNTS OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF NOVEMBER, AND THAT THEY DO NOT AGREE, AND THAT THEY SETTLE NOTHING, AND THAT A STRANGER WITH A PENCIL CANNOT CHECK ANY PART OF THEM.** Three people were asked one at a time, not in front of each other, for one thing each that they could carry, out of a sentence written at the head of a page on the fifteenth in the same words on all three slates before anybody was asked anything. **Each of the three was put on a tether — thirty feet of line off a belt at the waist to a ring on the outside of that bell, and the tender on the surface and not in that bell — AT ABOUT TEN PAST EIGHT IN THE MORNING ON THE FIFTEENTH, BEFORE ANYBODY HAD SAID A WORD TO ANY OF THEM**, and the man who keeps the leaf said out loud at the time that it was a rope and not a person and that nobody was going to be holding the other end of it. Each was told before he was asked anything that he could stop it and that nobody would ask him why, and each said out loud before he answered anything else that he did not intend to stop it. **A man of about thirty-four of the second lay gave a SOUND: about nine strokes of about the length of a heartbeat and not even, the eighth shorter than the other eight, not from that wall and not from that floor and coming from further off than that room, and that there is a thing in that room he has been hearing in his own head for four days and he does not know where he heard it. A man of about twenty-nine gave a MOVEMENT: something on the far side of that back wall came down about a foot and stopped, heard and not seen, not the water, late on the knocking with a space in between, and he does not know what was in the space and is not going to put something in it. A woman of about thirty-one gave WHAT WAS IN THE AIR: water in the air in that room, not sea and not a drain, the smell of a stone floor that has had a roof over it for a very long time and has never had a fire in it, and a sweetness that came and went about four times while she stood there, and that she does not know that the sweetness is the paper and the man of about fifty-one does not know that either and has not offered.** Put together the three have a clock — about nine strokes, then a space, then something settling, then a change in the air, inside about two minutes — **and not one of the three knew at the time that the other two were carrying the other two parts of it. That is not a finding, it is not a recording, it is not a verdict, and no part of it can be taken off a page by a stranger with a pencil, because every part of it is a thing one man heard with his own ears or felt in his own body.** All three went into the second column in the order they were said and **none of them was asked to give it better and none was thanked.**
4. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO CAME UP ON THE NINETEENTH OF NOVEMBER WITH SOMETHING IN HIM THAT IS NOT HIS, AND IS KEEPING IT.** He is one of the four men paid a day apiece. He went down at about half past ten under a slate with his own reason, being that he had never in nineteen years of stands been in a room with a floor in it that was swept, and that he wanted to stand on one, and he came up at about twenty past eleven on the air. He is not hurt, nobody has named him a casualty, **no figure is set against him anywhere, and no sheet that carries money carries any line against him or about him.** At about two in the afternoon on that after deck he said one thing, once, in front of all nine of them: there is a woman in that room who has put a bowl of water down outside a door on the off side, and a man has gone past it and gone in without stopping, and the handle of the bowl is turned to the left as a person goes in and the rim of it is chipped on the left and the chip is old — and he has never seen any of it and does not know what it is. **He said out loud that he had worked out that a man who says a thing like that and then argues about it spends the rest of his life arguing about it, and that he has nineteen years of stands to do and is not spending them like that, and that nobody is to ask him for it and nobody is to have it, and that it cannot be given back because it was never taken.** It went into the second column with the hour against it and not into the first column and not onto any sheet that carries money. Nobody argued with him, nobody said the word brave, nobody put a figure on him, he was not made an example, nobody asked him why, **he went on working the twentieth and the twenty-first, and he is not the pump hand of about forty-four who came up short on the seventh and that earlier entry may not be repeated, improved on or treated as a wound left standing open. A later phase may have him working and may not have him asked about it.**
5. **THE COST OF THE CRATE, WHICH NOBODY WAS WARNED ABOUT.** A crate and matting and a lid is about three foot by two foot by two foot and will not go under that stove-pipe bracket; the after deck had to be cleared; the man who had slept under that bracket for three weeks went into the forepeak on the eighteenth; the boy gave up his bunk without being asked and was not thanked. **Nobody was thanked for any part of it and no figure is set against it, and the reason nobody was warned is that nobody had any idea what was in that room until a basket came up out of it on the Saturday.**
6. **A BAR ABOUT THE HEIGHT OF A MAN'S OWN CHEST, ABOUT NINE FOOT, ON THE FAR SIDE OF THE LAST OF THOSE FIFTEEN FRAMES, WORN BRIGHT ALONG THE TOP FOR ABOUT TWO FOOT IN THE MIDDLE AND DULL AT BOTH ENDS, FOUND BY A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SEVEN ON THE TWENTIETH AND NOT SEEN ON THE SEVENTEENTH.** Three accounts of it, said once each, and **the three do not agree**: a rail for a man to hold on to, being his own account, and he has been in holds nineteen years; a rail for a man to stand beside while something heavy comes past him, being the pump hand of about forty-four's, who has run air into twenty holds on this coast; and a rail for moving a thing, being the master of that boat of about nineteen tons', who has rails under his own forepeak where a man cannot get at because something on top of them gets moved often and by two men who cannot get their hands round it. **None of the three was asked to say it again, nobody on that deck picked one, nobody wrote down which he thought was right, and the party does not know. A later phase may look at that bar again and may not settle it.**
7. **THE TETHER, AND THE HOUSE RULE IT EXISTS TO KEEP.** Thirty feet of three-inch line off a belt at the waist to a ring on the outside of that bell, belayed, going over the after side of that bell and up to a man on the surface with a hand on a chain weight, with a cutoff he could pull without asking. **It went on all three of the men of the fifteenth at about ten past eight in the morning, before anybody had said a word to any of them, and the man who keeps the leaf said out loud at the time that if the rope went on after the asking then the rope was part of the asking, and that it is not a man and not a person, and that if anybody had told one of the three otherwise he was to say so now.** A man of about thirty-four of the second lay said four words: he had not been asked and had not offered and would not be asked and would not offer. **A later phase may put a rope on a man and may not put a person on the other end of one.**
8. **THE AIR, AND WHY THERE IS NONE, AND THAT IS A LOCK FOR MOVEMENT 5.** Four fresh days were bought off that supply boat on the seventeenth of November at seven hundred and twenty pence, bearing the seventeenth, and those four days are **the seventeenth, the eighteenth, the nineteenth and the twentieth, and the twentieth was the last of them.** The thirteenth to the sixteenth were dived on air out of bottles that boat carried off her own coast and filled off her own compressor, the master naming it as his own out loud on the surface, no figure of it on any sheet, nobody asking him for it twice. **No line has been opened for the twenty-first or the twenty-second, and the man who keeps the leaf said out loud at about eight in the morning on the twenty-first that the party was off that floor for a working day and that a boat lying still over a trench burns more coal than a boat working and he would rather they burned it there than twenty-two fathoms down. NOBODY ASKED WHY AND NOBODY ASKED HIM FOR IT A SECOND TIME. MOVEMENT 5 OPENS WITH NO LINE OPENED AFTER THE TWENTIETH OF NOVEMBER, AND A LATER PHASE MAY NOT RUN A DIVE ON AIR THAT IS ON NEITHER THE SHEET NOR THE BOAT'S OWN BOTTLES, AND NOBODY IS TO BE ASKED WHY.**
9. **THE SUPPLY BOAT AND THE END OF THE MONTH.** A man of about fifty-four in her, who has run that run for nineteen years, has said out loud for the third time on this trip and in the same words that coal off that boat goes up at the end of the month. **No line was opened for it and the man who keeps the leaf said so out loud. A later phase may not print that figure on any sheet and may not use it as the source of a figure.**
10. **THE FIFTY-SIXTH WAGE TUESDAY, ON THE SIXTEENTH OF NOVEMBER.** The column stood at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with twenty envelopes in a chest at ten in the morning and at four in the afternoon, the fifty-sixth wage Tuesday came and went at the close of the day, the column did not move, and **fifty-six weeks stand fallen due.** The fifty-seventh is the twenty-third of November and the fifty-eighth is the thirtieth. **A wage Tuesday does not pay a wage; a wage Tuesday is the day a harbor finds out what it owes.** One of the four men paid a day apiece asked out loud what a man is owed if the boat goes home early, and was given the same answer for the third time in the same words — that a day in advance is a day in advance and is not taken back, that it is not a promise of a day after it, that the master's boat is not this party and he was never in it, and that he cannot be asked to stay and is not going to be asked — and he thanked him and was told again that he was not to be thanked for it.
11. **THE CISTERN'S COUNT, WHICH IS RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE MOVED.** The ninety-ninth on Monday the fifteenth, the hundredth on Thursday the eighteenth with the figure said out loud on that deck once and standing on a slate in that market and in no other place, and the hundred and first on Monday the twenty-second with **the figure of that hundred not said again.** The chain runs 96 at 473, 97 at 477, 98 at 480, 99 at 483, 100 at 486, 101 at 490. **Movement 5 carries 102 on Monday the twenty-third, 103 on Thursday the twenty-sixth, 104 on Monday the thirtieth and 105 on Thursday the second of December, and the wipes carry 82 on Sunday the twenty-eighth of November and 83 on Sunday the fifth of December.**
12. **THE MONEY.** This movement took nothing in on any line and asked nobody for anything.
